import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Architecture | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

`openbb-core` is the runtime. It ships no data sources and no commands of its own. When it starts, it reads Python entry points, loads every installed extension, and assembles them into two surfaces that share one engine: the Python Interface (`from openbb import obb`) and the REST API (the FastAPI app at `openbb_core.api.rest_api:app`). Neither surface wraps the other. Both dispatch to the same router functions through the same command runner.

The core depends on FastAPI and Uvicorn for serving, Pydantic for models and validation, `requests` and `aiohttp` for outbound HTTP, and `websockets`. pandas is an optional extra: install `openbb-core[pandas]` to use `to_dataframe()` and `to_numpy()` on results, and add `polars` and `pyarrow` for `to_polars()`. The `openbb-core[flask]` extra lets a Flask app registered as an extension be mounted on the REST API.

## What a bare install exposes

With only `openbb-core` installed there are no commands. Importing the Python Interface prints `Failed to import extensions. Are any installed?`, and `obb` exposes only its utility properties: `obb.user` (user settings, including credentials and preferences), `obb.system` (system settings), `obb.coverage` (installed providers, commands, and their models), and `obb.reference` (the command metadata written at build time).

The REST API serves every command under `/api/v1`; the version segment comes from `api_settings.version`. Once any command is installed it also serves `/api/v1/coverage/providers`, `/api/v1/coverage/commands`, and `/api/v1/coverage/command_model`. Setting `OPENBB_DEV_MODE=1` adds `/api/v1/system` and `/api/v1/user/me`. Run the bare app with any ASGI server:

```bash
uvicorn openbb_core.api.rest_api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

The `openbb-api` launcher from `openbb-platform-api` wraps the same app with extra configuration; see [OpenBB API](../extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx).

## How a command runs

A router extension registers plain Python functions with `@router.command`. The engine mounts each one at `/<entry-point name>/<function name>`, and the package builder writes a matching method on `obb`. The function `factors` in the router registered as `famafrench` becomes both `obb.famafrench.factors()` and `GET /api/v1/famafrench/factors`. Sub-routers included with a prefix add a path segment, which is how `obb.quantitative.stats.skew()` maps to `/quantitative/stats/skew`.

When the Python method is called, the generated code validates the arguments, fills in per-command defaults from the user settings, resolves which provider to use, and hands the call to the command runner. The REST route applies the same per-command defaults to the request's parameters. From that point the two paths are identical: the runner calls the router function, attaches the provider name, captured warnings, and execution metadata (`extra["metadata"]`) to the returned [`OBBject`](obbject.mdx), builds a chart when `chart=True` was passed and a charting extension is installed, and then runs any OBBject extensions registered to act on command output.

### The provider layer

Commands declared with `model="<ModelName>"` contain no data-fetching code. Their body is normally the single line `return await OBBject.from_query(Query(**locals()))`. The engine collects every installed provider whose `fetcher_dict` has a `<ModelName>` key and builds the command's `provider` choices and parameters from those fetchers' models.

Each provider implements a `Fetcher` for the model, built from two Pydantic models and three static methods. `QueryParams` describes the inputs and `Data` describes one output row. At call time, `transform_query` validates the parameters into the `QueryParams` model, `extract_data` (or the async `aextract_data`) retrieves the raw payload, and `transform_data` validates it into `Data` rows. This transform-extract-transform sequence is called the TET pattern. Credentials the provider declares are checked before the fetcher runs.

Fields inherited from a standard model in `openbb_core.provider.standard_models` become named parameters shared by every provider of that model. Fields a provider adds itself are provider-specific. [Standardization](../developer/standardization.mdx) explains the rules, and [Provider extensions](../developer/extension_types/provider.md) walks through building one.

## Output handling

After a command runs, the Python Interface reads `user_settings.preferences.output_type`. When the value is `"OBBject"` (the default), the `OBBject` is returned as-is. For any other value, the matching accessor is called, for example `to_dataframe()` for `"dataframe"`. The REST API ignores this preference and returns the JSON serialization of the `OBBject`. Commands that return a Pydantic model or plain value instead of an `OBBject` are returned as the handler produced them; the `output_type` conversions exist only on `OBBject`.

Streaming commands return an [`OBBStream`](streaming.mdx) handle from the Python Interface and a `text/event-stream` response from the REST API instead of an `OBBject`.

## Where extensions plug in

Router extensions add commands and namespaces, provider extensions add data sources for models, OBBject extensions add accessors to results or run callbacks on command output, and charting extensions add chart views for specific routes. Each kind is discovered through its own entry-point group; [Extension types](extensions.mdx) lists the groups and what each entry point must resolve to.

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Extension types | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

OpenBB discovers extensions through Python entry points declared in each package's `pyproject.toml`. A single distribution can register entry points in any combination of groups. Every V5 data package does this: it registers a provider under `openbb_provider_extension` and its own command namespace under `openbb_core_extension`, so installing `openbb-famafrench` adds both the `famafrench` provider and `obb.famafrench`.

## Router extensions: `openbb_core_extension`

A router extension adds a top-level namespace to `obb` and the same commands as HTTP routes under `/api/v1/<name>`. Each command is a function decorated with `@router.command(...)`.

The entry point must resolve to an already-constructed `openbb_core.app.router.Router`, `fastapi.FastAPI`, or `fastapi.APIRouter` instance. A `FastAPI` app contributes its `.router`, and an `APIRouter` is wrapped in a `Router`. Factory functions are not called; an entry point that resolves to anything else is skipped.

```toml
[project.entry-points."openbb_core_extension"]
my_router = "my_package.my_router:router"
```

The entry-point name becomes the namespace: `obb.my_router.*` and `/api/v1/my_router/*`.

With the `openbb-core[flask]` extra installed, an entry point in this group can also resolve to a Flask application. Flask apps are mounted on the REST API at `/api/v1/<name>` and their routes are merged into the OpenAPI schema; they do not appear in the Python Interface.

## Provider extensions: `openbb_provider_extension`

A provider extension supplies data for one or more models. It declares a `Provider` whose `fetcher_dict` maps model names to `Fetcher` subclasses. A router command declared with `model="<ModelName>"` offers every installed provider that has that key, and at call time the engine runs the selected provider's fetcher. Streaming providers implement `stream_data` instead of `transform_data`; see [Streaming responses](streaming.mdx).

The entry point must resolve to an `openbb_core.provider.abstract.provider.Provider` instance.

```toml
[project.entry-points."openbb_provider_extension"]
my_provider = "my_package:my_provider"
```

Callers select the provider with `provider="<name>"`, where `<name>` is the `name` argument given to `Provider(...)`. Keep the entry-point name the same to avoid confusion; `openbb-us-eia` is an exception, registering the entry point `us_eia` for a provider named `eia`.

## OBBject extensions: `openbb_obbject_extension`

An OBBject extension attaches an accessor to every `OBBject`, or runs a callback on command output. The entry point must resolve to an `openbb_core.app.model.extension.Extension` instance; other objects are ignored.

```toml
[project.entry-points."openbb_obbject_extension"]
my_accessor = "my_package:ext"
```

By default an extension registers a pandas-style accessor, so callers write `obbject.<extension name>.<method>(...)`. The accessor object is created on first access and cached on that `OBBject`. [OBBject extensions](../developer/extension_types/obbject.md) shows both the class and function forms.

Setting `on_command_output=True` turns the extension into a callback that runs after matching commands, on both the Python Interface and the REST API. It only loads when `allow_on_command_output` is enabled in the system settings or `OPENBB_ALLOW_ON_COMMAND_OUTPUT` is set. `command_output_paths` limits it to specific routes, `results_only=True` makes the command return only `results`, and `immutable=False` lets it modify the returned `OBBject`, which additionally requires `allow_mutable_extensions` or `OPENBB_ALLOW_MUTABLE_EXTENSIONS`. [OBBject plugins](../developer/extension_types/plugins.md) covers the details.

## Charting extensions: `openbb_charting_extension`

A charting extension provides chart views for routes registered by router extensions. `openbb-charting` loads every entry point in this group and matches views to commands by method name; the entry-point name is not used for matching.

The entry point must resolve to a class. Each public static method defined in that class's module is a view, named after the route it charts: the leading `/` is dropped and the remaining `/` become `_`. The IMF provider's view for `/imf/portwatch/country_activity` is `ImfViews.imf_portwatch_country_activity`:

```python
class ImfViews:
    """IMF chart views."""

    @staticmethod
    def imf_portwatch_country_activity(**kwargs):
        """Chart port activity for a country."""
        ...
```

```toml
[project.entry-points."openbb_charting_extension"]
imf = "openbb_imf.imf_views:ImfViews"
```

A view receives keyword arguments that include the command's results as `obbject_item`, and returns a `Chart` model, a figure, or a `(figure, content)` tuple. Installing a view adds a `chart` parameter to the command after the next build. [Charting extensions](../developer/extension_types/charting.md) has the full contract.

`openbb-core` also resolves two charting groups of its own: `openbb_charting_hooks` for `ChartingHook` subclasses that run at stages of chart creation, and `openbb_charting_backend` for a rendering backend selected by the `charting_backend` system setting.

## Summary

| Group | Adds | Entry-point target |
| ----- | ---- | ------------------ |
| `openbb_core_extension` | Commands and namespaces | `Router`, `FastAPI`, or `APIRouter` instance (or a Flask app, REST only) |
| `openbb_provider_extension` | Data sources for models | `Provider` instance |
| `openbb_obbject_extension` | Accessors on `OBBject`, or command-output callbacks | `Extension` instance |
| `openbb_charting_extension` | Chart views for routes | A class whose static methods are named after routes |

title: The OBBject envelope
sidebar_position: 2
description: >
  OBBject is the return type used across openbb-core. Its fields, conversion
  methods, and how the output_type preference applies them.
keywords:

  - to_dataframe
  - to_polars
  - to_numpy
  - to_dict
  - to_llm
  - show
  - output_type
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="OBBject | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

`OBBject`, imported from `openbb_core.app.model.obbject`, is a generic Pydantic model (`OBBject[T]`) that wraps command results together with provider attribution, warnings, an optional chart, and metadata. Router commands build it with `OBBject(results=...)` or, for provider-backed commands, `await OBBject.from_query(query)`.

Streaming commands return an [`OBBStream`](streaming.mdx) instead. A router declares one or the other through its return annotation.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | A new UUIDv7 string |
| `results` | `T \| None` | `None` |
| `provider` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `warnings` | `list[Warning_] \| None` | `None` |
| `chart` | `Chart \| None` | `None` |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | `{}` |

The runner fills `provider` from the command's provider choice and `warnings` from any warnings raised while the command ran. When the `metadata` preference is on (the default), `extra["metadata"]` holds the arguments, route, start timestamp, and duration in nanoseconds. Fetchers that return an `AnnotatedResult` put their metadata in `extra["results_metadata"]`.

`OBBject.accessors` is a class-level set with the names of every accessor registered by an [OBBject extension](../developer/extension_types/obbject.md).

## Conversion methods

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `to_dataframe(index="date", sort_by=None, ascending=None)` | `pandas.DataFrame` |
| `to_df(...)` | Alias for `to_dataframe` |
| `to_polars()` | `polars.DataFrame` |
| `to_numpy()` | `numpy.ndarray` |
| `to_dict(orient="list")` | `dict` or `list[dict]`; `orient` is one of `"dict"`, `"list"`, `"series"`, `"split"`, `"tight"`, `"records"`, `"index"` |
| `to_llm()` | `str`: the results as JSON records with ISO dates |
| `show(**kwargs)` | `None`: displays the chart; raises `OpenBBError` when no chart is set |

All conversions except `show()` go through pandas, so they need `openbb-core[pandas]`. `to_polars()` also needs `polars` and `pyarrow`. The Pydantic methods `model_dump()` and `model_dump_json()` serialize the whole envelope without extra dependencies.

A chart is produced by passing `chart=True` to a command that has a chart view, with a charting extension installed. `show()` then renders it.

## The output_type preference

`user_settings.preferences.output_type` controls what the Python Interface returns. With `"OBBject"`, the default, the envelope is returned as-is. Any other value calls `to_<value>()` on the envelope before returning. The accepted values are:

```python
Literal["OBBject", "dataframe", "polars", "numpy", "dict", "chart", "llm"]
```

`"chart"` passes validation, but `OBBject` has no `to_chart()` method, so the conversion fails; use `chart=True` and `show()` instead. The preferences model validates on assignment, so setting an unsupported value raises a validation error. [Output types](../user-guide/output-types.mdx) covers setting the preference.

title: Packaging and static assets
sidebar_position: 4
description: >
  How the openbb Python package is generated from installed extensions, when
  it rebuilds on its own, and when to run openbb-build.
keywords:
  - openbb-build
  - openbb.build
  - static assets
  - OPENBB_AUTO_BUILD
  - reference.json
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Packaging and static assets | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

The Python Interface is generated code. `openbb-core` ships the `openbb` package with a placeholder `package` directory, and a build step writes one module per router path into `site-packages/openbb/package/` plus a command reference at `site-packages/openbb/assets/reference.json`. The generated methods carry the signatures, type hints, and docstrings for every installed command. They contain no business logic; each one forwards to the live router function, so the output always reflects the installed code.

Because the files describe the extensions installed in one environment, they are not shipped pre-built. The REST API does not use them at all: `openbb_core.api.rest_api:app` loads routers from entry points every time it starts.

## When the package rebuilds

Importing `openbb` compares the extensions recorded in `reference.json` with the installed entry points, by name and distribution version. If an extension was added, removed, or changed version, the import prints the difference and rebuilds before `obb` is created. Set `OPENBB_AUTO_BUILD=false` to skip the check, for example in read-only deployments where the build step runs ahead of time.

The check does not notice edits to an extension installed in editable mode when its version stays the same. Rebuild by hand after changing anything the generated code copies: command names or signatures, `QueryParams` and `Data` fields or descriptions, `fetcher_dict` keys, examples, or entry points. Changes inside fetcher methods, router function bodies, and helpers take effect without a rebuild.

## Triggering a build

From a shell, run the console script that `openbb-core` installs:

```bash
openbb-build
```

It imports `openbb` in a subprocess, which triggers the automatic build when one is needed, and calls `openbb.build()` if it was not. From Python:

```python
import openbb

openbb.build()
```

`openbb.build()` regenerates every module. Its `lint` argument (default `True`) runs `ruff check --fix-only` over the generated files, and `verbose=True` prints each file as it is written. Restart the interpreter afterwards so `from openbb import obb` loads the new modules.

The build writes into the environment's `site-packages`, so the process needs write access there. Only one build runs at a time; a second concurrent build fails with a `RuntimeError` naming the lock file. If a build fails, set `OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE=true` and run `openbb-build` again for the full traceback.

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Streaming responses | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

A streaming command returns rows as they arrive instead of a finished result set. The provider's fetcher produces an async iterator of typed rows, the Python Interface hands back an `OBBStream` handle over that iterator, and the REST API sends the rows as a `text/event-stream` response. `OBBStream` is a sibling of [`OBBject`](obbject.mdx), not a subclass, and a command declares one or the other through its return annotation.

No V5 package currently ships a streaming command. The examples on this page use a placeholder extension that registers a router named `my_stream` and a provider named `my_provider` with a model called `MyTicks`.

## Fetcher contract

A fetcher becomes a streaming fetcher by overriding `stream_data` instead of `transform_data`. Its second type parameter is `AsyncIterator[<row model>]`, and the engine unwraps that to find the row type for docs and schemas.

`aextract_data` should return an async iterator without consuming it. Defining an inner async generator and returning it, as below, means the upstream connection (a websocket, SSE feed, or polling loop) opens only when the caller starts iterating. `stream_data` receives that iterator as `data` and must be an `async def` generator that yields validated rows.

```python
import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from openbb_core.provider.abstract.data import Data
from openbb_core.provider.abstract.fetcher import Fetcher
from openbb_core.provider.abstract.query_params import QueryParams
from pydantic import Field


class MyTicksQueryParams(QueryParams):
    """Tick stream query."""

    symbol: str = Field(description="Symbol to stream.")
    limit: int = Field(default=5, description="Number of ticks to emit.")


class MyTicksData(Data):
    """One tick."""

    symbol: str = Field(description="Symbol.")
    sequence: int = Field(description="Tick sequence number.")
    price: float = Field(description="Last price.")


class MyTicksFetcher(Fetcher[MyTicksQueryParams, AsyncIterator[MyTicksData]]):
    """Tick stream fetcher."""

    require_credentials = False

    @staticmethod
    def transform_query(params: dict[str, Any]) -> MyTicksQueryParams:
        """Validate the query."""
        return MyTicksQueryParams(**params)

    @staticmethod
    async def aextract_data(
        query: MyTicksQueryParams,
        credentials: dict[str, str] | None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:
        """Return an async iterator of raw messages."""

        async def messages():
            for sequence in range(query.limit):
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
                yield {"symbol": query.symbol, "sequence": sequence, "price": 100 + sequence}

        return messages()

    @staticmethod
    async def stream_data(
        query: MyTicksQueryParams,
        data: AsyncIterator[dict],
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[MyTicksData]:
        """Validate each raw message."""
        async for message in data:
            yield MyTicksData.model_validate(message)
```

`MyTicksFetcher.is_streaming` is `True` because `stream_data` is overridden. `await MyTicksFetcher.fetch_data({"symbol": "ABC"})` returns the row iterator, and `MyTicksFetcher.test({"symbol": "ABC", "limit": 2})` consumes the first row and checks that it is a `MyTicksData` with every declared field.

## Router contract

A streaming command is annotated `-> OBBStream` and returns `await OBBStream.from_query(Query(**locals()))`. Otherwise it looks like any other provider-backed command.

```python
from openbb_core.app.model.command_context import CommandContext
from openbb_core.app.model.example import APIEx
from openbb_core.app.model.stream import OBBStream
from openbb_core.app.provider_interface import (
    ExtraParams,
    ProviderChoices,
    StandardParams,
)
from openbb_core.app.query import Query
from openbb_core.app.router import Router

router = Router(prefix="", description="Streaming example.")


@router.command(
    model="MyTicks",
    examples=[APIEx(parameters={"symbol": "ABC", "provider": "my_provider"})],
)
async def ticks(
    cc: CommandContext,
    provider_choices: ProviderChoices,
    standard_params: StandardParams,
    extra_params: ExtraParams,
) -> OBBStream:
    """Stream ticks for a symbol."""
    return await OBBStream.from_query(Query(**locals()))
```

For an `OBBStream` return annotation, `@router.command` registers the route without a response model and documents a `200` response with `text/event-stream` content in the OpenAPI schema. `OBBStream.from_query` copies the provider name onto the handle and, if the result is an `AnnotatedResult`, stores its metadata in `extra["results_metadata"]`.

## Using a stream from Python

The command returns immediately with an `OBBStream`. Nothing is fetched until the stream is iterated or started. Iterate it inside async code:

```python
import asyncio

from openbb import obb


async def main():
    async for tick in obb.my_stream.ticks(symbol="ABC", limit=3):
        print(tick.sequence, tick.price)


asyncio.run(main())
```

`start()` drives the stream on a daemon thread with its own event loop and returns the handle, so a notebook or script keeps running while rows arrive. Without arguments, each row is written to standard output. `stop()` cancels the stream and waits up to `timeout` seconds (default 5.0) for the thread to exit:

```python
from openbb import obb

stream = obb.my_stream.ticks(symbol="ABC", limit=100)
stream.start()
stream.stop()
```

The `output` argument of `start()` also accepts a file path (opened for writing and closed when the stream ends), an open file or pipe, or a socket; anything without a `write` or `sendall` method raises `TypeError`. The `handler` argument receives each row before it is written. It can be sync or async. Returning `None` drops the row, and returning any other value writes that value instead. `wait()` blocks until the stream finishes, or until its optional `timeout`, and still responds to Ctrl+C while waiting.

```python
from openbb import obb


def even_only(tick):
    return tick if tick.sequence % 2 == 0 else None


stream = obb.my_stream.ticks(symbol="ABC", limit=10)
stream.start(output="ticks.ndjson", handler=even_only)
stream.wait()
```

Rows are serialized one per line. Pydantic rows are written with `model_dump_json()`, other objects with `json.dumps(..., default=str)`, and strings or bytes pass through unchanged, so a fetcher can yield pre-formatted SSE frames.

The underlying iterator is single-use. After a stream has been iterated or started, calling `start()` again raises `RuntimeError`; call the command again for a new stream. The first call to `start()` in a process registers an exit hook that stops every running stream. If that call happens on the main thread, it also installs SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that stop the streams and then defer to the handler that was installed before.

The handle carries `id` (a UUIDv7 string), `provider`, `warnings` raised while the command was opening the stream, `extra` (including `extra["metadata"]` when the `metadata` preference is on), and `media_type`. The `started` and `running` properties report whether iteration has begun and whether the background thread is alive.

`OBBStream` has none of the `to_*` conversion methods, so leave `output_type` at its default `"OBBject"` when calling streaming commands. A command whose handler returns a Starlette `StreamingResponse` directly, such as a wrapped FastAPI route, is also returned as an `OBBStream` over the response body.

## Using a stream from the REST API

The REST route returns a Starlette `StreamingResponse`. The body is the same line-by-line serialization described above, and the envelope fields that do not fit in the body are sent as headers:

| Header | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| `X-OpenBB-Stream-Id` | The stream `id` |
| `X-OpenBB-Provider` | The provider name, when set |
| `X-OpenBB-Warning` | The warnings as a JSON array, when any were raised |

```bash
curl -N "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/my_stream/ticks?symbol=ABC&limit=3"
```

The media type is `text/event-stream` unless the wrapped source declares another. A command that returns a Starlette `Response` of its own is forwarded unchanged.

description: "Fetch BLS CPI relative-importance and weights for one yearly file + sheet"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `BlsCpiRelativeImportance` | `BlsCpiRelativeImportanceQueryParams` | `BlsCpiRelativeImportanceData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
BlsCpiRelativeImportanceData,
BlsCpiRelativeImportanceQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
Year of the relative-importance file to fetch; None walks back until a published file is found.

**table**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Which of the 7 sheets in the relative-importance XLSX to return.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
December reference date for the weights.

**label**: `str | None`<br/>
BLS item or expenditure-category label.

**level**: `int | None`<br/>
Indent depth from the source XLSX.

**row_index**: `int`<br/>
Sequential ordering index assigned during parsing.

**section**: `str | None`<br/>
Section the row appears under in the source XLSX (Expenditure category or Special aggregate indexes).

**area**: `str | None`<br/>
Geographic area the weight refers to (e.g., U.S. City Average or a selected local area).

**footnote**: `str | None`<br/>
Resolved footnote text for any (N) markers attached to the row's label.

**basket**: `str`<br/>
Which CPI basket the weight refers to (CPI-U or CPI-W).

**relative_importance**: `float | None`<br/>
Weight as a percentage of the parent index.

**table_id**: `str`<br/>
Source table identifier.

**table_name**: `str`<br/>
Full BLS table title.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "Bls Cpi Supplemental Tables"
description: "Fetch one of the BLS CPI supplemental XLSX tables (C-CPI-U, CPI-W, historical, etc"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `BlsCpiSupplementalTables` | `BlsCpiSupplementalTablesQueryParams` | `BlsCpiSupplementalTablesData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
BlsCpiSupplementalTablesData,
BlsCpiSupplementalTablesQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**table**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* cpi-u-us<br/>
Which CPI supplemental table to load.

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Snapshot month to fetch; None resolves to the most recent published snapshot.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Reference date the row's values apply to.

**label**: `str`<br/>
Row label from the source XLSX.

**indent_level**: `int | None`<br/>
Indent depth in the source XLSX.

**frequency**: `str | None`<br/>
Reference-date frequency: monthly, semiannual, or annual.

**index_value**: `float | None`<br/>
Unadjusted (NSA) CPI index level at date.

**sa_index_value**: `float | None`<br/>
Seasonally-adjusted CPI index level at date.

**pct_change_1m_nsa**: `float | None`<br/>
One-month NSA percent change ending at date.

**pct_change_1m_sa**: `float | None`<br/>
One-month seasonally-adjusted percent change ending at date.

**pct_change_12m**: `float | None`<br/>
Twelve-month percent change ending at date.

**pct_change_window**: `float | None`<br/>
Two-month NSA percent change ending at date.

**pct_change_window_start_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Start-of-month for the pct_change_window comparison.

**relative_importance**: `float | None`<br/>
Relative-importance weight as a percent of the parent index.

**pricing_schedule**: `str | None`<br/>
Pricing-schedule code (M = monthly, S = semiannual, B = bimonthly).

**half**: `str | None`<br/>
Semiannual half (1st or 2nd) for historical-cpi-u-averages rows.

**value_string**: `str | None`<br/>
Raw cell text when the source value is not numeric.

**snapshot_date**: `date`<br/>
Publication month of the source XLSX snapshot.

**table_key**: `str`<br/>
Which CPI table family this row came from.

**table_id**: `str`<br/>
Stable identifier for the source (table, snapshot) tuple.

**table_name**: `str`<br/>
Human-readable BLS table title for the source snapshot.

**sheet**: `str`<br/>
XLSX sheet name the row was read from.

**row_index**: `int`<br/>
Sequential ordering index assigned during parsing.

**footnote**: `str | None`<br/>
Resolved footnote text for any (N) markers attached to the row's label.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "Bls Search"
description: "Search the BLS series catalog by category, keyword, or code"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `BlsSearch` | `BlsSearchQueryParams` | `BlsSearchData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
BlsSearchData,
BlsSearchQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**query**: `str | None`<br/>
The search word(s). Use semi-colon to separate multiple queries as an & operator.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**query**: `str | None`<br/>
The search word(s). Use semi-colon to separate multiple queries as an & operator.

**symbol**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Bound to the Series widget via cell-click grouping; clicking a row's symbol loads it there. Does not filter the search results. Multiple items allowed.

**category**: `str`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

The category of BLS survey to search within. An empty search query returns every series within the category. Options are:<br/>
<br/>
    cpi - Consumer Price Index<br/>
    ixp - Import/Export Price Indexes<br/>
    pce - Consumer Expenditure Survey<br/>
    ppi - Producer Price Index<br/>
    ip - Productivity (Industry, Major Sector & Total Factor)<br/>
    jolts - Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey<br/>
    nfp - Nonfarm Payrolls (Current Employment Statistics)<br/>
    cps - Current Population Survey<br/>
    lfs - Labor Force Statistics & International Comparisons<br/>
    wages - Employment Cost Index & Wage Estimates<br/>
    ec - Employer Costs for Employee Compensation<br/>
    sla - State & Local Area Employment & Unemployment<br/>
    bed - Business Employment Dynamics<br/>
    tu - American Time Use Survey<br/>
</details>

**include_extras**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Include additional information in the search results. Extra fields returned are metadata and vary by survey. Fields are undefined strings that typically have names ending with '_code'.

**include_code_map**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When True, includes the complete code map for eaçh survey in the category, returned separately as a nested JSON to the `extras['results_metadata']` property of the response. Example content is the NAICS industry map for PPI surveys. Each code is a value within the 'symbol' of the time series.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**title**: `str | None`<br/>
The title of the series.

**survey_name**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the survey.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
BLS series identifier. Click a cell to load it into the linked BLS Series widget.

**title**: `str | None`<br/>
The title of the series.

**survey_name**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the survey.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "Cftc Cds Index Trades"
description: "Get credit default swap index transactions disseminated by DTCC"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `CftcCdsIndexTrades` | `CftcCdsIndexTradesQueryParams` | `CftcCdsIndexTradesData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcCdsIndexTradesData,
CftcCdsIndexTradesQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**index**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by index family, matched against the UPI Underlier Name. E.g., 'CDX.NA.IG'. Matching is exact and case-insensitive, because 'ITRAXX EUROPE' is a substring of two other index families. Default is every index.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent date whose file holds index prints matching the query; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

**tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by the print's tenor at execution. E.g., '5Y'. Default is every tenor.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Filter out prints whose leg 1 notional is disseminated below this amount. A print above the reporting cap is disseminated at the cap, which is only a floor on its true size, so a threshold above a cap drops prints that may in fact exceed it. Caps vary by index, tenor and currency.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of prints to return. Default is all matching.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**dissemination_date**: `date`<br/>
Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in. The cumulative file carries no per-message dissemination timestamp.

**trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'CR:4411567497000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of action taken on the swap transaction: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), EROR (error), TERM (terminate), or REVI (revive).

**event_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Explanation or reason for the action being taken on the swap transaction: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation/step-in), COMP (compression or post trade risk reduction exercise), ETRM (early termination), CLRG (clearing), EXER (exercise), or CREV (credit event).

**event_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time of occurrence of the event, as determined by the reporting counterparty or a service provider.

**execution_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time the transaction was originally executed, resulting in the generation of a new UTI. It remains unchanged throughout the life of the UTI, so on a correction or termination it dates the original trade.

**index**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the asset or index underlying the product corresponding to the UPI. It names the index family only and carries no series number, so `maturity_date` is what pins the series.

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name issued by the UPI Service Provider. 'NA/CDS Corp Idx Tra' marks a tranche print.

**unique_product_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier (UPI), a unique set of characters that represents a particular OTC derivative.

**effective_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction come into effect. For a credit index this should be the effective date of the contract, usually one or two days after execution, and not the roll date of the underlying index.

**maturity_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction stop being effective, as included in the confirmation ('Expiration date'). Early termination does not affect it. Together with `index` it identifies the series traded.

**tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
Years from `execution_timestamp` to `maturity_date`, snapped to the nearest standard CDS index tenor within one year, else the rounded year count. Derived, not disseminated.

**coupon**: `float | None`<br/>
Per annum rate of the fixed leg, expressed as a decimal (0.05 is 500bp). The index's standardised coupon, and with `upfront_amount` the price of the print.

**coupon_day_count**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 20022 day count convention of the fixed leg. A004 is ACT/360.

**coupon_payment_frequency**: `str | None`<br/>
Time unit associated with the frequency of fixed leg payments: DAIL, WEEK, MNTH, YEAR, ADHO, or EXPI (payment at term).

**coupon_payment_frequency_multiplier**: `float | None`<br/>
Number of time units of `coupon_payment_frequency` between payments. MNTH with a multiplier of 3 is quarterly.

**upfront_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Payment amount corresponding to `upfront_type`, in `upfront_currency`. With `coupon` it prices the print.

**upfront_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of the other payment amount. UFRO is an upfront payment: the initial payment made by one of the counterparties either to bring a transaction to fair value or for any other reason that may be the cause of an off-market transaction. UWIN is an unwind or full termination payment; PEXH is a principal exchange.

**upfront_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which `upfront_amount` is denominated.

**spread**: `float | None`<br/>
Reported spread on the leg 1 index reference price, as disseminated. Conditional: it is required only where `coupon` is not populated and `upfront_type` is not 'UFRO', so it is an alternative to the coupon-plus-upfront quote rather than the price of the print. Read it together with `spread_notation` - the field also carries a price in points of par on the price-quoted indices. See the package README.

**spread_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Manner in which `spread` is expressed: 1 (monetary amount, in `spread_currency`), 3 (decimal, e.g. 0.0257 for 2.57%), or 4 (basis points, e.g. 257 for 2.57%).

**spread_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which `spread` is denominated. Only applicable when `spread_notation` is 1.

**index_factor**: `float | None`<br/>
The index version factor or percent, expressed as a decimal value, that multiplied by the notional amount yields the notional amount covered by the seller of protection. Below 1 once a constituent has defaulted.

**notional_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 1 notional amount specified in the contract, gross of any version incrementing due to a credit event. Values above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap and flagged by `is_capped`.

**notional_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which the leg 1 notional amount is denominated.

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap rather than its true value. Other disseminated amounts are proportionally scaled when the notional is capped.

**venue**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility the transaction was executed on. XOFF marks a transaction in a listed instrument executed off venue, XXXX an instrument not listed on any venue, and BILT a reporting counterparty that could not determine whether the instrument is listed.

**cleared**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction has been cleared, or is intended to be cleared, by a central counterparty: Y (centrally cleared), N (not centrally cleared), or I (intent to clear, for original swaps planned to be submitted to clearing).

**block_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether an election has been made to report the transaction as a block trade, by the reporting counterparty or as calculated by the SDR on its behalf or by a third party.

**package_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is part of a package transaction, being two or more transactions negotiated together as the product of a single economic agreement.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "Cftc Cot Index"
description: "Score COT positioning against each trader group's own lookback range"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `CftcCotIndex` | `CftcCotIndexQueryParams` | `CftcCotIndexData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcCotIndexData,
CftcCotIndexQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**asset_class**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* all<br/>
Asset class of the curated markets to score.

**lookback_weeks**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 52<br/>
Weeks of history the score ranks the latest net position within. 52 puts each reading in its own one-year range.

**futures_only**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Score the futures-only report, the basis COT positioning work conventionally uses. False scores the combined futures-and-options report, whose larger open interest dilutes every net-to-open-interest share.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache each market's report history locally.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**report_date**: `date`<br/>
Date of the CFTC report the scores are taken from.

**market**: `str`<br/>
Curated market name.

**open_interest**: `int | None`<br/>
Total open interest on the report date.

**large_specs**: `float | None`<br/>
Large speculators' net position as a 0-100 score within its own lookback range. 0 is the range low, 100 the range high.

**large_specs_change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in the large speculators' score since the prior report.

**large_specs_net_pct_oi**: `float | None`<br/>
Large speculators' net position as a percent of open interest.

**large_specs_zone**: `str | None`<br/>
Band the large speculators' score sits in.

**small_specs**: `float | None`<br/>
Small speculators' net position as a 0-100 score within its own lookback range.

**small_specs_change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in the small speculators' score since the prior report.

**small_specs_net_pct_oi**: `float | None`<br/>
Small speculators' net position as a percent of open interest.

**small_specs_zone**: `str | None`<br/>
Band the small speculators' score sits in.

**commercials**: `float | None`<br/>
Commercials' net position as a 0-100 score within its own lookback range. A high score is their least-hedged reading, not a bullish one.

**commercials_change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in the commercials' score since the prior report.

**commercials_net_pct_oi**: `float | None`<br/>
Commercials' net position as a percent of open interest.

**commercials_zone**: `str | None`<br/>
Band the commercials' score sits in, in hedging terms.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

**lookback_weeks**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 52<br/>

**futures_only**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>

title: "Cftc Fx Forward Points"
description: "Get FX forward points, built from executed forwards and FX swaps"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `CftcFxForwardPoints` | `CftcFxForwardPointsQueryParams` | `CftcFxForwardPointsData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcFxForwardPointsData,
CftcFxForwardPointsQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* EURUSD<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention. The USD/EM pairs (USDKRW, USDINR, USDBRL, ...) are non-deliverable forwards.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, which leaves thin tenors missing and yields nothing on a weekend.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects one day's file, and defaults to the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 30<br/>
Number of dissemination days to search back over, ending on `date`. Only used when source='search'. A longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days`. The source caps a search at 180 days.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1000000.0<br/>
Minimum trade notional, in the base currency. Sub-institutional prints trade percent away from the interbank market and would otherwise dominate a tenor's median. Set to 0 to keep every trade.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop tenors priced by fewer than this many trades. The default keeps every tenor, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve, being that of its freshest tenor.

**as_of_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the tenor's trades were reported on.

**staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Days between the tenor's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest tenors.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention.

**tenor**: `str`<br/>
Tenor bucket of the observation.

**tenor_days**: `int`<br/>
Lower bound of the tenor bucket, in days.

**spot_rate**: `float`<br/>
Spot rate of the tenor's as-of date, the median of that day's trades settling within two days, or of its shortest-dated tenor for a non-deliverable pair.

**forward_rate**: `float`<br/>
Median executed forward rate at the tenor.

**forward_points**: `float`<br/>
Executed forward rate less spot, in pips.

**theoretical_points**: `float | None`<br/>
Covered-interest-parity forward points from the two legs' rate curves, in pips - each leg's OIS, or its fixed-float IRS for an EM currency with no OIS. Present only when both legs have a curve; for a non-deliverable pair its gap to the executed points (`basis_points`) is the NDF basis to onshore rates.

**basis_points**: `float | None`<br/>
Executed points less the CIP points, in pips: positive where the market pays over covered-interest-parity fair value, negative under.

**quotation**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the base is at a forward premium (executed points positive, forward above spot) or a discount (points negative, forward below spot).

**carry**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether a long base-currency forward position earns or pays the points to the forward date. It earns at a discount - the base out-yields the quote, so it is bought forward below spot - and pays at a premium. The short-base side is the opposite (Lehman Brothers, FX Training Manual: pay or earn the points).

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Number of executed trades aggregated into the tenor.

**total_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Sum of the base currency notional of the tenor's trades.

**min_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Lowest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `max_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

**max_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Highest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `min_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcFxForwardTradesData,
CftcFxForwardTradesQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to a pair or currency, matched against the two reported legs. 'EURUSD', 'EUR/USD' and 'EUR USD' all match EUR/USD; a single code like 'INR' matches every pair with that leg. Default is every pair, deliverable and non-deliverable.

**product_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by product: Forward (deliverable outright), Non-Deliverable Forward (cash-settled EM outright), FX Swap (near and far legs), Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Default is every product.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent day whose file holds forward prints; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by the action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). Default is every action; pass NEWT for newly executed trades only.

**settlement_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to trades whose leg-1 settlement currency matches, e.g. 'USD' for the USD-settled trades regardless of pair orientation. Non-deliverable forwards and swaps always carry it - their single cash-settlement currency; deliverable trades carry it only when reported. Default is every settlement.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Drop prints whose larger notional leg is disseminated below this amount. The two legs value the same trade in each currency, so the larger is a currency-agnostic size proxy. Amounts above the reporting cap disseminate at the cap.

**ticker**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. Default is every product. A ticker query is answered by the source's search API, cached per day, not the daily files.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of prints to return, newest execution first. Default is all matching.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**event_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time the reported event occurred, in UTC. The tape is ordered by it, newest first: a termination or correction of an old trade is dated when it is reported now, not when the trade was struck.

**execution_timestamp**: `datetime`<br/>
Date and time the forward was originally executed, in UTC. It equals the reported time on a new trade, but predates it on an amendment or termination.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair of the forward, its two reported legs.

**product_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Product, read from the FISN: Forward, Non-Deliverable Forward (`settlement_currency` is the cash-settled leg), FX Swap, Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Derived, not disseminated.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). An amendment carries the original trade's identifier in `original_trade_key`.

**exchange_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Agreed forward rate on the trade, oriented as `exchange_rate_basis` states. For an FX swap it is the rate of the disseminated leg.

**exchange_rate_basis**: `str | None`<br/>
Quotation the forward rate is expressed in, e.g. 'USD/INR'.

**notional_1**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 1 notional, in `notional_currency_1`.

**notional_currency_1**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 1 notional.

**notional_2**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 2 notional, in `notional_currency_2`.

**notional_currency_2**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 2 notional.

**settlement_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Settlement currency of leg 1. For a non-deliverable forward or swap it is the single currency the net cash settles in rather than delivering; a deliverable trade carries the physical settlement currency of leg 1 when reported.

**effective_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the forward comes into effect.

**expiration_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the forward settles.

**days_to_expiry**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar days from execution to expiration.

**cleared**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is centrally cleared: Y (cleared), N (not cleared), or I (intent to clear).

**venue**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility, or BILT when the reporting counterparty could not determine the venue.

**event_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Reason for the action: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation), ETRM (early termination), or CLRG (clearing).

**block_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is reported as a block trade.

**prime_brokerage**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is a prime-brokerage transaction.

**package_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is one leg of a package transaction - legs negotiated and priced together, such as the near and far legs of a swap booked as a package.

**package_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Grouping key shared by the legs of one package - its execution time and package price or spread. Group on it to reassemble the package. Derived, not disseminated.

**package_price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the whole package, in the format `package_price_notation` states; the same on every leg. Present on price-quoted packages, where DTCC's 9.9999999999 not-provided placeholder has been dropped to null.

**package_price_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the package price is denominated in, when it is a monetary amount.

**package_price_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_price`: 1 (a monetary amount, in `package_price_currency`) or 3 (a decimal).

**package_spread**: `float | None`<br/>
Spread of the whole package; the same on every leg. Present on spread-quoted packages instead of a price.

**package_spread_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_spread`: 1 (a monetary amount) or 3 (a decimal).

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name, e.g. 'NA/Fwd NDF INR USD'.

**underlier**: `str | None`<br/>
UPI underlier name, the two legs of the pair as reported.

**unique_product_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier.

**dissemination_date**: `date`<br/>
Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in.

**trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'FX:4419882315000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

**original_trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
For an action other than 'New', the qualified identifier of the original trade being amended, corrected or terminated. Match it against a `trade_key` to follow a trade's lifecycle.

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* EURUSD<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention. Limited to the pairs whose options are reported to the CFTC in enough depth to build a surface each day. The USD/EM pairs (USDBRL, USDKRW, ...) are built from non-deliverable options against a spot and forward taken from the reported non-deliverable forwards.

**basis**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* empirical<br/>

**date**: `date | None`<br/>

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3<br/>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>

Dissemination date of the options.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair.

**strike**: `float`<br/>
Strike price of the underlying, on a grid of offsets from spot.

**strike_offset**: `float`<br/>
The strike's distance from spot, positive above spot: in points for a deliverable major, in basis points of spot for a non-deliverable USD/EM pair.

**vol_1w**: `float | None`<br/>

**vol_2w**: `float | None`<br/>

2-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

3-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

6-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

9-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

Number of prints to return, newest execution first. Default is all matching.

*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**event_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time the reported event occurred, in UTC. The tape is ordered by it, newest first: a termination or correction of an old trade is dated when it is reported now, not when the trade was struck.

**execution_timestamp**: `datetime`<br/>
Date and time the option was originally executed, in UTC. It equals the reported time on a new trade, but predates it on an amendment or termination.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair of the option, its two reported legs.

**option_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Option family, read from the FISN: Vanilla, Non-Deliverable (cash-settled, `settlement_currency` is the payout leg), Digital, Barrier, or Target. Derived, not disseminated.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). An amendment carries the original trade's identifier in `original_trade_key`.

**call_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the option holder has the right to buy.

**call_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Notional of the currency bought, in `call_currency`.

**put_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the option holder has the right to sell.

**put_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Notional of the currency sold, in `put_currency`.

**strike**: `float | None`<br/>
Strike price of the option, oriented as `strike_pair` states.

**strike_pair**: `str | None`<br/>
Quotation the strike is expressed in, e.g. 'EUR/USD'. When absent, the strike follows `exchange_rate_basis`.

**strike_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format the strike is expressed in, per the CFTC Part 43/45 spec: 1 (a price, i.e. the exchange rate) or 3 (a decimal).

**expiration_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the option expires.

**days_to_expiry**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar days from execution to expiration.

**premium_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Option premium paid, in `premium_currency`.

**premium_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the premium is denominated in.

**settlement_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency a cash-settled option pays out in. Populated for non-deliverable options, whose non-deliverable leg settles in this currency rather than delivering.

**cleared**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is centrally cleared: Y (cleared), N (not cleared), or I (intent to clear).

**venue**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility, or BILT when the reporting counterparty could not determine the venue.

**exchange_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Posted exchange rate on the trade, oriented as `exchange_rate_basis` states. A proxy for spot at execution, the pricing reference for the strike.

**exchange_rate_basis**: `str | None`<br/>
Quotation the exchange rate is expressed in, e.g. 'EUR/USD'.

**notional_1**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 1 notional, in `notional_currency_1`.

**notional_currency_1**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 1 notional.

**notional_2**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 2 notional, in `notional_currency_2`.

**notional_currency_2**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 2 notional.

**effective_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the option comes into effect.

**first_exercise_date**: `date | None`<br/>
First date the option may be exercised.

**event_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Reason for the action: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation), ETRM (early termination), EXER (exercise), or CLRG (clearing).

**block_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is reported as a block trade.

**prime_brokerage**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is a prime-brokerage transaction.

**package_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is one leg of a package transaction - a strategy (straddle, risk reversal, calendar spread, ...) whose legs are negotiated and priced together.

**package_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Grouping key shared by the legs of one package - its execution time and package price or spread. Group on it to reassemble a strategy. Derived, not disseminated.

**package_price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the whole package, in the format `package_price_notation` states; the same on every leg. Present on price-quoted packages, where DTCC's 9.9999999999 not-provided placeholder has been dropped to null.

**package_price_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the package price is denominated in, when it is a monetary amount.

**package_price_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_price`: 1 (a monetary amount, in `package_price_currency`) or 3 (a decimal).

**package_spread**: `float | None`<br/>
Spread of the whole package; the same on every leg. Present on spread-quoted packages instead of a price.

**package_spread_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_spread`: 1 (a monetary amount) or 3 (a decimal).

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name, e.g. 'NA/O Van Call EUR USD'. Its Call/Put label is unreliable; use the call and put currencies.

**underlier**: `str | None`<br/>
UPI underlier name, the two legs of the pair as reported.

**unique_product_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier.

**dissemination_date**: `date`<br/>
Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in.

**trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'FX:4419821879000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

**original_trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
For an action other than 'New', the qualified identifier of the original trade being amended, corrected or terminated. Match it against a `trade_key` to follow a trade's lifecycle.

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "Cftc Ois Curve"
description: "Get an overnight index swap curve, built from executed swap transactions"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `CftcOisCurve` | `CftcOisCurveQueryParams` | `CftcOisCurveData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcOisCurveData,
CftcOisCurveQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap curve. Each maps to that currency's overnight benchmark rate. Currencies whose overnight index swaps are too thinly reported to bootstrap a curve are not offered. CNY builds from FR007 fixed-float swaps, backstopped by the CFETS daily bulletin's traded curve.

**curve_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* par<br/>
Which representation of the curve to return in `rate`: the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. The forward curve is a separate endpoint, `ois_forward_curve`.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency, which still leaves sparse tenors missing.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects the most recent day on or before it that priced this currency, defaulting to the latest. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 7<br/>
Number of dissemination days to look back over, ending on `date`. With source='search' a longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days` and cap it with `max_staleness_days`. A thinly traded currency reaches a full curve only over a long window - the search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon. With source='slice' it is how far back to walk for the most recent day that priced this currency.

**max_staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Drop any node whose freshest print is older than this many days, measured from the curve's own date. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago in a different rate regime; capping staleness keeps the curve current rather than a mosaic of old levels. Only meaningful with source='search'. None keeps every live node and reports its age in `staleness_days`. Nodes that have already matured by the curve date are always dropped, cap or none.

**granularity**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* benchmark<br/>
Tenor axis of the curve. 'benchmark' snaps trades to standard nodes; 'observed' emits a node for every distinct tenor traded, including broken dates.

**aggregation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* median<br/>
How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate. Median is the default because notionals above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap, which biases notional-weighted averages.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades on their as-of day. The default keeps every node, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is. Raise it to admit only nodes several trades agree on, at the cost of losing the tenors a thin currency never trades in depth on any single day.

**cleared**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Keep only centrally cleared or intent-to-clear trades, dropping the bilateral uncleared prints that carry most of the off-market noise. Most useful with granularity='observed', where thin nodes are exposed to it.

**interpolation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* log_linear<br/>
How discount factors are interpolated between pillars, on the log of the discount factor. 'log_linear' is piecewise linear, giving piecewise-flat instantaneous forwards. 'log_cubic' is a monotone Hermite cubic, giving smooth forwards without overshooting into negative rates.

**overnight_anchor**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Anchor the curve's front end with the benchmark's latest published overnight fixing, as a 1-day node. The fixing is a realized rate, so the node carries no trades and its own as-of date.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve, being that of its freshest node.

**currency**: `str`<br/>
Currency of the curve.

**benchmark**: `str`<br/>
Overnight benchmark rate the swaps reference (SOFR, ESTR, ...).

**index**: `str`<br/>
Curve index plotted on the chart and used as the row index: the tenor label under 'benchmark' granularity, else the node's maturity date under 'observed' granularity.

**as_of_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the node's trades were reported on. Nodes are priced from the most recent day that cleared min_trades, so a thin tenor is dated earlier than a deep one.

**staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Days between the node's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest nodes.

**tenor**: `str`<br/>
Tenor of the curve node.

**tenor_days**: `int`<br/>
Tenor of the node, in days.

**tenor_years**: `float`<br/>
Tenor of the node, in years, on an ACT/365F basis.

**maturity_date**: `date`<br/>
Maturity date implied by the node's tenor, from its as-of date. Under 'observed' granularity this is also the curve's index.

**rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Rate of the selected `curve_type` at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%): the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. In percent rather than a decimal so the chart axis reads as a rate - the grid formatter is not applied to the chart. Omitted where the bootstrap degenerates.

**curve_type**: `str`<br/>
Which representation `rate` holds: par or zero.

**discount_factor**: `float | None`<br/>
Discount factor bootstrapped to the node's maturity.

**day_count**: `str | None`<br/>
Fixed-leg day count convention the node's trades reported, used to accrue the fixed leg in the bootstrap. ACT/360 for USD, EUR, CHF, MXN, COP and CLP; ACT/365F for GBP, JPY, CAD, SGD, INR, ZAR, THB, ILS, AUD and NZD. BRL reports BUS/252, recovered to the same year fraction on calendar days.

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Number of executed trades aggregated into the node.

**total_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Sum of the leg 1 notional of the node's trades.

**min_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Lowest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

**max_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Highest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any trade at the node had its notional disseminated at the reporting cap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap curve.

**forward_tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1Y<br/>
Length of the forward swap - the tenor of the swap priced at each forward start date. Independent of the spacing between starts.

**forward_step**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3M<br/>
Spacing between forward start dates. Set it apart from `forward_tenor` to plot, say, the 5Y forward at yearly starts (forward_tenor='5Y', forward_step='1Y').

**forward_count**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of forward start dates to plot. Defaults to the whole curve out to its last pillar; set it to plot only the first N steps (e.g. 10 with a 1Y step is the next ten years of the forward).

**method**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* implied<br/>
How the forward rates are formed. 'implied' reads them off the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson fit of the bootstrapped spot curve. 'observed' takes the fixed rates of the forward-starting swaps of the tenor directly, medianed by start and smoothed onto the grid - the market's own forward quotes, which reach only as far as that forward has traded.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days; 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Ends the search window, or selects the most recent slice on or before it that priced this currency. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 7<br/>
Days to look back over: the search window with source='search', or how far to walk back for the most recent priced day with source='slice'. The search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon, so a thin currency can fill its forwards from a full year of prints.

**max_staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Drop any underlying node whose freshest print is older than this many days. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago; capping staleness keeps the forward strip current. Only meaningful with source='search'.

**aggregation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* median<br/>
How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades.

**interpolation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* log_linear<br/>
Discount-factor interpolation for the bootstrap the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson forward fit is drawn from.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Tabs>

title: "Cftc Ois Policy Path"
description: "Get the central bank's expected overnight-rate path from forward-starting OIS"
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

---

## Implementation details

### Class names

| Model name | Parameters class | Data class |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| `CftcOisPolicyPath` | `CftcOisPolicyPathQueryParams` | `CftcOisPolicyPathData` |

### Import Statement

```python
from openbb_core.provider.standard_models. import (
CftcOisPolicyPathData,
CftcOisPolicyPathQueryParams,
)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the policy path, read from its forward-starting OIS. Only the currencies whose central banks trade meeting-dated OIS in depth are offered.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC) the path is built as of; defaults to the most recent. It anchors the forward start, so a window ending here is used and a trade whose start has since rolled to spot drops out.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 10<br/>
Number of recent daily files to combine, ending on `date`. Meeting-dated OIS are thin on any single day, so a handful of files are pooled to price each forward start in depth; a node's own freshest day is reported as `as_of_date`.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3<br/>
Drop a forward start priced by fewer than this many trades across the window. The default trims the one-off prints that are not meeting nodes.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date the path is built as of.

**currency**: `str`<br/>
Currency of the path.

**index**: `str`<br/>
Forward start date of the period - the row and chart index.

**rate**: `float`<br/>
Expected average overnight rate over the period, in percent.

**forward_days**: `int`<br/>
Days from the curve date to the period's start.

**start_date**: `date | str`<br/>
Start (effective date) of the period.

End (maturity) of the period.

Length of the period, in days.

**max_rate**: `float`<br/>
Highest executed rate at the node, in percent.

</TabItem>
