### Form

An [input form](/workspace/developers/widget-parameters/input-form) pairs a POST route that accepts one Pydantic model with a GET route that names it in `form_endpoint`. The launcher turns the model's fields into the form's inputs, adds a submit button if the model has none, and leaves the POST route out of the widget list. Workspace refreshes the GET widget after a successful submission.

```python
import uuid
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

app = FastAPI()

AccountType = Literal["General Fund", "Separately Managed", "Family Office"]


class IntakeSubmission(BaseModel):
    """Submit a new intake form."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(model_title_generator=lambda model: "Submit Form")

    first_name: str = Field(title="First Name")
    last_name: str = Field(title="Last Name")
    account_type: AccountType = Field(title="Account Type")


class IntakeRecord(BaseModel):
    """One submitted intake form."""

    first_name: str = Field(title="First Name")
    last_name: str = Field(title="Last Name")
    account_type: AccountType = Field(title="Account Type")
    record_id: uuid.UUID = Field(title="Record ID", default_factory=uuid.uuid4)


RECORDS: list[IntakeRecord] = []


@app.post("/intake_submit")
async def intake_submit(data: IntakeSubmission) -> bool:
    """Store a submitted form."""
    RECORDS.append(IntakeRecord(**data.model_dump()))
    return True


@app.get(
    "/intake",
    openapi_extra={"widget_config": {"form_endpoint": "/intake_submit"}},
)
async def intake() -> list[IntakeRecord]:
    """Submitted intake forms."""
    return RECORDS
```

### Server-side row model

A POST route becomes an `ssrm_table` widget, with no `widget_config` needed, when its body is `AgGridRowsRequest` or a subclass of it, or when its response is `AgGridRowsResponse[Row]`. Both models come from `openbb_core.app.model.aggrid`. The request carries AG Grid's `startRow`, `endRow`, `sortModel`, `filterModel`, and `grouping`; the response returns one page as `rowData` and the total row count as `rowCount`. See [SSRM mode](/workspace/developers/widget-types/ssrm_mode).

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from openbb_core.app.model.aggrid import AgGridRowsRequest, AgGridRowsResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Row(BaseModel):
    """One row."""

    symbol: str
    price: float


ROWS = [Row(symbol=f"SYM{i}", price=float(i)) for i in range(1000)]


@app.post("/rows")
async def rows(request: AgGridRowsRequest) -> AgGridRowsResponse[Row]:
    """Server-side paged rows."""
    page = ROWS[request.startRow : request.endRow]
    return AgGridRowsResponse[Row](rowData=page, rowCount=len(ROWS))
```

## apps.json and agents.json

`/apps.json` serves [app templates](/workspace/developers/json-specs/apps-json-reference) from the `--apps-json` file, by default `workspace_apps.json` in the data directory set in `~/.openbb_platform/user_settings.json` (`~/OpenBBUserData` unless changed). The launcher creates an empty file if none exists and adds the templates bundled with the package and those returned by routes ending in `apps.json`. A template is served only if every widget in its layout exists in the current `widgets.json`, so templates saved from Workspace appear only when the backend can supply them. A directory passed to `--apps-json` is searched for `workspace_apps.json`, then `apps.json`.

`/agents.json` serves the [agents](/workspace/developers/json-specs/agents-json-reference) file given with `--agents-json`, or the agents returned by routes ending in `agents.json`, or an empty object.

## Generate widgets.json without a server

The builder the launcher uses is a function of an OpenAPI dictionary and a list of exclusions, in the format described in [Exclude widgets](#exclude-widgets):

```python
import json

from openbb_platform_api.utils.widgets import build_json

from my_app import app

widgets = build_json(app.openapi(), [])
print(json.dumps(widgets, indent=2))
```

The same call works on an `openapi.json` document loaded from any server.

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="openbb-mcp | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

The [`openbb-mcp-server`](https://pypi.org/project/openbb-mcp-server/) package installs the `openbb-mcp` command, which serves the routes of a FastAPI app as Model Context Protocol tools through [FastMCP](https://gofastmcp.com). By default the app is the OpenBB REST API built from the installed extensions. `--app` serves any other FastAPI app, and `--spec` serves a proxy built from an `openbb-cli` `.spec` file.

## Installation

```bash
pip install openbb-mcp-server openbb-cboe openbb-imf
```

The package requires Python 3.10 or newer and `openbb-core` 2.x. The tools come from whatever provider and extension packages are installed alongside it. The `cli` extra installs `openbb-cli` and enables four more tools:

```bash
pip install "openbb-mcp-server[cli]"
```

## Launch

```bash
openbb-mcp
```

The default transport is `streamable-http` at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp`. Run `openbb-mcp --help` to print the flags and a commented `openbb.toml` example.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app` | Installed REST API | FastAPI app whose routes become tools: a Python file, `file.py:name`, or `package.module:name`. |
| `--name` | `app` | Name of the app instance or factory function. A `:name` suffix on `--app` sets it too. |
| `--factory` | Off | Call `--name` to create the app. |
| `--spec` | None | `.spec` file to serve as a proxy. Cannot be combined with `--app`. |
| `--config-file` | None | TOML file applied on top of the discovered `openbb.toml` files. Also read from `OPENBB_MCP_CONFIG`, `OPENBB_API_CONFIG`, or `OPENBB_CONFIG`. |
| `--transport` | `streamable-http` | `streamable-http`, `sse`, or `stdio`. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address for the HTTP transports. |
| `--port` | `8001` | Bind port for the HTTP transports. |
| `--allowed-categories` | All | Comma-separated categories to serve. Routes in other categories are never registered. |
| `--default-categories` | `all` | With tool discovery off, the categories whose tools are listed and callable. |
| `--tool-discovery` | Off | Hide the command tools behind the discovery tools. |
| `--system-prompt` | None | Text file used as the system prompt. |
| `--server-prompts` | None | JSON file of prompt definitions. |

Every other `--key value` pair is routed by name. A key that matches a [setting](#settings), with hyphens or underscores, sets it, as in `--enable-cli-tools false` or `--server-auth '["user", "pass"]'`. A key starting with `httpx-` sets an option of the httpx client that sends tool calls to the app, as in `--httpx-verify false`. Anything else goes to uvicorn with hyphens converted to underscores, as in `--log-level debug` or `--ssl-keyfile key.pem`. The values `true` and `false` become booleans, and a value wrapped in `[]` or `{}` is parsed as JSON.

## Configuration

Settings are resolved from four sources. Each overrides the ones below it:

1. Command-line flags.
2. The `[mcp]` table of the `openbb.toml` files, applied as if its keys were flags.
3. `OPENBB_MCP_*` environment variables.
4. `~/.openbb_platform/mcp_settings.json`, which the server writes with the defaults on its first run.

For some data providers, the API key must be set in the OpenBB [credentials](../../user-guide/credentials.mdx), not in the MCP settings.

### Settings

| Setting | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `OPENBB_MCP_NAME` | `str` | `"OpenBB MCP"` | Server name reported to clients. |
| `description` | `OPENBB_MCP_DESCRIPTION` | `str` | Built-in text | Server description. |
| `version` | `OPENBB_MCP_VERSION` | `str` | `None` | Server version. |
| `instructions` | `OPENBB_MCP_INSTRUCTIONS` | `str` | `None` | Text sent to the client during the MCP `initialize` handshake. When unset, the system prompt fills it. |
| `api_prefix` | `OPENBB_MCP_API_PREFIX` | `str` | `None` | Prefix stripped from route paths when naming tools. `None` uses the OpenBB API prefix, `/api/v1`. |
| `default_tool_categories` | `OPENBB_MCP_DEFAULT_TOOL_CATEGORIES` | `list[str]` | `["all"]` | With tool discovery off, the categories served. Other tools are registered but disabled, unless a route sets `enable`. Ignored with tool discovery on. |
| `allowed_tool_categories` | `OPENBB_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOL_CATEGORIES` | `list[str]` | `None` | The only categories served, with or without discovery. `None` or `["all"]` serves every category. |
| `enable_tool_discovery` | `OPENBB_MCP_ENABLE_TOOL_DISCOVERY` | `bool` | `False` | Hide the command tools behind `available_categories`, `available_tools`, `search_tools`, and `call_tool`. |
| `list_page_size` | `OPENBB_MCP_LIST_PAGE_SIZE` | `int` | `None` | Maximum items per page in MCP list responses. `None` returns everything in one page. |
| `describe_responses` | `OPENBB_MCP_DESCRIBE_RESPONSES` | `bool` | `False` | Keep the query parameter and response documentation in tool descriptions. When `False`, descriptions stop before it. |
| `system_prompt_file` | `OPENBB_MCP_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE` | `str` | `None` | Path to a text file used as the system prompt. |
| `server_prompts_file` | `OPENBB_MCP_SERVER_PROMPTS_FILE` | `str` | `None` | Path to a JSON file of prompt definitions. |
| `default_skills_dir` | `OPENBB_MCP_DEFAULT_SKILLS_DIR` | `str` | Bundled skills | Directory of skills, one subdirectory with a `SKILL.md` per skill. `null` or an empty string disables it. |
| `skills_reload` | `OPENBB_MCP_SKILLS_RELOAD` | `bool` | `False` | Re-read skill files on every read. |
| `skills_providers` | `OPENBB_MCP_SKILLS_PROVIDERS` | `list[str]` | `None` | Vendor skill directories to load: `claude`, `cursor`, `vscode`, `copilot`, `codex`, `gemini`, `goose`, `opencode`. |
| `enable_cli_tools` | `OPENBB_MCP_ENABLE_CLI_TOOLS` | `bool` | `True` | Register the `openbb-cli` dispatcher tools when `openbb-cli` is installed. |
| `on_duplicate` | `OPENBB_MCP_ON_DUPLICATE` | `str` | `None` | What to do when a tool, resource, or prompt is registered twice: `warn`, `error`, `replace`, or `ignore`. |
| `mask_error_details` | `OPENBB_MCP_MASK_ERROR_DETAILS` | `bool` | `None` | Hide exception details from clients. |
| `module_exclusion_map` | `OPENBB_MCP_MODULE_EXCLUSION_MAP` | `dict[str, str]` | `None` | Route path segments mapped to Python modules. Routes under a segment are hidden while its module is imported. `None` uses `{"coverage": "openbb_core"}`; `{}` hides nothing. |
| `uvicorn_config` | `OPENBB_MCP_UVICORN_CONFIG` | `dict` | `{"host": "127.0.0.1", "port": "8001"}` | Keyword arguments for uvicorn on the HTTP transports. Keys use underscores. |
| `httpx_client_kwargs` | `OPENBB_MCP_HTTPX_CLIENT_KWARGS` | `dict` | `{}` | Options for the httpx client that sends tool calls to the app, such as `headers`, `timeout`, or `verify`. |
| `client_auth` | `OPENBB_MCP_CLIENT_AUTH` | `[str, str]` | `None` | Username and password sent as httpx `auth` on requests to the app. |
| `server_auth` | `OPENBB_MCP_SERVER_AUTH` | `[str, str]` | `None` | Username and password that HTTP clients must send as a Bearer token. |

### Lists and dictionaries

List settings accept a comma-separated string or a JSON array, on the command line and in environment variables. Dictionary settings accept a JSON object on the command line; environment variables also accept comma-separated `key:value` pairs. Wrap JSON in single quotes in the shell so the double quotes reach the server intact.

```bash
openbb-mcp --default-categories cboe,imf
openbb-mcp --default-categories '["cboe", "imf"]'
openbb-mcp --uvicorn-config '{"host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 9000}'
```

```bash
OPENBB_MCP_DEFAULT_TOOL_CATEGORIES="cboe,imf"
OPENBB_MCP_UVICORN_CONFIG="host:0.0.0.0,port:9000"
OPENBB_MCP_HTTPX_CLIENT_KWARGS='{"timeout": 30}'
```

### openbb.toml

At startup `openbb-mcp` merges the layered `openbb.toml` files, lowest priority first: the `[tool.openbb]` table of the nearest `pyproject.toml` (so `[tool.openbb.mcp]` there), `~/.openbb_platform/openbb.toml`, the nearest `openbb.toml` walking up from the working directory, and the file given by `--config-file`, `OPENBB_MCP_CONFIG`, `OPENBB_API_CONFIG`, or `OPENBB_CONFIG`. `.openbb.toml` works in place of `openbb.toml`, and a syntax error in the explicit file stops the server at startup. The `[system]` table and the top-level shortcuts apply to the system settings of the server process, as described in [openbb.toml](../../user-guide/openbb-toml.mdx).

```toml
[mcp]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 8005
default-categories = "cboe,imf"
tool-discovery = true
enable_cli_tools = false

[mcp.auth]
hooks = ["my_pkg.auth:check_bearer_token"]

[mcp.middleware]
hooks = ["my_pkg.middleware:log_requests"]

[env]
OPENBB_MCP_NAME = "Research MCP"
```

`[mcp]` holds defaults for any flag or setting, with hyphens or underscores. `[env]` sets environment variables before the server starts, without replacing variables already set in the shell, and expands `$VAR` or `${VAR}` references. An entry that references an unset variable is skipped with a warning.

`[mcp.auth]` and `[mcp.middleware]` list `module:attribute` references to `async def hook(request, call_next)` functions. They wrap the `streamable-http` and `sse` transports, not `stdio`. Auth hooks run before middleware hooks, and each list runs in order. A reference that cannot be imported, is not async, or takes fewer than two arguments stops the server at startup.

`[mcp.spec]` configures [spec proxy mode](#spec-proxy-mode). When it is absent, a top-level `[spec]` table is used instead, so one `openbb.toml` can configure the same proxy for `openbb-api` and `openbb-mcp`.

## Authentication

### Server authentication

`server_auth` requires every HTTP request to carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the Base64 encoding of `username:password`. Requests without a valid token are rejected. Set it in `mcp_settings.json`, in the environment, or on the command line:

```json
{
  "server_auth": ["admin", "secretpass"]
}
```

```bash
OPENBB_MCP_SERVER_AUTH='["admin", "secretpass"]'
```

A client then sends the encoded pair, here `base64("admin:secretpass")`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openbb-mcp": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YWRtaW46c2VjcmV0cGFzcw=="
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Client authentication

`client_auth` is the credential the MCP server sends to the app it wraps, as httpx `auth`. A username and password pair is sent as HTTP Basic authentication, which matches the login of an OpenBB API started with `OPENBB_API_AUTH` enabled.

```bash
OPENBB_MCP_CLIENT_AUTH='["client_user", "client_pass"]'
```

### In code

`create_mcp_server` builds the FastMCP server from settings and an app. Its `auth` argument accepts any FastMCP `AuthProvider`, a `(username, password)` pair with the same meaning as `server_auth`, or `None`; anything else raises `TypeError`.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.jwt import JWTVerifier
from openbb_mcp_server.app.app import create_mcp_server
from openbb_mcp_server.models.settings import MCPSettings

auth = JWTVerifier(
    jwks_uri="https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
    issuer="https://auth.example.com",
    audience="openbb-mcp",
)
mcp = create_mcp_server(MCPSettings(), FastAPI(), auth=auth)
mcp.run(transport="streamable-http")
```

## Spec proxy mode

A `.spec` file, written by `openbb --generate-spec`, records the routes and address of an OpenBB API server. [Codegen](../../../cli/codegen.md) covers generating one. With `--spec`, the server builds a FastAPI app whose routes forward each request to the spec's `base_url`, and serves those routes as tools. The MCP process then needs no provider packages; the data comes from the upstream server.

```bash
openbb --generate-spec --server https://api.example.com --output api.spec
openbb-mcp --spec api.spec
```

The spec is checked at startup: it must be version 5, have a `base_url` and a `commands` table, and carry a `content_sha256` that matches its contents. `[mcp.spec]` adds what the file cannot hold:

```toml
[mcp.spec]
path = "/etc/openbb/api.spec"
base_url = "https://upstream.example.com"
content_sha256 = "<expected sha256>"

[mcp.spec.headers]
Authorization = "Bearer $OPENBB_UPSTREAM_TOKEN"
```

`base_url` replaces the recorded address, `content_sha256` pins the expected revision, and `[mcp.spec.headers]` adds headers to every upstream request with `$VAR` substitution, replacing any header of the same name. To serve several specs, give each a `[mcp.spec.NAME]` table with its own `path`, an optional `mount` that defaults to `/NAME`, and its own `base_url`, `content_sha256`, `headers`, `auth`, and `middleware`. The [openbb-api reference](openbb-api.mdx#spec-proxy-mode) describes the same tables for the REST launcher in more detail.

## Tools

### Names and categories

A tool's name is built from its route path after the API prefix, skipping `{placeholder}` segments. `/api/v1/cboe/equity/quote` is `cboe_equity_quote`, a two-segment path such as `/demo/items` is `demo_items`, and a single-segment path repeats the segment, so `/hello` is `hello_hello`. When one path serves several methods, the non-GET tools get a `_<method>` suffix, as in `demo_items_post`. A route's `mcp_config.name` replaces the generated name.

The first path segment is the tool's category, and the second, on paths with three or more segments, its subcategory; other tools fall in the subcategory `general`. For the default app, categories are the provider namespaces such as `cboe`, `imf`, and `fred`, plus `news`, `econometrics`, `quantitative`, and `technical` when those packages are installed.

### Built-in tools

These tools are registered next to the command tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `run_pipeline` | Run several tools in sequence on the server, feeding earlier results into later arguments. |
| `list_prompts` | List prompts with their arguments. |
| `get_prompt` | Render a prompt by `name` with optional `arguments`. |
| `list_resources` | List resources, including skills. |
| `read_resource` | Read a resource by `uri`. |
| `install_skill` | Write a skill into the bundled or a vendor skills directory. |
| `openbb_dispatch` | Run one command through `openbb-cli`. Requires the `cli` extra. |
| `openbb_batch_dispatch` | Run a list of commands concurrently through `openbb-cli`. Requires the `cli` extra. |
| `openbb_list_commands` | List every command with a one-line description. Requires the `cli` extra. |
| `openbb_describe_command` | Describe one command's parameters and output schema. Requires the `cli` extra. |

The four `openbb_*` tools take an optional `server_url`. Without one they use `OPENBB_SERVER_URL`, and without that they run in process. Set `enable_cli_tools` to `false` to leave them out.

`install_skill` writes files to the server's disk for any connected client. When clients are not trusted, keep the skills directories read-only for the server process or require `server_auth`.

### Tool discovery

With `--tool-discovery`, the command tools are left out of the tool list and reached through four more tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `available_categories` | Categories and subcategories with tool counts. |
| `available_tools` | Tools in a `category`, optionally one `subcategory`, with one-sentence descriptions. |
| `search_tools` | Full definitions, including input schemas, of the tools that best match a natural-language query. |
| `call_tool` | Run any tool by name with its arguments. |

A hidden tool can also be called directly by name. Discovery keeps no per-session state, so every client and transport sees the same tool list and several clients can share one server.

Without discovery, `default_tool_categories` limits the tools that are listed and callable, and tools outside those categories fail as unknown tools. With discovery, `default_tool_categories` is ignored. `allowed_tool_categories` applies in both modes: routes outside it are never registered and cannot be reached by name, through `call_tool`, or through `run_pipeline`.

### Pipelines

`openbb-econometrics`, `openbb-quantitative`, and `openbb-technical` commands take the rows to analyze as a `data` argument. `run_pipeline` passes rows between steps on the server, so a price history does not travel through the conversation. Each step has an optional `id`, a `tool`, its `arguments`, and `inputs`, which map an argument name to an earlier step's `id`. The input is that step's `results`, the rows of a chart artifact, a lone wrapped `result`, or the whole output when it has none of these. `outputs` selects the steps to return and defaults to the last one.

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "prices",
      "tool": "cboe_equity_historical",
      "arguments": {"symbol": "AAPL", "provider": "cboe"}
    },
    {
      "id": "rsi",
      "tool": "technical_rsi",
      "arguments": {"length": 14},
      "inputs": {"data": "prices"}
    }
  ],
  "outputs": ["rsi"]
}
```

The pipeline is validated before any step runs, a step cannot call `run_pipeline`, and a failing step is reported by its id. `run_pipeline` calls only tools the server serves.

### Parameter choices

Tool input schemas state the valid values of each parameter, taken from the provider `choices` and `x-widget_config` options declared on the command. A parameter with one fixed set of values gets an `enum`. When providers accept different values, the description lists them by provider, and multi-value or partially declared choices are listed in the description. A parameter whose options come from an `optionsEndpoint` names the tool that lists them.

### Charts

A Plotly figure in a tool result, returned directly or as an `OBBject` `chart` when the call passes `chart: true`, is replaced by an OpenBB Workspace artifact. Line, bar, scatter, pie, and donut figures become a `chart` artifact whose `content` rows and `chart_params` redraw the figure. Other figures become a `table` artifact of their data. Tool output schemas declare the artifact in place of the figure.

## Prompts

### System prompt

`--system-prompt`, `system_prompt_file`, or `OPENBB_MCP_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE` points to a text file. Its content is served as the `system_prompt` prompt and the `resource://system_prompt` resource, and fills `instructions` when that setting is empty. Clients do not apply it automatically; instruct them to read it.

When skills are loaded and no system prompt file is set, the server adds a short `system_prompt` that points the agent to the skills.

### Server prompts

`--server-prompts`, `server_prompts_file`, or `OPENBB_MCP_SERVER_PROMPTS_FILE` points to a JSON list of prompts. Each prompt has a `name`, a `description`, and a `content` string with `{placeholder}` arguments, plus optional `arguments` and `tags`. Each argument has a `name`, a `type` (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `list`, `dict`, or `any`), and an optional `default` and `description`. An argument without a default is required. An invalid prompt or argument is logged as an error and skipped.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "options_review",
    "description": "Review the options market for one symbol.",
    "content": "Review the options market for {symbol}. Get the quote with cboe_equity_quote, then summarize the implied volatility term structure with cboe_options_term_structure. Focus on {focus}.",
    "arguments": [
      {
        "name": "symbol",
        "type": "str",
        "description": "Ticker symbol, such as AAPL."
      },
      {
        "name": "focus",
        "type": "str",
        "default": "near-term expirations",
        "description": "What the summary should emphasize."
      }
    ],
    "tags": ["options"]
  }
]
```

### Inline prompts

A route can carry prompts in `openapi_extra["mcp_config"]["prompts"]`. Each `{placeholder}` in `content` becomes an argument: a prompt argument of the same name, else the endpoint parameter, else a required string. The rendered prompt starts by naming the route's tool, and the tool's description lists its prompts.

```python
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.get(
    "/macro/gdp",
    openapi_extra={
        "mcp_config": {
            "prompts": [
                {
                    "name": "gdp_summary_prompt",
                    "description": "Generate a brief summary of GDP for a country.",
                    "content": "Provide a concise summary of the GDP for {country} over the last {years} years.",
                    "arguments": [
                        {
                            "name": "years",
                            "type": "int",
                            "default": 5,
                            "description": "Number of years to summarize.",
                        }
                    ],
                    "tags": ["gdp", "summary"],
                }
            ]
        }
    },
)
def get_gdp_data(country: str, period: Literal["annual", "quarterly"] = "annual"):
    """Get GDP data for a specific country."""
    return {"country": country, "period": period}
```

The description of the `macro_gdp` tool then ends with:

```markdown
**Associated Prompts:**
- **gdp_summary_prompt**: Generate a brief summary of GDP for a country.
  - Arguments: `country`, `years`
```

MCP passes prompt arguments as strings, so quote every value in a `get_prompt` call:

```json
{
  "name": "gdp_summary_prompt",
  "arguments": {"years": "10", "country": "Japan"}
}
```

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Use the tool, macro_gdp, to perform the following task.\n\nProvide a concise summary of the GDP for Japan over the last 10 years."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Skills

Skills are Markdown guides served as MCP resources at `skill://<name>/SKILL.md` and listed by `list_resources`. The server ships five:

| Skill | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `develop_extension` | Creating a new OpenBB extension from scratch. |
| `build_workspace_app` | Building, running, and serving a Workspace application from an extension project. |
| `configure_mcp_server` | Installing, configuring, and connecting `openbb-mcp-server`. |
| `work_with_server` | Calling tools, reading responses, and handling errors as an agent. |
| `use_openbb_cli` | The `openbb` command line, `.spec` files, and spec proxy mode. |

Set `default_skills_dir` to another directory to replace them, or to `null` or an empty string to turn them off. `skills_providers` also loads skill directories from other tools, such as `["claude", "cursor"]`, and `skills_reload` re-reads skill files on every read while you edit them.

## Per-route configuration

`openapi_extra["mcp_config"]` controls how one route becomes a tool. If `mcp_config` is absent, `openapi_extra["x-mcp"]` is read instead. Values are validated with `MCPConfigModel`; an invalid configuration is logged as an error and ignored for that route.

| Key | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expose` | `bool` | `False` hides the route from the server. |
| `mcp_type` | `str` | Serve the route as a `tool`, `resource`, or `resource_template`. |
| `methods` | `list[str]` | HTTP methods of the route to serve, or `["*"]` for all. The others are left out. |
| `exclude_args` | `list[str]` | Arguments left out of the tool's input schema. Each needs a default, which is then used. |
| `name` | `str` | Tool name, replacing the generated one. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | Tags added next to the category. |
| `enable` | `bool` | With discovery off, serve (`True`) or hide (`False`) the tool regardless of `default_tool_categories`. |
| `describe_responses` | `bool` | Override `describe_responses` for this tool. |
| `mime_type` | `str` | MIME type of a route served as a resource. |
| `prompts` | `list[dict]` | [Inline prompts](#inline-prompts). |

```python
@app.get(
    "/some/route",
    openapi_extra={
        "mcp_config": {
            "mcp_type": "tool",
            "methods": ["GET"],
            "exclude_args": ["internal_param"],
            "name": "some_route",
        }
    },
)
def some_route(param1: str, internal_param: str = "default"):
    """An example route with MCP configuration."""
    return {"param1": param1}
```

In OpenBB routers, pass the dictionary as the `mcp_config` argument of `@router.command`, which stores it in `openapi_extra`.

## Connect a client

### Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop starts the server itself over `stdio`. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, `uvx` creates the environment on demand; add a `--with` pair for each provider package:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openbb-mcp": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--from",
        "openbb-mcp-server",
        "--with",
        "openbb-cboe",
        "--with",
        "openbb-imf",
        "openbb-mcp",
        "--transport",
        "stdio"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop after editing its configuration.

### Cursor

Start the server with `openbb-mcp`, then add it to the `mcpServers` object in Cursor's `mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openbb-mcp": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Changes from V4

Compared with `openbb-mcp-server` 1.4.1, the version on the V4 `main` branch, discovery no longer activates tools per session. `activate_tools`, `deactivate_tools`, and `activate_category` were removed; hidden tools are found with `search_tools` and run with `call_tool` or by name. `run_pipeline`, the `openbb-cli` dispatcher tools, chart artifacts, `openbb.toml` support, `--config-file`, and `--spec` are new.

`on_duplicate` replaces `on_duplicate_tools`, `on_duplicate_resources`, and `on_duplicate_prompts`. `cache_expiration_seconds`, `resource_prefix_format`, `dependencies`, and `deprecation_warnings` were removed, and `enable_cli_tools` was added.

description: The openbb-core package - the runtime that discovers installed extensions and exposes them as the obb Python client and a REST API.
keywords:
  - openbb-core
  - openbb-build
  - entry points
  - Router
  - Provider
  - OBBject
  - FastAPI
  - Pydantic
---

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 MD037 -->

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="openbb-core | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

`openbb-core` is the runtime layer. By itself it ships no data, no providers, and no commands. It finds the extensions installed in the current Python environment, merges them into one router, generates the typed `obb` client from that router, and serves the same router as a FastAPI application. Every call returns an [`OBBject`](../concepts/obbject.mdx).

The package contains both the `openbb_core` module and the `openbb` module that `from openbb import obb` imports. Most users never install it directly; provider and toolkit packages depend on it.

## Installation

```sh
pip install openbb-core
```

Two optional extras are declared. `pandas` adds pandas, which the data-processing extensions, `openbb-news`, and `openbb-charting` require through `openbb-core[pandas]`. `flask` adds Flask and `a2wsgi`.

```sh
pip install "openbb-core[pandas]"
```

The package requires Python `>=3.10,<4`. Its direct dependencies are `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic` 2, `websockets`, `aiohttp`, `requests`, `python-multipart`, `uuid7`, `importlib-metadata`, `python-dotenv`, `ruff`, `pyjwt`, and, on Python 3.10, `tomli`.

## Entry points

Extensions register with the runtime through setuptools entry points. The core reads three groups.

| Group | Target | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openbb_core_extension` | a `Router`, `FastAPI`, or `APIRouter` instance | Commands mounted under `obb.<name>` and `/api/v1/<name>` |
| `openbb_provider_extension` | a `Provider` instance | A data source selectable with `provider="<name>"` |
| `openbb_obbject_extension` | an `Extension` instance | An accessor on every `OBBject`, or a callback on command output |

A fourth group, `openbb_charting_extension`, is read by the charting engine rather than by the core; it maps chart views to command routes. The [extension types](../concepts/extensions.mdx) page describes each group and its options.

Each V5 provider package registers both a provider entry point and a router entry point, which is how `obb.fred`, `obb.sec`, and the other provider namespaces come to exist.

## Building the Python client

The `obb` object is generated code. After installing, upgrading, or removing an extension, regenerate it:

```sh
openbb-build
```

The command imports `openbb` in a subprocess, which rebuilds the static package when it is missing or stale, and calls `openbb.build()` directly if the import did not rebuild. Importing `openbb` also rebuilds on its own when it detects that extensions were added or removed since the last build; set `OPENBB_AUTO_BUILD=false` to turn that off, for example in a container image where the build ran at install time.

## Serving the REST API

The router that backs `from openbb import obb` is also a FastAPI application at `openbb_core.api.rest_api:app`, so any ASGI server can run it:

```sh
uvicorn openbb_core.api.rest_api:app --reload
```

The interactive OpenAPI documentation is served at `/docs`. For Workspace integration, widgets, and launcher options, use [`openbb-api`](./interface/openbb-api.mdx), which wraps this application.

## Classes for extension authors

Extension packages build on a small set of public classes.

| Class | Import path | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Router` | `openbb_core.app.router` | Declares commands with `@router.command(...)` |
| `Provider` | `openbb_core.provider.abstract.provider` | Describes a data source, its credentials, and its fetchers |
| `Fetcher` | `openbb_core.provider.abstract.fetcher` | Implements `transform_query`, `extract_data` or `aextract_data`, and `transform_data` |
| `QueryParams` | `openbb_core.provider.abstract.query_params` | Base Pydantic model for command parameters |
| `Data` | `openbb_core.provider.abstract.data` | Base Pydantic model for returned rows |
| `OBBject` | `openbb_core.app.model.obbject` | The response envelope |
| `Extension` | `openbb_core.app.model.extension` | Registers an OBBject accessor or command-output callback |

A provider's credentials are named `<provider>_<credential>`: a `Provider(name="fred", credentials=["api_key"])` produces the credential `fred_api_key`.

See the [architecture](../concepts/architecture.mdx) page for how a call flows through these pieces, and the [extension types](../developer/extension_types/index.md) section to start building.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 MD037 -->

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="openbb-news | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

`openbb-news` adds the `obb.news` namespace. Its main command, `rss`, reads an RSS or Atom feed from a registry of named feeds and returns each article with its title, date, author, link, a short excerpt, and optionally the full article body as Markdown. The registry ships with 562 feeds grouped into 21 outlets, and you can replace or extend it from `openbb.toml`.

The namespace also hosts `company`, a provider-backed command for news about specific tickers, served by whichever installed providers implement it.

## Installation

```sh
pip install openbb-news
openbb-build
```

The package depends on `openbb-core[pandas]`, `feedparser`, and `lxml`.

## Commands

| Command | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `obb.news.rss(outlet=None, source=None, limit=20, fetch_body=True)` | Articles from one feed, newest first |
| `obb.news.rss_providers()` | A list of `{"label", "value"}` pairs, one per active outlet |
| `obb.news.rss_feeds(outlet=None)` | A list of `{"label", "value"}` pairs, one per feed in the outlet |
| `obb.news.company(symbol, start_date, end_date, limit, provider)` | Company news from `nasdaq` or `tmx` |

The feed commands have no `provider` argument and need no credentials. The word "provider" in `rss_providers` and in the `[news.rss_providers]` configuration table refers to a news outlet, not to an OpenBB data provider.

## Reading a feed

`source` selects a feed by its key. `outlet` selects an outlet and, when `source` is omitted, reads that outlet's default feed.

```python
from openbb import obb

markets = obb.news.rss(outlet="benzinga")
yahoo = obb.news.rss(source="yahoo_finance", limit=10, fetch_body=False)

yahoo.to_df()
```

Each result has six fields: `title`, `date` (ISO 8601, UTC), `author` (the entry's author, or the feed's title when the entry has none), `url`, `excerpt` (plain text, cut at a word boundary near 280 characters), and `body`.

With `fetch_body=True`, the default, the command requests every article URL concurrently and extracts the body from the page's JSON-LD `articleBody`, or from the largest `<article>` or `<main>` element after removing navigation, headers, footers, scripts, and forms. The body is Markdown with inline images. When a page is paywalled or yields fewer than two paragraphs, the body falls back to the feed's own summary followed by a link to the source. Set `fetch_body=False` to skip the per-article page requests; the body is then the feed summary and source link.

A feed that cannot be reached, or that returns an HTTP error, produces an empty result rather than an exception. Calling `rss()` with neither `outlet` nor `source` also returns an empty result. An unknown `source` key raises an error that lists every valid key.

To find keys, list the outlets and then the feeds within one:

```python
from openbb import obb

outlets = obb.news.rss_providers()
feeds = obb.news.rss_feeds(outlet="globenewswire")
```

Both return the active set, so feeds added in `openbb.toml` appear in them.

## Bundled outlets

| Outlet | Label | Default feed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axios` | Axios | `axios_main` |
| `bbc` | BBC | `bbc_world` |
| `benzinga` | Benzinga | `benzinga_markets` |
| `brutalist_business` | Brutalist — Business | `brutalist_business_fortune` |
| `brutalist_culture` | Brutalist — Culture | `brutalist_culture_vox` |
| `brutalist_gaming` | Brutalist — Gaming | `brutalist_gaming_polygon` |
| `brutalist_news` | Brutalist — News | `brutalist_news_guardian` |
| `brutalist_politics` | Brutalist — Politics | `brutalist_politics_axios` |
| `brutalist_science` | Brutalist — Science | `brutalist_science_scientificamerican` |
| `brutalist_sports` | Brutalist — Sports | `brutalist_sports_yahoosports` |
| `brutalist_tech` | Brutalist — Tech | `brutalist_tech_verge` |
| `cbc` | CBC | `cbc_business` |
| `drudge_report` | Drudge Report | `drudge_report` |
| `drugs_com` | Drugs.com | `drugs_com_medical_news` |
| `fortune` | Fortune | `fortune` |
| `fox_news` | Fox News | `fox_news_latest` |
| `globenewswire` | GlobeNewswire | `globenewswire_all` |
| `google_news` | Google News | `google_news_us` |
| `pr_newswire` | PR Newswire | `pr_newswire_global` |
| `wired` | Wired | `wired_business` |
| `yahoo_finance` | Yahoo Finance | `yahoo_finance` |

Most of the 562 feeds come from two press-release services. GlobeNewswire contributes one feed per ICB industry and one per subject code, such as earnings releases, dividends, and mergers and acquisitions. PR Newswire contributes a global feed and feeds for eight regional editions, each also split by industry category. The eight `brutalist_*` outlets group the publishers aggregated by brutalist.report under its topics.

## Configuring feeds in openbb.toml

The feed registry reads the `[news]` table from the layered OpenBB configuration. The table can live in any of these files, and later files override earlier ones key by key:

1. `[tool.openbb.news]` in the `pyproject.toml` of the working directory or its nearest parent that has one
2. `~/.openbb_platform/openbb.toml`
3. `openbb.toml` or `.openbb.toml` in the working directory or the nearest parent that has one
4. The file named by the `OPENBB_CONFIG` environment variable

The configuration is read on every call to `rss`, `rss_providers`, and `rss_feeds`, so edits take effect on the next request without restarting Python or the API server. The [openbb.toml](../user-guide/openbb-toml.mdx) page describes the rest of the file.

### Adding feeds

`[news.rss_feeds]` maps a feed key to a URL. In the short form, the value is the URL string; the feed is placed in an outlet named `custom`, and its label is the key with underscores replaced by spaces and title-cased.

```toml
[news.rss_feeds]
internal_research = "https://research.example.com/feed.xml"
team_blog = "https://blog.example.com/atom.xml"
```

The table form sets the outlet and label explicitly. Feeds that share an outlet value are grouped together in `rss_feeds` and in the Workspace widget. An entry without a `url` is ignored.

```toml
[news.rss_feeds.alpha_notes]
url = "https://alpha.example.com/rss"
provider = "acme_research"
label = "Alpha Notes"

[news.rss_feeds.beta_notes]
url = "https://beta.example.com/rss"
provider = "acme_research"
label = "Beta Notes"
```

### Keeping the bundled feeds

When `[news.rss_feeds]` contains any entries, it replaces the 562 bundled feeds. Set `merge_defaults = true` to keep them and add yours on top. A key that matches a bundled key replaces that feed's URL.

```toml
[news]
merge_defaults = true

[news.rss_feeds]
internal_research = "https://research.example.com/feed.xml"
```

Without `merge_defaults`, only the configured outlets exist, and `rss(outlet="benzinga")` returns an empty result because the outlet has no feeds.

### Naming outlets

An outlet's display label defaults to its id, humanized: `acme_research` becomes "Acme Research". `[news.rss_providers]` sets the label explicitly, for your own outlets or for bundled ones.

```toml
[news.rss_providers]
acme_research = "ACME Research Desk"
benzinga = "Benzinga Wire"
```

A complete configuration that keeps the bundled feeds and adds a two-feed outlet:

```toml
[news]
merge_defaults = true

[news.rss_providers]
acme_research = "ACME Research Desk"

[news.rss_feeds.alpha_notes]
url = "https://alpha.example.com/rss"
provider = "acme_research"
label = "Alpha Notes"

[news.rss_feeds.beta_notes]
url = "https://beta.example.com/rss"
provider = "acme_research"
label = "Beta Notes"
```

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.news.rss(outlet="acme_research", fetch_body=False)
obb.news.rss(source="beta_notes")
```

The first call reads `alpha_notes`, the first feed of the outlet in label order, because configured outlets have no preset default feed.

## Company news

`obb.news.company` is a standard provider-backed command. In V5 the `nasdaq` and `tmx` providers implement it, so it appears once either package is installed. Both accept several comma-separated symbols, and TMX adds a `page` parameter for paging through results.

```python
from openbb import obb

aapl = obb.news.company(symbol="AAPL", limit=10, provider="nasdaq")
air_canada = obb.news.company(symbol="AC", provider="tmx")
```

Both return `date`, `title`, `author`, `excerpt`, `body`, `images`, `url`, and `symbols`. Nasdaq adds `publisher` and `topic`; TMX adds `source`.

When `openbb-news` is not installed, the two providers register the same command in their own namespaces instead, as `obb.nasdaq.news.company` and `obb.tmx.news.company`.

## REST API and Workspace

Under [`openbb-api`](./interface/openbb-api.mdx), the feed commands are `GET` endpoints:

```sh
curl "http://127.0.0.1:6900/api/v1/news/rss?source=yahoo_finance&limit=5&fetch_body=false"
```

The `rss` endpoint is also exposed to OpenBB Workspace as the "RSS News Feed" newsfeed widget in the News category. Its Provider dropdown lists the outlets from `rss_providers`, its Feed dropdown lists the feeds from `rss_feeds` for the selected outlet, and it opens on Benzinga's Markets feed. Because both dropdowns call the configuration-aware endpoints, feeds added in `openbb.toml` appear in the widget.

See the [reference](/odp/python/reference/news) for every parameter.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 MD037 -->

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Providers | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

A provider package connects one data source to OpenBB. In V5 each package registers two entry points: a provider, which is the value passed as `provider=`, and a router, which becomes a namespace on `obb` and a path prefix on the REST API. Commands live in the namespace of the package that serves them, so `pip install openbb-fred` adds `obb.fred` and nothing else.

```python
from openbb import obb

spy = obb.cboe.equity.historical(symbol="SPY", start_date="2024-01-01")
factors = obb.famafrench.factors(frequency="daily", start_date="2024-01-01")
```

Each package installs independently and can be removed without affecting the others. After installing or removing one, run `openbb-build` or restart the Python session so the `obb` client is regenerated.

:::important
OpenBB does not host or serve data. Provider packages are connectors to public or third-party services, and coverage, rate limits, and terms of use are set by those services. Report connector bugs on [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/issues/new/choose).
:::

## Available providers

| Package | Namespace | `provider=` | Source | Credentials |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openbb-bls` | `obb.bls` | `bls` | [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/developers/) | `bls_api_key`, optional |
| `openbb-cboe` | `obb.cboe` | `cboe` | [Cboe](https://www.cboe.com) delayed equity, index, futures, and options data | None |
| `openbb-cftc` | `obb.cftc` | `cftc` | [CFTC](https://cftc.gov/) Commitments of Traders and DTCC swap data | `cftc_app_token`, optional |
| `openbb-deribit` | `obb.deribit` | `deribit` | [Deribit](https://deribit.com/) public crypto derivatives market data | None |
| `openbb-ecb` | `obb.ecb` | `ecb` | [European Central Bank Data Portal](https://data.ecb.europa.eu) | None |
| `openbb-us-eia` | `obb.eia` | `eia` | [U.S. Energy Information Administration](https://www.eia.gov/opendata/) | `eia_api_key` |
| `openbb-famafrench` | `obb.famafrench` | `famafrench` | [Kenneth French Data Library](https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html) | None |
| `openbb-federal-reserve` | `obb.federal_reserve` | `federal_reserve` | [Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/data.htm) Board, FOMC, and regional banks | None |
| `openbb-finra` | `obb.finra` | `finra` | [FINRA](https://www.finra.org/finra-data) | None |
| `openbb-fred` | `obb.fred` | `fred` | [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org), Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis | `fred_api_key` |
| `openbb-government-us` | `obb.uscongress`, `obb.ustreasury`, `obb.usda` | `congress_gov`, `us_treasury`, `usda` | [GovInfo](https://www.govinfo.gov) and Congress.gov, [U.S. Treasury](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov), [USDA](https://www.usda.gov) | `congress_gov_api_key`, optional |
| `openbb-imf` | `obb.imf` | `imf` | [International Monetary Fund](https://data.imf.org) | None |
| `openbb-jodi` | `obb.jodi` | `jodi` | [JODI](https://www.jodidata.org) Oil and Gas World Databases | None |
| `openbb-nasdaq` | `obb.nasdaq` | `nasdaq` | [Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com) public website data, US, Nordic, and Baltic markets | None |
| `openbb-oecd` | `obb.oecd` | `oecd` | [OECD Data Explorer](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/) | None |
| `openbb-sec` | `obb.sec` | `sec` | [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/data) EDGAR | None |
| `openbb-tmx` | `obb.tmx` | `tmx` | [TMX](https://www.tmx.com) Canadian markets data, unofficial | None |

Install any of them by package name:

```sh
pip install openbb-fred openbb-cboe
```

`openbb-government-us` is the only package that registers more than one provider. Its three agencies each get their own namespace and `provider=` value.

The generated [API reference](/odp/python/reference) documents every command, parameter, and returned field for these namespaces.

## Credentials

Credential names follow the pattern `<provider>_<credential>`. Five are defined, and only two are required for the commands that use them.

`fred_api_key` is required by the FRED commands. Request a free key from your account page at [fred.stlouisfed.org](https://fred.stlouisfed.org).

`eia_api_key` is required by the EIA commands that call the EIA API. Register for a free key at [eia.gov/opendata/register.php](https://www.eia.gov/opendata/register.php).

`bls_api_key` is optional. The BLS API accepts 25 series and 10 years per request without a key, and 50 series and 20 years with one; `obb.bls.series` splits larger queries into as many requests as the limits require. Register at [data.bls.gov/registrationEngine](https://data.bls.gov/registrationEngine/).

`cftc_app_token` is optional. Commitments of Traders requests made without a token may be throttled by IP address, and the DTCC swap endpoints never need one. Create a Socrata account, then generate the token from the CFTC Public Reporting developer settings.

`congress_gov_api_key` is needed only for requests about Congresses before the 108th (2003). Later Congresses are read from keyless GovInfo bulk data. Sign up at [api.congress.gov/sign-up](https://api.congress.gov/sign-up/).

Set a credential for the current session:

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.user.credentials.fred_api_key = "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
```

To keep a credential across sessions, store it under `credentials` in `~/.openbb_platform/user_settings.json`, or export an environment variable with the credential's name in upper case, such as `FRED_API_KEY`. The [credentials](../../user-guide/credentials.mdx) page covers these methods and the `openbb.toml` options.

## Provider coverage

The installed providers, and the commands each one serves, are available from the Python client:

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.coverage.providers
```

The result is a dictionary keyed by provider name. When a command is missing from `obb`, its package is usually not installed, or the client has not been rebuilt since installation.

## Providers removed in V5

These V4 provider packages are not part of V5: `openbb-alpha-vantage`, `openbb-benzinga`, `openbb-biztoc`, `openbb-econdb`, `openbb-finviz`, `openbb-fmp`, `openbb-intrinio`, `openbb-multpl`, `openbb-seeking-alpha`, `openbb-stockgrid`, `openbb-tiingo`, `openbb-tradier`, `openbb-tradingeconomics`, `openbb-wsj`, and `openbb-yfinance`. Their last V4 releases require `openbb-core` 1.x, so they cannot be installed alongside `openbb-core` 2.

`openbb-congress-gov` was merged into `openbb-government-us`. Its data is now served under `obb.uscongress` with `provider="congress_gov"`.

The shared routers that V4 providers fed into, such as `obb.equity`, `obb.economy`, and `obb.fixedincome`, are not installed with the V5 provider packages and are not covered by this documentation. Code written against them should move to the provider namespaces. The [migration guide](../../migration-from-v4.mdx) lists the changes.

## Building a provider

Anyone can publish a provider package. The [provider extension](../../developer/extension_types/provider.md) guide walks through the `Provider` and `Fetcher` classes and the entry points a package needs. Search [PyPI](https://pypi.org/search/?q=openbb-) for community packages.

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="Data Providers FAQ | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Which data sources are available?</summary>

V5 has seventeen provider packages, covering U.S. and international statistical agencies, central banks, regulators, and several exchanges. Each installs its own namespace, such as `obb.fred`, `obb.sec`, or `obb.cboe`. The [providers](../extensions/providers/index.mdx) page lists every package with its namespace and credentials, and the [API reference](/odp/python/reference) documents every command.

If the data you need is not covered, send a [feature request](https://openbb.co/request-a-feature) describing the use case.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Where did obb.equity, obb.economy, and the other shared namespaces go?</summary>

V5 provider packages do not feed shared asset-class routers. Every command lives in the namespace of the provider package that serves it, so equity price history from Cboe is `obb.cboe.equity.historical` and from Nasdaq is `obb.nasdaq.equity.historical`. Code written for V4 needs to move to the provider namespaces; the [migration guide](../migration-from-v4.mdx) lists the changes.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">What happened to yfinance, FMP, Intrinio, and the other V4 providers?</summary>

They were removed from V5: `openbb-alpha-vantage`, `openbb-benzinga`, `openbb-biztoc`, `openbb-econdb`, `openbb-finviz`, `openbb-fmp`, `openbb-intrinio`, `openbb-multpl`, `openbb-seeking-alpha`, `openbb-stockgrid`, `openbb-tiingo`, `openbb-tradier`, `openbb-tradingeconomics`, `openbb-wsj`, and `openbb-yfinance`. Their last releases require `openbb-core` 1.x and cannot be installed with V5. `openbb-congress-gov` was merged into `openbb-government-us`, whose Congress data is under `obb.uscongress`.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Which providers need an API key?</summary>

Only FRED and the EIA require one: set `fred_api_key` and `eia_api_key`. Three others take an optional credential. `bls_api_key` raises the BLS API's per-request limits, `cftc_app_token` avoids throttling on Commitments of Traders requests, and `congress_gov_api_key` is needed only for Congresses before the 108th. Every other provider is keyless.

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.user.credentials.fred_api_key = "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
```

The [credentials](../user-guide/credentials.mdx) page covers storing keys between sessions.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">A namespace or command is missing from obb.</summary>

Namespaces and commands come from the installed packages. If `openbb-technical` is not installed, `obb.technical` does not exist; if `openbb-cboe` is not installed, neither does `obb.cboe`. Install the package by name, then rebuild the Python client:

```sh
pip install openbb-cboe
openbb-build
```

Importing `openbb` also rebuilds automatically when it detects that extensions were added or removed, but an already running Python session must be restarted to pick up the change.

To see what the environment serves, list the installed providers and their commands:

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.coverage.providers
```

A few commands depend on a second package. `obb.news.company`, for example, appears only when `openbb-news` and at least one of `openbb-nasdaq` or `openbb-tmx` are installed.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Why doesn't the returned data match the start and end dates I requested?</summary>

A provider returns what its source publishes. The source may not have data for the whole period, may publish with a delay, or may limit how far back a given interval goes. For example, `obb.cboe.equity.historical(symbol="SPY", interval="1m")` returns one-minute bars for the most recent trading day only.

If a result looks wrong for a technical reason, search the [GitHub issues](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/issues/new/choose) and open one if it is not already reported. Include the command, its parameters, the installed package versions, and the full error message.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">How do I get data for listings outside the U.S.?</summary>

Coverage depends on the provider. `openbb-tmx` serves Canadian listings under `obb.tmx`, and `openbb-nasdaq` serves Nasdaq Nordic and Baltic markets under `obb.nasdaq.nordic`. Symbol conventions differ by source, so look a symbol up with the provider's own search before requesting data:

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.tmx.equity.search(query="royal bank")
obb.tmx.equity.historical(symbol="RY", start_date="2024-01-01")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">How can I request a data provider or function?</summary>

Please [request a feature](https://openbb.co/request-a-feature) and describe your use case.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Can I contribute my own data provider extension?</summary>

Yes. A provider is a Python package that registers a `Provider` and a router through entry points. The [provider extension](../developer/extension_types/provider.md) guide covers the structure, and the [developer quickstart](../quickstart/developer.mdx) walks through a first package.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Can my company become a data partner?</summary>

Yes. Visit the [data vendors](https://openbb.co/use-cases/data-vendors) page and fill out the form.

</details>

title: Errors
sidebar_position: 3

keywords:

  - EmptyDataError
  - UnauthorizedError

  - debug mode
  - openbb-build
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Errors FAQ | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

The Python interface condenses exceptions into a short message that starts with `[Error] ->`, `[Empty] ->`, or `[Unexpected Error] ->`. Set `OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE=true` to see the full traceback instead. The REST API maps the same exceptions to the HTTP status codes listed below.

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">[Arg] provider -> input: cboe -> Input should be 'nasdaq' or 'tmx'</summary>

The value passed as `provider` is not one of the providers installed for that command.

The provider package may not be installed. Install it and import `openbb` again.

The package may be installed while the `openbb` package has not been rebuilt. With `OPENBB_AUTO_BUILD` at its default of `true`, importing `openbb` rebuilds when the installed extensions change. If that did not happen, rebuild from the command line with the environment active:

```bash
openbb-build
```

The provider may not cover the command. The command's docstring lists its providers under the `provider` parameter, and `obb.reference` returns the same information:

```python
from openbb import obb

[p for p in obb.reference["paths"]["/news/company"]["parameters"] if p != "standard"]
```

```console
['nasdaq', 'tmx']
```

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'equity'</summary>

The V5 provider packages do not install the shared asset-class namespaces from V4, such as `obb.equity`, `obb.economy`, and `obb.fixedincome`. Each provider package owns its own namespace, for example `obb.fred`, `obb.sec`, or `obb.nasdaq`. [Migration from V4](../migration-from-v4.mdx) lists the changes.

For a V5 namespace, the error means the extension that provides it is not installed, or it is installed and the `openbb` package has not been rebuilt. Install the extension and run `openbb-build` if importing `openbb` did not rebuild it.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Missing credential 'fred_api_key'</summary>

The endpoint needs a provider credential that is not set. Add it to `~/.openbb_platform/user_settings.json`, set the matching environment variable (`FRED_API_KEY`), or assign it for the current session:

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.user.credentials.fred_api_key = "your-fred-key"
```

A related message, `Provider fallback failed.`, appears when a command is called without `provider` and none of the providers in its priority list has all of its credentials set. Each provider is listed with the reason it was skipped: `missing credentials` or `not installed`. Pass `provider` explicitly or set the missing credentials.

[Settings & Configuration](../settings/index.mdx#credentials) lists the credential names that V5 providers use.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">json.decoder.JSONDecodeError when importing openbb</summary>

`user_settings.json` or `system_settings.json` in `~/.openbb_platform/` is not valid JSON. Trailing commas and comments are the usual cause. Fix the file, or remove it to have a default one created on the next import.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">RuntimeError: OBBject Extension Error</summary>

An installed OBBject extension runs on command output, and running it has not been permitted. Extensions that only read the output need `allow_on_command_output`; extensions that modify it also need `allow_mutable_extensions`. Set them in `~/.openbb_platform/system_settings.json`:

```json
{
  "allow_on_command_output": true,
  "allow_mutable_extensions": true
}
```

The environment variables `OPENBB_ALLOW_ON_COMMAND_OUTPUT` and `OPENBB_ALLOW_MUTABLE_EXTENSIONS` set the same values. Enable them only for extensions installed from a trusted source.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Unauthorized (UnauthorizedError) - HTTP status 502</summary>

The provider rejected the credentials that were sent. The default message reads `Unauthorized <provider> API request. Please check your <provider> credentials and subscription access.`

Verify the credential value, its access level, and the subscription status directly with the provider.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Bad Request (OpenBBError) - HTTP status 400</summary>

A handled error raised by openbb-core or a provider, such as a missing credential. The message after `[Error] ->` in Python, or the `detail` field of the API response, states the cause.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Unprocessable Entity - HTTP status 422</summary>

Parameter validation failed: a required parameter is missing, or a value has the wrong type or is not an allowed choice. In Python, the message starts with the number of errors and lists each one on an `[Arg]` line with the parameter name, the input, and the reason.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">No Content (EmptyDataError) - HTTP status 204</summary>

The request succeeded but returned no data. The Python message defaults to `[Empty] -> No results found. Try adjusting the query parameters.`, and the API responds with status 204 and an empty body.

Widen the query, for example with a longer date range or fewer filters. If every combination of parameters returns nothing, open a bug report on [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/issues/new?assignees=&labels=type%3Abug&projects=&template=bug_report.md&title=%5BBug%5D) with the operating system and version, the Python version, and the code that produced the error.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Unexpected Error - HTTP status 500</summary>

An exception that openbb-core does not handle. The Python message has the form `[Unexpected Error] -> <ExceptionClass> -> <message>`, and the API returns `Unexpected Error -> <ExceptionClass> -> <message>` in `detail`. Set debug mode, described below, and run the code again to get the full traceback.

If the traceback points to OpenBB code, open a bug report on [GitHub](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/issues/new?assignees=&labels=type%3Abug&projects=&template=bug_report.md&title=%5BBug%5D) with the traceback, the operating system and version, the Python version, and the code that produced the error.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">How do I start in debug mode?</summary>

Debug mode is controlled by the `OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE` environment variable. To enable it permanently, add it to `~/.openbb_platform/.env`:

```env
OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE=true
```

To enable it for one session, set it before importing `openbb`:

```python
import os

os.environ["OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE"] = "true"

from openbb import obb
```

With debug mode on, Python raises the original exception with its full traceback, and the REST API re-raises it so the traceback appears in the server log. For `openbb-api` and `openbb-mcp`, `debug-mode = true` in `openbb.toml` has the same effect. The `debug_mode` key in `system_settings.json` only affects openbb-charting and does not enable full tracebacks.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">"Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required"</summary>

A dependency is being compiled from source on Windows. Download and install [Microsoft C++ Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/), restart the machine, then run the installation again.

<div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center'}}>
  <img
    alt="Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer, first screen"
    src="https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBBTerminal/assets/85772166/ceb57be0-6dae-42f2-aca6-bf62ce7d6135"
    width="80%"
  />
</div>

<div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center'}}>
  <img
    alt="Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer, workload selection"
    src="https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBBTerminal/assets/85772166/f8aef8fc-a080-4164-bd36-460714ec44f3"
    width="80%"
  />
</div>

</details>

<HeadTitle title="License FAQ | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">How is ODP V5 licensed?</summary>

Every file in the OpenBB repository, and every package published from it for V5, is licensed under the [Apache License, Version 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). That includes `openbb-core`, the provider and extension packages, `openbb-platform-api`, `openbb-mcp-server`, `openbb-cli`, and ODP Desktop. The full text is in the [LICENSE](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/blob/develop/LICENSE) file of the repository, and the text of the license governs where it differs from this summary.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">What changed from V4?</summary>

V4 and earlier releases were licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0-only). V5 changes the license to Apache-2.0 (OpenBB-finance/OpenBB#7677). Releases made under the AGPL keep that license; the V4 licensing FAQ remains in the [V4 documentation](/odp/v4/python/faqs/license).

The REST API reports the new license as well: the default `license_name` in the OpenAPI document served by `openbb-core` is `Apache-2.0`.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Can I use ODP in a commercial or proprietary product?</summary>

Yes. Apache-2.0 permits use, modification, and redistribution, including in closed-source products and hosted services, without a separate commercial license and without publishing your changes. When you redistribute ODP or a modified version of it, include a copy of the license, keep the existing copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices, mark the files you changed, and carry over the contents of any `NOTICE` file. The license also grants a patent license from each contributor and does not grant rights to the OpenBB trademarks.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Do my extensions have to use the same license?</summary>

No. An extension that registers through the ODP entry points is your own package and can use any license, including a proprietary one. The same applies to FastAPI apps served with `openbb-api` and to projects generated with `openbb --generate-extension`.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Does the license cover the data returned by providers?</summary>

No. The license covers the software. Provider packages connect to public or third-party services, and the data they return is subject to each source's own terms of use, which may restrict storage, redistribution, or commercial use. Check those terms before redistributing data.

</details>

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Who can I contact about licensing?</summary>

Send questions to [licensing@openbb.co](mailto:licensing@openbb.co).

</details>

<HeadTitle title="OpenBB Python (V5) | OpenBB Docs" />

OpenBB Python is a set of packages built on `openbb-core`. Each provider package connects one data source and adds its own namespace, such as `obb.fred`, `obb.sec`, or `obb.cboe`. The same installed commands are available from Python with `from openbb import obb`, as a REST API, as MCP tools, and as OpenBB Workspace widgets, and extensions you write yourself plug into all of them the same way.

:::important
V5 is a breaking release. Commands move from shared routers such as `obb.equity` into provider namespaces, fifteen V4 provider packages are removed, and the license changes from AGPL-3.0 to Apache-2.0. [Migration from V4](./migration-from-v4.mdx) lists every change. The V4 documentation remains available under [/odp/v4/python](/odp/v4/python).
:::

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Installation | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

OpenBB Python V5 is a set of separately published packages. `openbb-core` is the runtime: it contains the `openbb` import package, the REST API app, and the `openbb-build` command, but no data. Each provider package adds a data source and its own namespace on `obb`. The `openbb` distribution installs the runtime with every provider and interface package, or you can install the runtime with only the providers you want. Either way, the `openbb` import package is generated from whatever is installed.

## Requirements

Every V5 package declares `requires-python = ">=3.10,<4"`. CI runs the core test suite on Python 3.10 through 3.14 on Linux, and on 3.10 and 3.14 on macOS and Windows.

Install into a virtual environment rather than the system Python. Any environment manager works; the commands below use the standard library `venv` module.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
```

On Windows, activate with `.venv\Scripts\activate`.

For a graphical installer that manages the environment for you, see [ODP Desktop](../desktop/installation.md).

## Install from PyPI

`pip install openbb` installs V5:

```bash
pip install openbb
```

The `openbb` package contains no code of its own. It installs `openbb-core` with its `flask` and `pandas` extras, every provider package in the [package reference](#package-reference), `openbb-news`, `openbb-charting` with PyWry, `openbb-cli`, `openbb-platform-api`, `openbb-mcp-server`, and `openbb-devtools`. It does not install `openbb-econometrics`, `openbb-quantitative`, or `openbb-technical`; add those separately:

```bash
pip install openbb-econometrics openbb-quantitative openbb-technical
```

The `routers` extra, `pip install "openbb[routers]"`, installs those three together with the shared asset-class routers such as `openbb-equity` and `openbb-economy`. This documentation does not cover the shared routers, and several providers leave commands to them when they are installed, so the provider namespaces lose commands that the [reference](/odp/python/reference) lists. [Migrating from V4](migration-from-v4.mdx#provider-owned-namespaces) explains the interaction.

### Install individual packages

For a smaller environment, install `openbb-core` with only the provider packages you need:

```bash
pip install openbb-core openbb-cboe openbb-imf
```

Every provider package depends on `openbb-core[pandas]`, so installing a provider on its own also pulls in the runtime and pandas. Add or remove providers later with `pip`; the Python interface picks up the change on the next import.

Check the installation with a keyless provider:

```python
from openbb import obb

quote = obb.cboe.equity.quote(symbol="AAPL", provider="cboe")
quote.to_dataframe()
```

### Package reference

| Package | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| `openbb-core` | Runtime, the `openbb` import package, `openbb_core.api.rest_api:app`, and `openbb-build` |
| `openbb-bls` | `obb.bls` |
| `openbb-cboe` | `obb.cboe` |
| `openbb-cftc` | `obb.cftc` |
| `openbb-deribit` | `obb.deribit` |
| `openbb-ecb` | `obb.ecb` |
| `openbb-us-eia` | `obb.eia` |
| `openbb-famafrench` | `obb.famafrench` |
| `openbb-federal-reserve` | `obb.federal_reserve` |
| `openbb-finra` | `obb.finra` |
| `openbb-fred` | `obb.fred` |
| `openbb-government-us` | `obb.uscongress`, `obb.ustreasury`, `obb.usda` |
| `openbb-imf` | `obb.imf` |
| `openbb-jodi` | `obb.jodi` |
| `openbb-nasdaq` | `obb.nasdaq` |
| `openbb-oecd` | `obb.oecd` |
| `openbb-sec` | `obb.sec` |
| `openbb-tmx` | `obb.tmx` |
| `openbb-news` | `obb.news` |
| `openbb-econometrics` | `obb.econometrics` |
| `openbb-quantitative` | `obb.quantitative` |
| `openbb-technical` | `obb.technical` |
| `openbb-charting` | The `charting` accessor on command results; the `pywry` extra adds native chart windows |
| `openbb-platform-api` | The `openbb-api` launcher for the REST API and OpenBB Workspace |
| `openbb-mcp-server` | The `openbb-mcp` MCP server; the `cli` extra adds the `openbb-cli` dispatcher tools |
| `openbb-cli` | The `openbb` command line interface |

Some providers need an API key before their commands return data. See [Credentials](user-guide/credentials.mdx) for where to put them, and [Providers](extensions/providers/index.mdx) for what each provider covers. The CLI has its own [installation guide](../cli/installation.md).

### Upgrading from V4

Install V5 into a new virtual environment instead of upgrading a V4 one. The V4 releases of providers that V5 removed, such as `openbb-fmp` and `openbb-yfinance`, require `openbb-core` 1.x and cannot be installed next to V5. [Migrating from V4](migration-from-v4.mdx) lists the other changes to expect.

## Build the Python interface

`from openbb import obb` is backed by modules generated inside the installed `openbb` package. On import, the runtime compares the installed extensions with the ones recorded at the last build and rebuilds when they differ, printing `Extensions to add` or `Extensions to remove` followed by `Building...`.

To build ahead of time, for example in a container image or CI job, run:

```bash
openbb-build
```

`openbb-build` imports `openbb` in a subprocess, and calls `openbb.build()` directly if that import did not rebuild. Set `OPENBB_AUTO_BUILD=false` to turn off the rebuild on import. [Packaging and static assets](concepts/packaging.mdx) describes what the build generates.

## Install from source

The source install puts every package from the repository into the active environment in editable mode. V5 is on the repository's default branch, `develop`. The install needs Git, Python 3.10 or newer, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). `dev_install.py` uses the `uv` module of the running interpreter when it is installed, and the `uv` executable on `PATH` otherwise.

Five providers, `openbb-bls`, `openbb-ecb`, `openbb-imf`, `openbb-oecd`, and `openbb-us-eia`, generate metadata files from their upstream APIs when they are built, and the generators import `openbb-core`. Those files are not tracked in Git, so on a fresh clone `openbb-core` has to be installed first and uv's build isolation turned off. The EIA catalog also needs an EIA API key in `EIA_API_KEY`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB.git
cd OpenBB
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install uv
python -m uv pip install "hatchling>=1.25" "requests>=2.31" editables
python -m uv pip install --editable "openbb_platform/core[pandas]"
export EIA_API_KEY="YOUR_EIA_KEY"
UV_NO_BUILD_ISOLATION=true python openbb_platform/dev_install.py
```

The first build downloads the provider metadata and can take a long time. Later builds reuse the generated files.

The script lists the tracked `pyproject.toml` files under `openbb_platform/core`, `openbb_platform/extensions`, `openbb_platform/obbject_extensions`, `openbb_platform/providers`, and `cli`, then runs `uv pip install` against the interpreter that launched it with each package as `--editable`, including all optional extras and each package's `dev` dependency group. It finishes by building the `openbb` package, so no separate `openbb-build` is needed. Because packages are found with `git ls-files`, a new package directory is picked up only once its `pyproject.toml` is tracked by Git.

Router extensions under `openbb_platform/extensions`, other than `openbb-news`, are skipped by default. Without them, the environment contains `openbb-core`, `openbb-news`, every provider, `openbb-charting`, `openbb-platform-api`, `openbb-mcp-server`, `openbb-devtools`, and `openbb-cli`.

The skipped routers include `openbb-econometrics`, `openbb-quantitative`, and `openbb-technical`. Install those three as editable packages from the same checkout:

```bash
python -m pip install -e openbb_platform/extensions/econometrics -e openbb_platform/extensions/quantitative -e openbb_platform/extensions/technical
openbb-build
```

`dev_install.py --routers` installs every router instead, including the shared asset-class routers such as `openbb-equity` and `openbb-economy`. Those are not covered by this documentation, and several providers leave commands to them when they are installed, so the provider namespaces lose commands that the [reference](/odp/python/reference) lists. [Migrating from V4](migration-from-v4.mdx#provider-owned-namespaces) explains the interaction.

## Next steps

Start with the [User Quickstart](quickstart/user.mdx) to make your first queries, or the [Developer Quickstart](quickstart/developer.mdx) to build an extension. To serve the installed commands over HTTP or MCP, see the [REST API](quickstart/rest_api.mdx) and [MCP server](quickstart/mcp.mdx) quickstarts.
