import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Migration from V4 | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

V5 is a breaking release. `openbb-core` moves to 2.0.0, most command paths change, fifteen provider packages are gone, and packaging, the CLI, and the REST API all behave differently. This page walks through what a V4 user has to change. The V4 documentation stays available at [/odp/v4/python](/odp/v4/python).

Install V5 into a new virtual environment instead of upgrading a V4 one in place. Shared router packages such as `openbb-economy` or `openbb-equity`, whether left over from V4 or installed with `dev_install.py --routers`, change which commands the V5 providers register, as explained under [provider-owned namespaces](#provider-owned-namespaces). The [installation guide](./installation.mdx) covers the setup.

## License

V4 packages were licensed AGPL-3.0-only. V5 relicenses the repository and every package in it under Apache-2.0 (OpenBB-finance/OpenBB#7677), and the `license_name` in the REST API's OpenAPI document now reads `Apache-2.0`. See the [license FAQ](./faqs/license.mdx).

## Removed providers and extensions

These provider packages were deleted from the repository and have no V5 counterpart: `openbb-alpha-vantage`, `openbb-benzinga`, `openbb-biztoc`, `openbb-econdb`, `openbb-finviz`, `openbb-fmp`, `openbb-intrinio`, `openbb-multpl`, `openbb-seeking-alpha`, `openbb-stockgrid`, `openbb-tiingo`, `openbb-tradier`, `openbb-tradingeconomics`, `openbb-wsj`, and `openbb-yfinance`. Code that passes one of their names as `provider=` has to move to a different source or be dropped.

Two packages were folded into others. `openbb-congress-gov` now ships inside `openbb-government-us` (#7604), which still registers `obb.uscongress`. The `openbb-regulators` extension is gone, and its `obb.regulators.sec.*` commands are registered by `openbb-sec` under `obb.sec.*`.

A command whose providers were all removed disappears with them. `obb.news.world` is the visible case: Benzinga, Biztoc, FMP, Intrinio, and Tiingo were its only V4 providers, so V5 does not generate it. `obb.news.company` remains, backed by `nasdaq` and `tmx`.

## Provider-owned namespaces

V4 put most data commands into shared asset-class routers such as `obb.equity`, `obb.economy`, `obb.fixedincome`, `obb.derivatives`, and `obb.commodity`, and picked the source with `provider=`. The V5 documentation does not cover those router packages. In V5 each provider package registers its own namespace and arranges its commands beneath it, so the source is part of the path and `provider=` is only needed when a command has more than one source.

| Namespace | Package |
| --- | --- |
| `obb.bls` | `openbb-bls` |
| `obb.cboe` | `openbb-cboe` |
| `obb.cftc` | `openbb-cftc` |
| `obb.deribit` | `openbb-deribit` |
| `obb.ecb` | `openbb-ecb` |
| `obb.eia` | `openbb-us-eia` |
| `obb.famafrench` | `openbb-famafrench` |
| `obb.federal_reserve` | `openbb-federal-reserve` |
| `obb.finra` | `openbb-finra` |
| `obb.fred` | `openbb-fred` |
| `obb.imf` | `openbb-imf` |
| `obb.jodi` | `openbb-jodi` |
| `obb.nasdaq` | `openbb-nasdaq` |
| `obb.oecd` | `openbb-oecd` |
| `obb.sec` | `openbb-sec` |
| `obb.tmx` | `openbb-tmx` |
| `obb.uscongress`, `obb.usda`, `obb.ustreasury` | `openbb-government-us` |
| `obb.news` | `openbb-news` |
| `obb.econometrics` | `openbb-econometrics` |
| `obb.quantitative` | `openbb-quantitative` |
| `obb.technical` | `openbb-technical` |

The calls below show the pattern. Arguments are elided because some parameters changed between versions; check each command's reference page before porting a call.

| V4 | V5 |
| --- | --- |
| `obb.economy.fred_series(..., provider="fred")` | `obb.fred.economy.fred_series(...)` |
| `obb.economy.cpi(..., provider="imf")` | `obb.imf.cpi(...)` |
| `obb.imf_utils.presentation_table(...)` | `obb.imf.presentation_table(...)` |
| `obb.equity.price.historical(..., provider="cboe")` | `obb.cboe.equity.historical(...)` |
| `obb.derivatives.options.chains(..., provider="cboe")` | `obb.cboe.options.chains(...)` |
| `obb.equity.fundamental.filings(..., provider="sec")` | `obb.sec.company_filings(...)` |
| `obb.regulators.sec.cik_map(...)` | `obb.sec.cik_map(...)` |
| `obb.fixedincome.government.treasury_auctions(..., provider="government_us")` | `obb.ustreasury.treasury_auctions(...)` |
| `obb.commodity.psd_data(..., provider="government_us")` | `obb.usda.psd_data(...)` |
| `obb.commodity.petroleum_status_report(..., provider="eia")` | `obb.eia.petroleum_status_report(...)` |

For everything else, browse the [Python reference](/odp/python/reference) by namespace. REST paths follow the same structure, so `/api/v1/economy/fred_series` becomes `/api/v1/fred/economy/fred_series`, and any client that calls the API by path needs updating.

Data model names change along with the paths. A command registered under a provider namespace uses a provider-prefixed model, so the V4 `ConsumerPriceIndex` model appears as `FredConsumerPriceIndex`, `ImfConsumerPriceIndex`, and `OecdConsumerPriceIndex` in the [data model reference](/odp/python/data_models/FredConsumerPriceIndex).

Several providers, `openbb-fred`, `openbb-cboe`, and `openbb-sec` among them, check at import time whether the matching shared router package (`openbb-economy`, `openbb-equity`, `openbb-derivatives`, and so on) is importable, whatever its version. When it is, the provider leaves those commands to the router and skips registering them under its own namespace. A shared router in the environment therefore hides commands that the reference lists under `obb.fred`, `obb.cboe`, or `obb.sec`. Start from a new environment, and leave out `--routers` when installing from source, to avoid the problem.

## Other renamed namespaces and commands

The IMF router was renamed. `obb.imf_utils.*` is now `obb.imf.*`, and the REST prefix `/api/v1/imf_utils/` is now `/api/v1/imf/`. IMF data that V4 served through the shared routers, such as `obb.economy.cpi(provider="imf")`, sits in the same namespace, and the PortWatch shipping data has its own group at `obb.imf.portwatch`.

V4's single `government_us` provider is split into three providers inside `openbb-government-us`: `us_treasury` behind `obb.ustreasury`, `usda` behind `obb.usda`, and `congress_gov` behind `obb.uscongress`. Replace every `provider="government_us"` argument. Congress data from the 108th Congress (2003) onward now comes from keyless GovInfo bulk files; only earlier Congresses fall back to the Congress.gov API and need `congress_gov_api_key`.

EIA commands that V4 placed in `obb.commodity`, `petroleum_status_report` and `short_term_energy_outlook`, now live in `obb.eia` next to the EIA API coverage added in V5. The package is still `openbb-us-eia` and the provider name is still `eia`. OECD had no namespace of its own in V4; its data came only through the shared routers. V5 adds `obb.oecd`.

`openbb-sec` keeps its HTTP responses in a single disk cache. The folder defaults to the `sec` subfolder of the `cache_directory` preference (`~/OpenBBUserData/cache/sec`); `OPENBB_SEC_CACHE_DIR` overrides it, and `OPENBB_SEC_CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT` caps its size (default 8 GB). The package installs an `openbb-sec` command that manages the cache and serves the provider as an OpenBB Workspace backend when run without a subcommand.

```bash
openbb-sec info
openbb-sec clear
```

Technical indicators return different rows. V4 appended the indicator columns to the input records and returned the combined frame. V5 returns typed rows with the date and the indicator's own fields only: `obb.technical.rsi` yields `date` and `rsi`, and `obb.technical.bbands` yields `date`, `lower`, `middle`, `upper`, `bandwidth`, and `percent`. Join the result back to your prices if you relied on the combined output. Parameter order also changed for some commands (V4 `rsi` took `target` before `index`, V5 reverses them), so pass arguments by keyword.

## Configuration: openbb.toml

V5 adds a TOML configuration file and a layered loader in `openbb-core` (#7492). The V4 files `~/.openbb_platform/user_settings.json` and `system_settings.json` keep working; they form the base that the TOML layers merge on top of. Later layers override earlier ones:

| Order | Source |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Model defaults |
| 2 | `~/.openbb_platform/system_settings.json` and `user_settings.json` |
| 3 | `[tool.openbb]` in the nearest `pyproject.toml`, searching upward from the working directory |
| 4 | `~/.openbb_platform/openbb.toml` or `.openbb.toml` |
| 5 | `openbb.toml` or `.openbb.toml` in the working directory or the nearest parent that has one |
| 6 | The file named by `OPENBB_CONFIG`, or by `--config-file` for `openbb-api` and `openbb-mcp` |

After the TOML layers, the loader reads `~/.openbb_platform/.env` and the file named by `OPENBB_ENV_FILE` into the environment. Neither the `.env` files nor the TOML ever overwrite a variable already exported in the shell.

`[system]` and `[user]` map onto the settings models, with `[user.credentials]`, `[user.preferences]`, and `[user.defaults]` under the latter. A few system flags can also be set at the top level in kebab case: `debug-mode`, `test-mode`, `headless`, `logging-suppress`, `allow-mutable-extensions`, and `allow-on-command-output`.

```toml
debug-mode = false

[user.credentials]
fred_api_key = "REPLACE_ME"

[user.preferences]
output_type = "dataframe"
```

Not every entry point applies the file. `openbb-api` and `openbb-mcp` run the loader at startup, before `openbb-core` is imported. `openbb-news` reads its `[news]` table, and `openbb-sec` consults the layers to resolve its cache folder. A Python session that runs `from openbb import obb` does not load `openbb.toml` on import; it reads the JSON settings files and `~/.openbb_platform/.env` as V4 did. The CLI has a loader of its own, described in the [CLI section](#cli). Full details are in the [openbb.toml guide](./user-guide/openbb-toml.mdx) and the [settings reference](./settings/index.mdx).

## Build and packaging

Every V5 package declares its metadata in the standard `[project]` table and builds with hatchling. The `[tool.poetry]` sections are gone, and each package directory carries its own `uv.lock`. Extension authors have to port their `pyproject.toml` the same way. Entry points move from Poetry plugin tables to `[project.entry-points]`, with unchanged group names. A V4 provider declared:

```toml
[tool.poetry.plugins."openbb_provider_extension"]
my_provider = "my_package:my_provider"

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"
```

The V5 equivalent:

```toml
[project.entry-points."openbb_provider_extension"]
my_provider = "my_package:my_provider"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

The `openbb-cookiecutter` template generates projects in this layout, depending on `openbb-core[pandas]>=2.0.0`. See [Packaging](./concepts/packaging.mdx) and [provider extensions](./developer/extension_types/provider.md).

pandas is no longer a hard dependency of `openbb-core`. It moved to the `pandas` extra, which every V5 provider package already requires. With `openbb-core` installed alone, `to_dataframe()` and `to_df()` raise an `OpenBBError` whose message includes the install command.

```bash
pip install "openbb-core[pandas]"
```

From a source checkout, `openbb_platform/dev_install.py` now uses uv instead of Poetry and fails if uv is not installed. Run it from an activated environment. It installs every package tracked under `openbb_platform/core`, `extensions`, `obbject_extensions`, `providers`, and `cli` in editable mode with all extras and each package's `dev` dependency group, then builds the `openbb` package. The V4 `-e`/`--extras` and `-c`/`--cli` switches are gone. Router extensions in `openbb_platform/extensions`, which include `openbb-technical`, `openbb-quantitative`, and `openbb-econometrics`, are installed only when you pass `--routers`; `openbb-news` is always installed. `--routers` also installs the shared asset-class routers described under [provider-owned namespaces](#provider-owned-namespaces), so install the three data-processing extensions on their own instead, as shown in the [installation guide](./installation.mdx#install-from-source).

`openbb-build` still regenerates the static `openbb` package after extensions are installed or removed.

## CLI

`openbb-cli` 2.0.0 changes what `openbb` does with no flags. In V4 it opened the interactive shell. In V5 it runs a single command in-process and exits: the command path is the dotted Python path under `obb`, parameters are `--key value` pairs, and the result is written to stdout as one JSON line with `ok`, `result`, and, on failure, `error`. The exit code is 0 on success and 1 when the command fails.

```bash
openbb sec.cik_map --symbol MSFT
```

Pass `-i` (`--interactive`) to get the V4-style shell. In that mode output defaults to Rich tables.

```bash
openbb -i
```

`--batch` reads newline-delimited JSON requests from stdin and writes one response line per request, running up to eight at a time (`--batch-concurrency` or `OPENBB_CLI_BATCH_CONCURRENCY` changes the limit).

```bash
echo '{"id": "1", "command": "sec.cik_map", "params": {"symbol": "MSFT"}}' | openbb --batch
```

The package no longer pulls in the whole platform. V4 `openbb-cli` depended on `openbb[all]`; V5 depends on `openbb-core[pandas]`, so install the provider packages you want to call next to it. The `charting`, `interactive`, and `all` extras add `openbb-charting` and PyWry.

The CLI can also work against other servers. `--server URL` (or `OPENBB_SERVER_URL`) dispatches commands to a running `openbb-api` instead of the in-process `obb`. `--generate-spec` reads the OpenAPI document from `--server` (`--openapi-path` points at a non-default location), or walks a Socrata story with `--socrata-story`, and writes a `.spec` file. `--spec [NAME=]PATH` runs commands from that file without fetching OpenAPI again; repeat it with `NAME=` to mount several specs under separate namespaces. `--list-commands` and `--describe COMMAND` print what a spec contains, and `--generate-extension` turns a spec into an installable OpenBB extension, with `--include` and `--exclude` glob filters on command names.

```bash
openbb --server https://api.example.com --generate-spec --output example.spec
openbb --spec example.spec --list-commands
openbb --spec example.spec --generate-extension --output ./openbb_example
```

`--generate-extension` prints the install and build commands for the generated project when it finishes.

CLI settings come from the same `openbb.toml` locations as `openbb-core`, but the CLI reads `[tool.openbb-cli]` from `pyproject.toml`, takes its explicit file from `--config` or `OPENBB_CLI_CONFIG`, and loads an extra `.env` from `--env-file` or `OPENBB_CLI_ENV_FILE`. Its keys include `server`, `spec`, `[specs.NAME]`, `[headers]`, `[query]`, and `[settings]`. `openbb --show-config` prints the merged result and `openbb --print-config-template` prints a commented template. See [CLI modes](../cli/modes.md), [code generation](../cli/codegen.md), and [CLI configuration](../cli/configuration.md).

## REST API

POST commands read all of their parameters from the JSON request body. In V4 a data-processing command such as `/api/v1/technical/rsi` took the `data` records in the body and its scalar options (`target`, `length`, and so on) from the query string. In V5 the body is one JSON object holding the records and the options together:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:6900/api/v1/technical/rsi" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"length": 2, "data": [{"date": "2024-01-02", "close": 185.6}, {"date": "2024-01-03", "close": 184.2}, {"date": "2024-01-04", "close": 181.9}, {"date": "2024-01-05", "close": 181.2}, {"date": "2024-01-08", "close": 185.6}]}'
```

The `chart` flag that `openbb-charting` adds to charted routes is still a query parameter. In the Python interface nothing changes for callers: the generated method exposes the same keyword arguments.

Commands can now stream. A router that declares an `OBBStream` return type, backed by a fetcher that implements `stream_data`, is served as a `text/event-stream` response. Because the body carries the events, the stream id, provider, and warnings travel in the `X-OpenBB-Stream-Id`, `X-OpenBB-Provider`, and `X-OpenBB-Warning` headers. In Python the same command returns an `OBBStream` handle instead of an `OBBject`, and the one-shot CLI follows the stream to stdout until it ends or you press Ctrl+C. See [Streaming responses](./concepts/streaming.mdx).

The REST app can also host Flask applications. A Flask app registered directly under the `openbb_core_extension` entry-point group is mounted at `/api/v1/<entry point name>`, and its routes are merged into `openapi.json`. This needs the `flask` extra of `openbb-core`.

## openbb-api and openbb-mcp

`openbb-api` (`openbb-platform-api`) and `openbb-mcp` (`openbb-mcp-server`) run the layered loader before anything else starts, so the `[system]` and `[user]` sections of `openbb.toml` apply to the server. Both accept `--config-file PATH` as the explicit layer. Without the flag, `openbb-api` checks `OPENBB_API_CONFIG` and then `OPENBB_CONFIG`, and `openbb-mcp` checks `OPENBB_MCP_CONFIG`, `OPENBB_API_CONFIG`, and `OPENBB_CONFIG`.

Each launcher reads its own table of flag defaults, `[launcher]` for `openbb-api` and `[mcp]` for `openbb-mcp`; flags on the command line still win. An `[env]` table sets environment variables before `openbb-core` loads, skips any already set in the shell, and expands `$VAR` and `${VAR}` references against the current environment.

```toml
[launcher]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 6900

[env]
FRED_API_KEY = "$FRED_KEY"
```

Both launchers accept `--spec PATH` with a `.spec` file generated by the CLI. Instead of the installed commands, they serve a proxy whose routes forward to the spec's upstream `base_url`, which `openbb-api` exposes to OpenBB Workspace and `openbb-mcp` turns into MCP tools. `--spec` and `--app` are mutually exclusive. The `[spec]` table (`[mcp.spec]` for the MCP server) sets `path`, an optional `base_url` override, a `content_sha256` pin, and `headers` injected on upstream requests; `[spec.NAME]` subtables (`[mcp.spec.NAME]` for the MCP server) mount several specs at once. Middleware and authentication hooks are listed under `[middleware]` for `openbb-api` and `[mcp.middleware]` and `[mcp.auth]` for `openbb-mcp`.

When `openbb-cli` is installed, `openbb-mcp` also registers the `openbb_dispatch`, `openbb_batch_dispatch`, `openbb_list_commands`, and `openbb_describe_command` tools, which wrap the CLI dispatcher. `--enable-cli-tools false` turns them off. Details are on the [openbb-api](./extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx) and [openbb-mcp](./extensions/interface/openbb-mcp.mdx) pages.

## Extension additions

`openbb-technical` 2.0.0 keeps every V4 indicator and adds more, including `supertrend`, `williams_r`, `mfi`, `kama`, `tema`, `pivot_points`, `realized_volatility`, and `hurst`. It also adds `multi` to run several indicators over one series, `screen` to filter a basket of symbols by indicator conditions, `indicators` to list what is registered, and the `obb.technical.signals` group for crossovers, divergences, breakouts, candlestick patterns, oscillator signals, and regime detection. See [openbb-technical](./extensions/data-processing/technical.mdx).

`openbb-quantitative` adds factor analysis: `factors` regresses a return series on a factor matrix and charts the exposures as a heat map, `attribution` splits total return into factor contributions and alpha, `risk_decomposition` splits variance by factor, and `rolling.factors` runs the regression over a moving window. The GARCH model lives in `openbb-econometrics` as `obb.econometrics.garch`, next to the new `kpss`, `cointegration_johansen`, `heteroskedasticity`, `normality`, and `summary_statistics` commands. See [openbb-quantitative](./extensions/data-processing/quantitative.mdx) and [openbb-econometrics](./extensions/data-processing/econometrics.mdx).

`openbb-news` adds `obb.news.rss`, which reads RSS and Atom feeds from a bundled registry and from feeds you define in the `[news]` table of `openbb.toml`. By default your `[news.rss_feeds]` entries replace the bundled registry; set `merge_defaults = true` to keep it.

```toml
[news]
merge_defaults = true

[news.rss_feeds]
my_feed = "https://example.com/feed.rss"
```

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.news.rss(source="yahoo_finance")
```

See [openbb-news](./extensions/openbb-news.mdx).

`openbb-core` no longer imports `openbb-charting` by name. The charting engine is the OBBject extension named by the `charting_extension` system setting, falling back to the default `charting` accessor, and rendering backends and lifecycle hooks register through the `openbb_charting_backend` and `openbb_charting_hooks` entry-point groups. `openbb-charting` 4.0.0 remains the default engine; see [openbb-charting](./extensions/infrastructure/openbb-charting/index.md).

title: Quick start — Developer
sidebar_position: 2
description: >
  Register a FastAPI APIRouter as an openbb_core_extension and call it as a
  method on obb and as a REST endpoint.
keywords:
  - quickstart
  - developer
  - FastAPI
  - APIRouter
  - openbb_core_extension
  - openbb-build
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Quick start (Developer) | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

Any `FastAPI` app or `APIRouter` registered under the `openbb_core_extension` entry-point group becomes an OpenBB extension. Its routes are served by the OpenBB REST API and generated as methods on `obb`. This page registers a one-route router and calls it both ways.

## 1. Install openbb-core

```bash
pip install openbb-core
```

FastAPI and Uvicorn are installed with it.

## 2. Write the router

Create a project directory with an empty `my_extension/__init__.py` and this `my_extension/app.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel


class GreetResponse(BaseModel):
    message: str


router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/greet")
def greet(name: str = "world") -> GreetResponse:
    """Return a greeting."""
    return GreetResponse(message=f"hello, {name}")
```

This is an ordinary FastAPI router with no OpenBB imports.

## 3. Register the entry point

`pyproject.toml` in the project directory:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "openbb-my-app"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = ["openbb-core"]

[project.entry-points."openbb_core_extension"]
my_app = "my_extension.app:router"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["my_extension"]
```

The entry-point name, `my_app`, becomes the namespace on `obb` and the path segment in the REST API. The value must point to an already-created `FastAPI` or `APIRouter` instance; factory functions are not called.

## 4. Install the package

From the project directory:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

## 5. Build the Python Interface

```bash
openbb-build
```

This generates the `obb.my_app` methods. Importing `openbb` also rebuilds on its own when it detects a newly installed extension; [Packaging and static assets](../concepts/packaging.mdx) explains when each applies.

## 6. Call it from Python

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.my_app.greet(name="analyst")
```

```text
GreetResponse(message='hello, analyst')
```

The Python Interface returns whatever the route returns. OpenBB does not wrap it in an `OBBject`, so the `to_dataframe()` family of methods is not available on this result. To get them, annotate the route's return type as `OBBject[...]` and return `OBBject(results=...)`; see [The OBBject envelope](../concepts/obbject.mdx).

## 7. Call it over REST

Start the API with Uvicorn, which serves commands under `/api/v1`:

```bash
uvicorn openbb_core.api.rest_api:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

In another terminal:

```bash
curl "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/my_app/greet?name=analyst"
```

```json
{"message":"hello, analyst"}
```

The `openbb-api` launcher from `openbb-platform-api` serves the same routes on port 6900 by default and adds OpenBB Workspace support; see [Quick start (REST API)](rest_api.mdx).

If `openbb-build` fails, set `OPENBB_DEBUG_MODE=true` and run it again for the full error. [From FastAPI](../developer/extension_types/from_fastapi.md) covers how dependencies, streaming responses, and other FastAPI features behave in the Python Interface, and the [Developer](../developer/index.md) section covers building providers and native OpenBB routers.

title: MCP Server
sidebar_position: 4
description: >
  Serve the installed OpenBB Python V5 commands as Model Context Protocol
  tools with openbb-mcp, and connect Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or
  OpenBB Workspace.
keywords:

  - Model Context Protocol
  - openbb-mcp
  - openbb-mcp-server

  - streamable-http
  - stdio
  - openbb.toml
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="MCP Server Quickstart | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

`openbb-mcp` turns the routes of the OpenBB REST API into MCP tools. Each installed provider contributes its commands, so the tool list is whatever the environment has installed.

## Install

Install the server with the providers the agent should use:

```bash
pip install openbb-mcp-server openbb-cboe openbb-imf
```

The `cli` extra adds four tools that run commands through `openbb-cli`, locally or against a remote `openbb-api` server:

```bash
pip install "openbb-mcp-server[cli]"
```

## Start the server

```bash
openbb-mcp
```

The server listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp` over the `streamable-http` transport. Tool names come from the route path after `/api/v1`, so `obb.cboe.equity.quote` is the tool `cboe_equity_quote`. Next to the command tools, every server has `run_pipeline` for chaining tools on the server, `list_prompts`, `get_prompt`, `list_resources`, and `read_resource` for clients without native prompt and resource support, and `install_skill`.

On first start the server writes its defaults to `~/.openbb_platform/mcp_settings.json`.

## Choose the tools

A large installation produces hundreds of tools. Two flags keep the list manageable. `--allowed-categories` serves only the named categories, where a category is the first path segment after the prefix, which in V5 is usually the provider namespace:

```bash
openbb-mcp --allowed-categories cboe,imf
```

`--tool-discovery` hides the command tools behind four discovery tools, `available_categories`, `available_tools`, `search_tools`, and `call_tool`, so the agent searches for what it needs instead of receiving every definition up front:

```bash
openbb-mcp --tool-discovery
```

Discovery keeps no per-session state, so several clients can share one server.

## Pick a transport

`--transport` accepts `streamable-http` (the default), `sse`, and `stdio`. Use `stdio` when the client launches the server as a subprocess, as Claude Desktop does:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openbb-mcp": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--from",
        "openbb-mcp-server",
        "--with",
        "openbb-cboe",
        "--with",
        "openbb-imf",
        "openbb-mcp",
        "--transport",
        "stdio"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

HTTP clients such as Cursor and VS Code take the URL of a running server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openbb-mcp": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Save the configuration

Command-line flags can live in an `[mcp]` table of an `openbb.toml` file, either in `~/.openbb_platform/`, in the working directory or one of its parents, or at a path passed with `--config-file`:

```toml
[mcp]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 8001
allowed-categories = "cboe,imf"
tool-discovery = true
```

Flags given on the command line still win over the file.

## Add to OpenBB Workspace

Follow the [MCP tools](/workspace/analysts/ai-features/mcp-tools) guide to connect the running server to OpenBB Workspace.

<div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center'}}>
  <img
    className="pro-border-gradient"
    alt="Adding the OpenBB MCP server to OpenBB Workspace"
    src="https://openbb-cms.directus.app/assets/6d66dcf3-98c0-4150-aace-035a063df35a.png"
    width="100%"
  />
</div>

## Next steps

The [openbb-mcp reference](../extensions/interface/openbb-mcp.mdx) covers every setting, authentication, prompts, skills, per-route `mcp_config`, and serving a `.spec` file as a proxy.

keywords:

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="REST API Quickstart | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

Every command available on `obb` is also a route of a FastAPI app, `openbb_core.api.rest_api:app`, built from the same installed extensions. You can serve that app with the `openbb-api` launcher or with any ASGI server.

## Start the server

Install the launcher and at least one provider:

```bash
pip install openbb-platform-api openbb-cboe
```

Then start it:

```bash
openbb-api
```

`openbb-api` binds to `127.0.0.1:6900` and moves to the next free port if 6900 is taken. Next to the command routes it serves a landing page at `/` and the `widgets.json`, `apps.json`, and `agents.json` files that OpenBB Workspace reads; the [Workspace quickstart](workspace.mdx) covers that side. The [openbb-api reference](../extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx) lists every launcher flag.

The app itself needs only `openbb-core`, so any ASGI server can run it. With `uvicorn`, which `openbb-core` installs, it listens on uvicorn's default `127.0.0.1:8000`:

```bash
uvicorn openbb_core.api.rest_api:app
```

## Make a request

Routes live under the `/api/v1` prefix and mirror the Python path: `obb.cboe.equity.quote` becomes `GET /api/v1/cboe/equity/quote`, and keyword arguments become query parameters.

```bash
curl "http://127.0.0.1:6900/api/v1/cboe/equity/quote?symbol=AAPL&provider=cboe"
```

The response body is the serialized `OBBject`, with the rows under `results`:

```python
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "http://127.0.0.1:6900/api/v1/cboe/equity/quote",
    params={"symbol": "AAPL", "provider": "cboe"},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
rows = response.json()["results"]
```

Interactive documentation is at `/docs` (Swagger UI) and `/redoc`, and the OpenAPI schema is at `/openapi.json`.

## Listen on the network

Bind to `0.0.0.0` inside a container or to accept connections from other machines:

```bash
openbb-api --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6900
```

The same values can come from the `OPENBB_API_HOST` and `OPENBB_API_PORT` environment variables, or from a `[launcher]` table in `openbb.toml`:

```toml
[launcher]
host = "0.0.0.0"
port = 6900
```

`openbb-api` looks for `openbb.toml` in `~/.openbb_platform/` and in the working directory and its parents, and `--config-file PATH` adds one more file on top. Command-line flags override the file. See [openbb.toml](../user-guide/openbb-toml.mdx) for the full lookup order and the `[system]` table.

## Require a login

The API accepts every request by default. Set three environment variables before starting the server to require HTTP Basic authentication on the command routes:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENBB_API_AUTH` | `true` |
| `OPENBB_API_USERNAME` | The username clients must send |
| `OPENBB_API_PASSWORD` | The password clients must send |

The variables can also go in `~/.openbb_platform/.env`, which is loaded at startup. Clients then send a standard `Authorization: Basic` header, which `requests` builds from a tuple:

```python
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "http://127.0.0.1:6900/api/v1/cboe/equity/quote",
    params={"symbol": "AAPL", "provider": "cboe"},
    auth=("my_user", "my_password"),
    timeout=30,
)
```

Requests with a missing or wrong password get `401 Unauthorized`. Data provider keys are separate from this login; the server reads them from its own [credentials](../user-guide/credentials.mdx).

:::warning
Basic authentication sends the password on every request. Outside `localhost`, serve the API over HTTPS.
:::

## Restrict CORS

The API allows every origin, method, and header by default. That suits local development; for a server reachable from the internet, list the allowed origins under `api_settings.cors` in `~/.openbb_platform/system_settings.json`, which both `openbb-api` and the bare app read at startup:

```json
{
  "api_settings": {
    "cors": {
      "allow_origins": ["https://pro.openbb.co"],
      "allow_methods": ["GET", "POST"],
      "allow_headers": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

`openbb-api` also accepts the same fields in `openbb.toml`. The bare `uvicorn` command does not read `openbb.toml`.

```toml
[system.api_settings.cors]
allow_origins = ["https://pro.openbb.co"]
allow_methods = ["GET", "POST"]
allow_headers = ["*"]
```

[Settings](../settings/index.mdx) lists the other API settings.

## Serve over HTTPS

Pass a certificate and key to the server. `openbb-api` hands unrecognized flags to `uvicorn.run` as keyword arguments, so uvicorn options take underscores there:

```bash
openbb-api --ssl_certfile ./localhost.crt --ssl_keyfile ./localhost.key
```

With the uvicorn command, use its own hyphenated flags:

```bash
uvicorn openbb_core.api.rest_api:app --ssl-certfile ./localhost.crt --ssl-keyfile ./localhost.key
```

A self-signed certificate works for local use once the operating system or browser trusts it. [ODP Desktop](../../desktop/backends.md#self-signed-certificate) can generate one.

## Next steps

The [Workspace quickstart](workspace.mdx) connects the running server to OpenBB Workspace. The [openbb-api reference](../extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx) covers the remaining launcher flags, the `openbb.toml` tables, custom apps, and `.spec` proxy mode. To give AI agents the same commands, continue with the [MCP server quickstart](mcp.mdx).

description: >
  Install a provider, set its API key, and make a first call with
  from openbb import obb.
keywords:

  - FRED

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Quick start (User) | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

This walkthrough uses FRED, the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis economic database. In V5 each provider package adds its own namespace to `obb`, so FRED commands live under `obb.fred`.

## 1. Install

```bash
pip install openbb-fred
```

`openbb-fred` depends on `openbb-core` with its pandas extra, and `openbb-core` provides the `openbb` package that `from openbb import obb` imports. Other ways to install are covered in [Installation](../installation.mdx).

The first import builds the Python Interface for the installed extensions, which takes a moment and prints `Building...`. In containers and CI, run `openbb-build` right after installing instead; see [Packaging and static assets](../concepts/packaging.mdx).

## 2. Set the FRED API key

The provider declares one credential, `fred_api_key`. Request a key from your account at [fred.stlouisfed.org](https://fred.stlouisfed.org) under "My Account", then "API Keys".

Export it in the shell that runs Python:

```bash
export FRED_API_KEY="YOUR_FRED_KEY"
```

Or store it in `~/.openbb_platform/user_settings.json`, which is created on the first import:

```json
{
  "credentials": {
    "fred_api_key": "YOUR_FRED_KEY"
  },
  "preferences": {},
  "defaults": {
    "commands": {}
  }
}
```

If both are set, the JSON value is used. [Configure credentials](../user-guide/credentials.mdx) explains the other options and how the REST API and MCP server read keys.

## 3. Make a call

```python
from openbb import obb

print(obb.fred.economy)
```

Printing a namespace lists its commands and sub-namespaces, including `fred_series`. Request a series by its FRED ID:

```python
gdp = obb.fred.economy.fred_series(symbol="GDP", start_date="2015-01-01")

print(gdp.provider)
print(gdp.extra["results_metadata"]["GDP"]["title"])
print(gdp.to_dataframe())
```

The call returns an `OBBject`. `results` holds one record per date, `extra["results_metadata"]` carries each series' title, units, and frequency, and `to_dataframe()` returns a pandas DataFrame indexed by date. See [The OBBject envelope](../concepts/obbject.mdx) for the other fields and methods, and the [reference page](/odp/python/reference/fred/economy/fred_series) for every parameter.

## 4. Pick an output type

For a one-off conversion, call a method such as `to_dataframe()`, `to_dict()`, or `to_llm()` on the result. To change what every command returns in this session, set the preference:

```python
obb.user.preferences.output_type = "dataframe"
```

Accepted values are `"OBBject"` (the default), `"dataframe"`, `"numpy"`, `"dict"`, `"llm"`, and `"polars"`. [Output types](../user-guide/output-types.mdx) lists what each returns and which packages it needs.

## 5. Verify

In a new session, confirm the key is loaded and the call reaches FRED. The key prints as asterisks, and the provider is `fred`.

```python
from openbb import obb

print(obb.user.credentials.fred_api_key)
print(obb.fred.economy.fred_series(symbol="GDP", limit=5).provider)
```

A `Missing credential 'fred_api_key'` error means the key was not found; check the variable name or the JSON file. From here, the [User Guide](../user-guide/index.mdx) covers defaults, parameters, warnings, and errors, and the [REST API quickstart](rest_api.mdx) serves the same commands over HTTP.

title: Workspace Integration
sidebar_position: 5
description: >
  Connect OpenBB Python V5 to OpenBB Workspace as a custom backend with
  openbb-api, using the installed providers, your own FastAPI app, or a
  .spec file that proxies a remote deployment.
keywords:

  - custom backend
  - openbb-api
  - openbb-platform-api
  - widgets.json
  - FastAPI
  - data connectors
  - .spec
---

import HeadTitle from "@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx";

<HeadTitle title="Workspace Quickstart | OpenBB Python (V5)" />

OpenBB Workspace loads data from [custom backends](/workspace/developers/data-integration): HTTP servers that describe their widgets in a `widgets.json` file. The `openbb-api` launcher, from the `openbb-platform-api` package, generates that file from a FastAPI app's routes and serves it next to the data. The app can be the installed OpenBB commands, a FastAPI file of your own, or a proxy built from a `.spec` file.

## Serve the installed commands

```bash
pip install openbb-platform-api openbb-cboe
openbb-api
```

The server starts on `http://127.0.0.1:6900`. Each command of each installed provider becomes a widget, shaped by any `widget_config` its router declares. Commands from `openbb-econometrics`, `openbb-quantitative`, and `openbb-technical` are left out, since they transform data passed in by the caller rather than fetch it.

To add the server to Workspace, sign in at [pro.openbb.co](https://pro.openbb.co), open **Data Connectors** from the sidebar, and click **Add Data**. Enter a name and the server address printed in the terminal, click **Test**, then **Add**. The widgets appear in the Workspace search.

<div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center'}}>
  <img
    className="pro-border-gradient"
    alt="The Add Data dialog in OpenBB Workspace"
    src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/770e6d6c-6cd7-4073-a874-af0850f404cc"
    width="100%"
  />
</div>

:::tip
If **Test** fails, the browser may be blocking requests from the HTTPS Workspace page to an HTTP server. The launcher's startup message recommends Chrome. Otherwise, [serve the API over HTTPS](rest_api.mdx#serve-over-https).
:::

## Serve your own app

`--app` replaces the installed commands with the routes of a FastAPI app. The app can still call `obb`; only its own routes become widgets.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from openbb import obb

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/quote_summary")
def quote_summary(symbol: str = "AAPL") -> str:
    """Delayed Cboe quote with 30-day implied volatility."""
    quote = obb.cboe.equity.quote(symbol=symbol, provider="cboe").results[0]
    return (
        f"## {quote.name}\n\n"
        f"Last price: {quote.last_price}\n\n"
        f"30-day implied volatility: {quote.iv30}"
    )
```

Save it as `quote_app.py` and launch it:

```bash
openbb-api --app quote_app.py --reload
```

The route returns a string, so the widget is a Markdown widget. Its name comes from the path, its description from the docstring, and the `symbol` argument becomes a text parameter with `AAPL` as the default.

<div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center'}}>
  <img
    className="pro-border-gradient"
    alt="A Markdown widget generated from a custom FastAPI route"
    src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/150b214e-468e-45bf-b28e-6fb1e1a7a5c2"
    width="514"
  />
</div>

The app does not have to call `obb`. With only `openbb-platform-api` installed and no providers, any FastAPI file works, and the return annotation picks the widget type: a `str` becomes a Markdown widget, and a list of dictionaries or Pydantic models becomes a table.

```python
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()


class Row(BaseModel):
    """One row of the table."""

    label: str = Field(title="Label", description="Row label.")
    change: float = Field(
        title="Change",
        description="Change as a fraction.",
        json_schema_extra={
            "x-widget_config": {
                "formatterFn": "normalizedPercent",
                "renderFn": "greenRed",
            }
        },
    )


@app.get("/greeting")
async def greeting(
    language: Literal["English", "French", "Spanish"] = "English",
) -> str:
    """Markdown widget with a dropdown parameter."""
    greetings = {"English": "Hello", "French": "Bonjour", "Spanish": "Hola"}
    return f"# {greetings[language]}"


@app.get("/changes")
async def changes() -> list[Row]:
    """Table widget with column definitions from the model."""
    return [Row(label="A", change=0.0125), Row(label="B", change=-0.004)]
```

The `Literal` argument becomes a dropdown. The `Row` fields become column definitions, with each `title` as the header, each `description` as the header tooltip, and the `x-widget_config` values merged into the column. The [openbb-api reference](../extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx) covers metric, PDF, chart, Omni, form, and server-side row model widgets, and the `openapi_extra` overrides for any generated field.

## Proxy a remote deployment

A `.spec` file generated by `openbb-cli` records the routes of an OpenBB API server and its address. `openbb-api --spec` builds a backend whose routes forward each request to that server, so Workspace can reach a remote deployment through a launcher with no provider packages installed:

```bash
pip install openbb-cli
openbb --generate-spec --server https://api.example.com --output api.spec
openbb-api --spec api.spec
```

Widgets are generated from the parameter and response schemas in the spec, and their source label is the spec's file name. See the [openbb-api reference](../extensions/interface/openbb-api.mdx#spec-proxy-mode) for credentials, integrity checks, and mounting several specs, and [Codegen](../../cli/codegen.md) for generating spec files.

Fetch BLS CPI relative-importance and weights for one yearly file + sheet.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Latest CPI relative-importance weights for CPI-U & CPI-W.
obb.bls.cpi.relative_importance(provider='bls')
# 2024 weights for selected local areas (Table 2).
obb.bls.cpi.relative_importance(provider='bls', year=2024, table=2)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
Year of the relative-importance file to fetch; None walks back until a published file is found.

**table**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Which of the 7 sheets in the relative-importance XLSX to return.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `BlsCpiRelativeImportance`

Serializable results.

```python
from openbb import obb

```

## Parameters

*Default:* 1<br/>
Numbered change-analysis table to load.

Stable identifier for the source table.

Full BLS table title.

National or state scope of the table.

Source table number within the scope.

**measure**: `str`<br/>
JOLTS measure published in this table.

Comparison window for the table.

Whether the table is seasonally adjusted.

First-of-month start date of the comparison window.

**period_end**: `date | None`<br/>
First-of-month end date of the comparison window.

title: "revisions"

- bls
- jolts
- revisions
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="bls/jolts/revisions - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Fetch the JOLTS SA/NSA revision XLSX in long form (1st / 2nd / benchmark levels + revision deltas).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Full seasonally-adjusted JOLTS revision workbook.
obb.bls.jolts.revisions(provider='bls')
# NSA revision rows for Construction (industry code 23) only.
obb.bls.jolts.revisions(provider='bls', seasonally_adjusted=False, industry_code='23')
# SA Quits revisions across every industry / region.
obb.bls.jolts.revisions(provider='bls', measure='Quits')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**seasonally_adjusted**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to return the seasonally-adjusted revision workbook.

**industry_code**: `str | None`<br/>
Optional industry or region sheet code to restrict the results.

**measure**: `str | None`<br/>
Optional measure name to restrict the results.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `BlsJoltsRevisions`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
First-of-month reference date the revision values describe.

**industry_code**: `str`<br/>
BLS industry or region sheet code.

**industry_name**: `str`<br/>
Human-readable industry or region name.

**seasonally_adjusted**: `bool`<br/>
Whether the row comes from the seasonally-adjusted workbook.

**measure**: `str`<br/>
JOLTS measure for the row.

**level_1st**: `float | None`<br/>
First-published level (thousands).

**level_2nd**: `float | None`<br/>
Second-revision level (thousands).

**level_benchmark**: `float | None`<br/>
Benchmarked level (thousands).

**revision_1st_to_2nd_level**: `float | None`<br/>

Sequential parser order.

Fetch one table from a BLS monthly PPI Detailed Report (XLSX, 2022+).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Latest monthly PPI Detailed Report, Table 1 (FD-ID summary).
obb.bls.ppi.detailed_report(provider='bls')
# Specific month and table — unadjusted commodity indexes.
obb.bls.ppi.detailed_report(provider='bls', date='2026-04-01', table=9)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Month of the Detailed Report to fetch; None resolves to the most recent release.

**table**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Which of the 14 tables in the monthly PPI Detailed Report to return.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `BlsPpiDetailedReport`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
First day of the calendar month this row's values apply to.

**code**: `str | None`<br/>
Concatenated series identifier for the row.

**group_code**: `str | None`<br/>
BLS 'Group code' from the source XLSX.

**item_code**: `str | None`<br/>
BLS 'Item code' from the source XLSX.

**industry_code**: `str | None`<br/>
NAICS industry code from the source XLSX.

**product_code**: `str | None`<br/>
Product breakdown code of an industry's net output.

**label**: `str | None`<br/>
Human-readable series title from the source XLSX.

**footnote**: `str | None`<br/>
Combined BLS footnote text for any markers on the label.

**level**: `int | None`<br/>
Row indent depth in the source XLSX hierarchy.

**index_value**: `float | None`<br/>
Price-index value at the date.

**pct_change_1m**: `float | None`<br/>
One-month percent change in the index ending at the date.

**pct_change_12m**: `float | None`<br/>
Twelve-month percent change in the index ending at the date.

**relative_importance**: `float | None`<br/>
Relative-importance weight of this series within its parent aggregate, as a percentage.

**other_index_base**: `str | None`<br/>
Alternative index base period for this row when BLS overrides the table-wide default.

**seasonally_adjusted**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the values on this row are seasonally adjusted.

**table_id**: `str`<br/>
Source table identifier.

**table_name**: `str`<br/>
Full BLS table title.

**table_number**: `int`<br/>
Which of the 14 numbered tables in the monthly PPI Detailed Report this row belongs to.

**release_period**: `str`<br/>
Reporting month of the source release.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "tables"
description: "Fetch a BLS Productivity prod2 supplemental table in long form (every column preserved)"
keywords:
- bls
- productivity
- tables
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="bls/productivity/tables - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Fetch a BLS Productivity prod2 supplemental table in long form (every column preserved).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Quarterly Nonfarm business sector labor productivity (the default headline series).
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls')
# Manufacturing sector unit labor costs, quarterly.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', sector='Manufacturing sector', measure='Unit labor costs')
# Total economy hours worked, in billions of hours.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', dataset='total-economy-hours-employment', sector='Total economy', measure='Hours worked', units='Billions of hours')
# Nonfarm business labor productivity growth by business cycle.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', dataset='major-sectors-business-cycles', units='Compound annual growth rate')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**dataset**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* major-sectors-quarterly<br/>
Productivity supplemental dataset to load.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**sector**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Nonfarm business sector<br/>
Sector to restrict the results. Defaults to the headline Nonfarm business sector; clear it to load every sector.

**measure**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Labor productivity<br/>
Measure to restrict the results. Defaults to Labor productivity; clear it to load every measure.

**units**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Index (2017=100)<br/>
Units to restrict the results. Defaults to the 2017=100 index (one row per period); clear it to load every units basis. The source is long-form, so leaving every dimension open returns one row per sector / measure / units / period.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `BlsProductivityTables`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
First-of-period date the observation applies to.

**period_kind**: `str`<br/>
Period kind for the row (quarter, annual, or business cycle).

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
Year reported in the source XLSX.

**quarter**: `int | str | None`<br/>
Quarter index reported in the source XLSX.

**sector**: `str | None`<br/>
BLS sector this row belongs to.

**basis**: `str | None`<br/>
Worker-counting basis used for the row.

**component**: `str | None`<br/>
Sub-sector component for the total-economy workbook.

**measure**: `str`<br/>
Productivity measure being reported.

**units**: `str`<br/>
Units the value is expressed in.

**value**: `float | None`<br/>
Numeric observation.

**value_string**: `str | None`<br/>
Raw cell text when the value isn't numeric.

**cycle_period**: `str | None`<br/>
Business-cycle period label as published by BLS.

**cycle_start_date**: `date | None`<br/>
First-of-quarter start date for the business-cycle period.

**cycle_end_date**: `date | None`<br/>
First-of-quarter end date for the business-cycle period.

**row_index**: `int`<br/>
Sequential parser order preserving the source layout.

**table_id**: `str`<br/>
Stable dataset identifier.

**table_title**: `str`<br/>
Human-readable dataset title.

**source_file**: `str`<br/>
Filename of the source XLSX on bls.gov.

**release_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Release date stamped in the workbook header.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "search"
description: "Search the BLS series catalog by category, keyword, or code"
keywords:
- bls
- search
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="bls/search - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Search the BLS series catalog by category, keyword, or code.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Search the CPI category for series matching a query.
obb.bls.search(provider='bls', category='cpi', query='urban')
# List every series in the JOLTS category.
obb.bls.search(provider='bls', category='jolts')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**query**: `str | None`<br/>
The search word(s). Use semi-colon to separate multiple queries as an & operator.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**query**: `str | None`<br/>
The search word(s). Use semi-colon to separate multiple queries as an & operator.

**symbol**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Bound to the Series widget via cell-click grouping; clicking a row's symbol loads it there. Does not filter the search results. Multiple items allowed.

**category**: `str`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

The category of BLS survey to search within. An empty search query returns every series within the category. Options are:<br/>
<br/>
    cpi - Consumer Price Index<br/>
    ixp - Import/Export Price Indexes<br/>
    pce - Consumer Expenditure Survey<br/>
    ppi - Producer Price Index<br/>
    ip - Productivity (Industry, Major Sector & Total Factor)<br/>
    jolts - Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey<br/>
    nfp - Nonfarm Payrolls (Current Employment Statistics)<br/>
    cps - Current Population Survey<br/>
    lfs - Labor Force Statistics & International Comparisons<br/>
    wages - Employment Cost Index & Wage Estimates<br/>
    ec - Employer Costs for Employee Compensation<br/>
    sla - State & Local Area Employment & Unemployment<br/>
    bed - Business Employment Dynamics<br/>
    tu - American Time Use Survey<br/>
</details>

**include_extras**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Include additional information in the search results. Extra fields returned are metadata and vary by survey. Fields are undefined strings that typically have names ending with '_code'.

**include_code_map**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When True, includes the complete code map for eaçh survey in the category, returned separately as a nested JSON to the `extras['results_metadata']` property of the response. Example content is the NAICS industry map for PPI surveys. Each code is a value within the 'symbol' of the time series.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `BlsSearch`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**title**: `str | None`<br/>
The title of the series.

**survey_name**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the survey.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
BLS series identifier. Click a cell to load it into the linked BLS Series widget.

**title**: `str | None`<br/>
The title of the series.

**survey_name**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the survey.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Fetch BLS time series data by series identifier.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Fetch a single series by symbol from the BLS API.
obb.bls.series(provider='bls', symbol='CUUR0000SA0')
# Fetch multiple series with calculations enabled.
obb.bls.series(provider='bls', symbol='CUUR0000SA0,WPUFD4', calculations=True)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): bls.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='bls' label='bls'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): bls.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**category**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* cpi<br/>
Survey category that scopes the symbol picker's choices. Does not filter the returned data (series are fetched by symbol); keep it in sync with the Search widget to drill down by clicking.

**calculations**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Include calculations in the response, if available. Default is True.

**annual_average**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Include annual averages in the response, if available. Default is False.

**aspects**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Include all aspects associated with a data point for a given BLS series ID, if available. Returned with the series metadata, under `extras` of the response object. Default is False.

## Parameters

<Tabs>

Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**interval**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1d<br/>
Time interval of the data to return. The most recent trading day is not including in daily historical data. Intraday data is only available for the most recent trading day at 1 minute intervals.

<details>

- 1m
- 1d
</details>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>

This represents the number of round lot orders at the given price. The normal round lot size is 100 shares. A size of 2 means there are 200 shares available at the given price.

The specific trading venue where the sale order was placed.

**quote_conditions**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Conditions or condition codes applicable to the quote.

**quote_indicators**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Indicators or indicator codes applicable to the participant quote related to the price bands for the issue, or the affect the quote has on the NBBO.

**sales_conditions**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Conditions or condition codes applicable to the sale.

**sequence_number**: `int | None`<br/>
The sequence number represents the sequence in which message events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11).

**market_center**: `str | None`<br/>
The ID of the UTP participant that originated the message.

**participant_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the quote was generated by the exchange.

**trf_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the TRF (Trade Reporting Facility) received the message.

**sip_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the SIP (Security Information Processor) received the message from the exchange.

**last_price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the last trade.

**last_tick**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the last sale was an up or down tick.

**last_size**: `int | None`<br/>
Size of the last trade.

**last_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and Time when the last price was recorded.

**open**: `float | None`<br/>
The open price.

**high**: `float | None`<br/>
The high price.

**low**: `float | None`<br/>
The low price.

**close**: `float | None`<br/>
The close price.

**volume**: `float | int | None`<br/>
The trading volume.

**exchange_volume**: `float | int | None`<br/>
Volume of shares exchanged during the trading day on the specific exchange.

**prev_close**: `float | None`<br/>
The previous close price.

**change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in price from previous close.

**change_percent**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in price as a normalized percentage.

**year_high**: `float | None`<br/>
The one year high (52W High).

**year_low**: `float | None`<br/>
The one year low (52W Low).

**iv30**: `float | None`<br/>
The 30-day implied volatility of the stock.

**iv30_change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in 30-day implied volatility of the stock.

**iv30_change_percent**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in 30-day implied volatility of the stock as a normalized percentage value.

**iv30_annual_high**: `float | None`<br/>
The 1-year high of 30-day implied volatility.

**hv30_annual_high**: `float | None`<br/>
The 1-year high of 30-day realized volatility.

**iv30_annual_low**: `float | None`<br/>
The 1-year low of 30-day implied volatility.

The 1-year high of 60-day implied volatility.

Get the settlement prices for Cboe futures contracts.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Settlement prices for the most recent session.
obb.cboe.futures.settlement_prices(provider='cboe')
# Final settlement prices for expired contracts.
obb.cboe.futures.settlement_prices(final_settlement=True, provider='cboe')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cboe' label='cboe'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
The settlement date. Sessions that settled nothing, such as weekends and holidays, fall back to the most recent session that did.

**options**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When True, returns options on futures.

**archives**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Settlement price archives for select years and products. Overridden by the other parameters.

**final_settlement**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Final settlement prices for expired contracts. Overrides archives.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Historical Cboe index levels, daily or one-minute.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Daily historical index levels.
obb.cboe.index.historical(symbol='AAVE10RP', provider='cboe')
# One-minute levels for the most recent trading day.
obb.cboe.index.historical(symbol='BUK100P', interval='1m', provider='cboe')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): cboe.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cboe' label='cboe'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): cboe.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**interval**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1d<br/>
Time interval of the data to return. The most recent trading day is not including in daily historical data. Intraday data is only available for the most recent trading day at 1 minute intervals.

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- 1m
- 1d
</details>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
When True, the company directories will be cached for 24 hours and are used to validate symbols. The results of the function are not cached. Set as False to bypass.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "cds_index_trades"
description: "Get credit default swap index transactions disseminated by DTCC"
keywords:
- cftc
- cds_index_trades
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/cds_index_trades - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get credit default swap index transactions disseminated by DTCC.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get the CDX.NA.IG tape.
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(index='CDX.NA.IG', provider='cftc')
# Get the 5Y CDX.NA.HY prints of at least 10mm notional.
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(index='CDX.NA.HY', tenor='5Y', min_notional=10000000, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**index**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by index family, matched against the UPI Underlier Name. E.g., 'CDX.NA.IG'. Matching is exact and case-insensitive, because 'ITRAXX EUROPE' is a substring of two other index families. Default is every index.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent date whose file holds index prints matching the query; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

**tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by the print's tenor at execution. E.g., '5Y'. Default is every tenor.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Filter out prints whose leg 1 notional is disseminated below this amount. A print above the reporting cap is disseminated at the cap, which is only a floor on its true size, so a threshold above a cap drops prints that may in fact exceed it. Caps vary by index, tenor and currency.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of prints to return. Default is all matching.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcCdsIndexTrades`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**dissemination_date**: `date`<br/>
Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in. The cumulative file carries no per-message dissemination timestamp.

**trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'CR:4411567497000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of action taken on the swap transaction: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), EROR (error), TERM (terminate), or REVI (revive).

**event_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Explanation or reason for the action being taken on the swap transaction: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation/step-in), COMP (compression or post trade risk reduction exercise), ETRM (early termination), CLRG (clearing), EXER (exercise), or CREV (credit event).

**event_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time of occurrence of the event, as determined by the reporting counterparty or a service provider.

**execution_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time the transaction was originally executed, resulting in the generation of a new UTI. It remains unchanged throughout the life of the UTI, so on a correction or termination it dates the original trade.

**index**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the asset or index underlying the product corresponding to the UPI. It names the index family only and carries no series number, so `maturity_date` is what pins the series.

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name issued by the UPI Service Provider. 'NA/CDS Corp Idx Tra' marks a tranche print.

**unique_product_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier (UPI), a unique set of characters that represents a particular OTC derivative.

**effective_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction come into effect. For a credit index this should be the effective date of the contract, usually one or two days after execution, and not the roll date of the underlying index.

**maturity_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction stop being effective, as included in the confirmation ('Expiration date'). Early termination does not affect it. Together with `index` it identifies the series traded.

**tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
Years from `execution_timestamp` to `maturity_date`, snapped to the nearest standard CDS index tenor within one year, else the rounded year count. Derived, not disseminated.

**coupon**: `float | None`<br/>
Per annum rate of the fixed leg, expressed as a decimal (0.05 is 500bp). The index's standardised coupon, and with `upfront_amount` the price of the print.

**coupon_day_count**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 20022 day count convention of the fixed leg. A004 is ACT/360.

**coupon_payment_frequency**: `str | None`<br/>
Time unit associated with the frequency of fixed leg payments: DAIL, WEEK, MNTH, YEAR, ADHO, or EXPI (payment at term).

**coupon_payment_frequency_multiplier**: `float | None`<br/>
Number of time units of `coupon_payment_frequency` between payments. MNTH with a multiplier of 3 is quarterly.

**upfront_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Payment amount corresponding to `upfront_type`, in `upfront_currency`. With `coupon` it prices the print.

**upfront_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of the other payment amount. UFRO is an upfront payment: the initial payment made by one of the counterparties either to bring a transaction to fair value or for any other reason that may be the cause of an off-market transaction. UWIN is an unwind or full termination payment; PEXH is a principal exchange.

**upfront_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which `upfront_amount` is denominated.

**spread**: `float | None`<br/>
Reported spread on the leg 1 index reference price, as disseminated. Conditional: it is required only where `coupon` is not populated and `upfront_type` is not 'UFRO', so it is an alternative to the coupon-plus-upfront quote rather than the price of the print. Read it together with `spread_notation` - the field also carries a price in points of par on the price-quoted indices. See the package README.

**spread_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Manner in which `spread` is expressed: 1 (monetary amount, in `spread_currency`), 3 (decimal, e.g. 0.0257 for 2.57%), or 4 (basis points, e.g. 257 for 2.57%).

**spread_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which `spread` is denominated. Only applicable when `spread_notation` is 1.

**index_factor**: `float | None`<br/>
The index version factor or percent, expressed as a decimal value, that multiplied by the notional amount yields the notional amount covered by the seller of protection. Below 1 once a constituent has defaulted.

**notional_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 1 notional amount specified in the contract, gross of any version incrementing due to a credit event. Values above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap and flagged by `is_capped`.

**notional_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency in which the leg 1 notional amount is denominated.

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap rather than its true value. Other disseminated amounts are proportionally scaled when the notional is capped.

**venue**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility the transaction was executed on. XOFF marks a transaction in a listed instrument executed off venue, XXXX an instrument not listed on any venue, and BILT a reporting counterparty that could not determine whether the instrument is listed.

**cleared**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction has been cleared, or is intended to be cleared, by a central counterparty: Y (centrally cleared), N (not centrally cleared), or I (intent to clear, for original swaps planned to be submitted to clearing).

**block_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether an election has been made to report the transaction as a block trade, by the reporting counterparty or as calculated by the SDR on its behalf or by a third party.

**package_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is part of a package transaction, being two or more transactions negotiated together as the product of a single economic agreement.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>



---

Score COT positioning against each trader group's own lookback range.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.cot_index(provider='cftc')
# Score the index and bond markets against their own year.

```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**asset_class**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* all<br/>
Asset class of the curated markets to score.

**lookback_weeks**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 52<br/>
Weeks of history the score ranks the latest net position within. 52 puts each reading in its own one-year range.

**futures_only**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Score the futures-only report, the basis COT positioning work conventionally uses. False scores the combined futures-and-options report, whose larger open interest dilutes every net-to-open-interest share.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache each market's report history locally.

</TabItem>

</TabItem>

Date of the CFTC report the scores are taken from.

**market**: `str`<br/>
Curated market name.

**open_interest**: `int | None`<br/>
Total open interest on the report date.

**small_specs_change**: `float | None`<br/>

Small speculators' net position as a percent of open interest.

Band the small speculators' score sits in.

title: "fx_forward_curve"
description: "Get the outright FX forward curve, in units of the currency per one US dollar"
keywords:
- cftc
- fx_forward_curve
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/fx_forward_curve - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the outright FX forward curve, in units of the currency per one US dollar.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_forward_curve(provider='cftc')
# Get the USDKRW forward curve, in KRW per US dollar.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_curve(pair='USDKRW', provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USDJPY<br/>
Currency pair. The curve is quoted as the foreign currency per one US dollar whichever way the pair is named. The USD/EM pairs (USDKRW, USDINR, ...) are non-deliverable forwards.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth; 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, which leaves thin tenors missing.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, defaulting to today. With source='slice' it selects the most recent day on or before it that priced this pair. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 30<br/>
Number of dissemination days to search back over, ending on `date`. Only used when source='search'. A longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days`.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1000000.0<br/>
Minimum trade notional, in the base currency. Set to 0 to keep every trade.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop tenors priced by fewer than this many trades.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcFxForwardCurve`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair the curve is built for.

**index**: `str`<br/>
Settlement tenor of the node - the row and chart index.

**tenor_days**: `int`<br/>
Lower bound of the tenor bucket, in days.

**rate**: `float`<br/>
Outright forward rate, in units of the foreign currency per US dollar.

**spot**: `float`<br/>
Spot rate of the tenor's as-of date, per US dollar.

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Number of executed trades aggregated into the tenor.

**total_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Sum of the base currency notional of the tenor's trades.

**min_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Lowest executed rate at the node, per US dollar.

**max_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Highest executed rate at the node, per US dollar.

**as_of_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the tenor's trades were reported on.

**staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Days between the tenor's as-of date and the curve's date.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>
