---
title: "fx_forward_points"
description: "Get FX forward points, built from executed forwards and FX swaps"
keywords:
- cftc
- fx_forward_points
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/fx_forward_points - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get FX forward points, built from executed forwards and FX swaps.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(provider='cftc')
# Get USDJPY forward points.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(pair='USDJPY', provider='cftc')
# Include sub-institutional trades, which price away from the market.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(pair='EURUSD', min_notional=0, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* EURUSD<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention. The USD/EM pairs (USDKRW, USDINR, USDBRL, ...) are non-deliverable forwards.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, which leaves thin tenors missing and yields nothing on a weekend.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects one day's file, and defaults to the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 30<br/>
Number of dissemination days to search back over, ending on `date`. Only used when source='search'. A longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days`. The source caps a search at 180 days.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1000000.0<br/>
Minimum trade notional, in the base currency. Sub-institutional prints trade percent away from the interbank market and would otherwise dominate a tenor's median. Set to 0 to keep every trade.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop tenors priced by fewer than this many trades. The default keeps every tenor, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcFxForwardPoints`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve, being that of its freshest tenor.

**as_of_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the tenor's trades were reported on.

**staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Days between the tenor's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest tenors.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention.

**tenor**: `str`<br/>
Tenor bucket of the observation.

**tenor_days**: `int`<br/>
Lower bound of the tenor bucket, in days.

**spot_rate**: `float`<br/>
Spot rate of the tenor's as-of date, the median of that day's trades settling within two days, or of its shortest-dated tenor for a non-deliverable pair.

**forward_rate**: `float`<br/>
Median executed forward rate at the tenor.

**forward_points**: `float`<br/>
Executed forward rate less spot, in pips.

**theoretical_points**: `float | None`<br/>
Covered-interest-parity forward points from the two legs' rate curves, in pips - each leg's OIS, or its fixed-float IRS for an EM currency with no OIS. Present only when both legs have a curve; for a non-deliverable pair its gap to the executed points (`basis_points`) is the NDF basis to onshore rates.

**basis_points**: `float | None`<br/>
Executed points less the CIP points, in pips: positive where the market pays over covered-interest-parity fair value, negative under.

**quotation**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the base is at a forward premium (executed points positive, forward above spot) or a discount (points negative, forward below spot).

**carry**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether a long base-currency forward position earns or pays the points to the forward date. It earns at a discount - the base out-yields the quote, so it is bought forward below spot - and pays at a premium. The short-base side is the opposite (Lehman Brothers, FX Training Manual: pay or earn the points).

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Number of executed trades aggregated into the tenor.

**total_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Sum of the base currency notional of the tenor's trades.

**min_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Lowest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `max_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

**max_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Highest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `min_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>



---

title: "fx_forward_trades"
description: "Get the raw FX forward and swap transactions disseminated by DTCC, newest first"

- fx_forward_trades

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/fx_forward_trades - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the raw FX forward and swap transactions disseminated by DTCC, newest first.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_forward_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get the newly executed non-deliverable forward prints.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_trades(product_type='Non-Deliverable Forward', action_type='NEWT', provider='cftc')
# Get the USD-settled non-deliverable forward and swap prints.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_trades(settlement_currency='USD', provider='cftc')
# Get the 20 largest INR forward prints of the day.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_trades(pair='INR', min_notional=50000000, limit=20, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to a pair or currency, matched against the two reported legs. 'EURUSD', 'EUR/USD' and 'EUR USD' all match EUR/USD; a single code like 'INR' matches every pair with that leg. Default is every pair, deliverable and non-deliverable.

**product_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by product: Forward (deliverable outright), Non-Deliverable Forward (cash-settled EM outright), FX Swap (near and far legs), Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Default is every product.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent day whose file holds forward prints; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by the action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). Default is every action; pass NEWT for newly executed trades only.

**settlement_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to trades whose leg-1 settlement currency matches, e.g. 'USD' for the USD-settled trades regardless of pair orientation. Non-deliverable forwards and swaps always carry it - their single cash-settlement currency; deliverable trades carry it only when reported. Default is every settlement.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Drop prints whose larger notional leg is disseminated below this amount. The two legs value the same trade in each currency, so the larger is a currency-agnostic size proxy. Amounts above the reporting cap disseminate at the cap.

**ticker**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. Default is every product. A ticker query is answered by the source's search API, cached per day, not the daily files.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of prints to return, newest execution first. Default is all matching.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

List of warnings.

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**event_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and time the reported event occurred, in UTC. The tape is ordered by it, newest first: a termination or correction of an old trade is dated when it is reported now, not when the trade was struck.

**execution_timestamp**: `datetime`<br/>
Date and time the forward was originally executed, in UTC. It equals the reported time on a new trade, but predates it on an amendment or termination.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair of the forward, its two reported legs.

**product_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Product, read from the FISN: Forward, Non-Deliverable Forward (`settlement_currency` is the cash-settled leg), FX Swap, Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Derived, not disseminated.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). An amendment carries the original trade's identifier in `original_trade_key`.

**exchange_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Agreed forward rate on the trade, oriented as `exchange_rate_basis` states. For an FX swap it is the rate of the disseminated leg.

**exchange_rate_basis**: `str | None`<br/>
Quotation the forward rate is expressed in, e.g. 'USD/INR'.

**notional_1**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 1 notional, in `notional_currency_1`.

**notional_currency_1**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 1 notional.

**notional_2**: `float | None`<br/>
Leg 2 notional, in `notional_currency_2`.

**notional_currency_2**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency of the leg 2 notional.

**settlement_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Settlement currency of leg 1. For a non-deliverable forward or swap it is the single currency the net cash settles in rather than delivering; a deliverable trade carries the physical settlement currency of leg 1 when reported.

**effective_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the forward comes into effect.

**expiration_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the forward settles.

**days_to_expiry**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar days from execution to expiration.

**cleared**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is centrally cleared: Y (cleared), N (not cleared), or I (intent to clear).

**venue**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility, or BILT when the reporting counterparty could not determine the venue.

**event_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Reason for the action: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation), ETRM (early termination), or CLRG (clearing).

**block_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is reported as a block trade.

**prime_brokerage**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the transaction is a prime-brokerage transaction.

**package_trade**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the print is one leg of a package transaction - legs negotiated and priced together, such as the near and far legs of a swap booked as a package.

**package_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Grouping key shared by the legs of one package - its execution time and package price or spread. Group on it to reassemble the package. Derived, not disseminated.

**package_price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the whole package, in the format `package_price_notation` states; the same on every leg. Present on price-quoted packages, where DTCC's 9.9999999999 not-provided placeholder has been dropped to null.

**package_price_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the package price is denominated in, when it is a monetary amount.

**package_price_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_price`: 1 (a monetary amount, in `package_price_currency`) or 3 (a decimal).

**package_spread**: `float | None`<br/>
Spread of the whole package; the same on every leg. Present on spread-quoted packages instead of a price.

**package_spread_notation**: `str | None`<br/>
Format of `package_spread`: 1 (a monetary amount) or 3 (a decimal).

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name, e.g. 'NA/Fwd NDF INR USD'.

**underlier**: `str | None`<br/>
UPI underlier name, the two legs of the pair as reported.

**unique_product_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier.

**dissemination_date**: `date`<br/>
Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in.

**trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'FX:4419882315000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

**original_trade_key**: `str | None`<br/>
For an action other than 'New', the qualified identifier of the original trade being amended, corrected or terminated. Match it against a `trade_key` to follow a trade's lifecycle.

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "fx_implied_vol"

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/fx_implied_vol - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get FX implied volatility from vanilla options disseminated by DTCC.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_implied_vol(provider='cftc')
# Get the USDJPY implied-volatility smile by tenor.
obb.cftc.fx_implied_vol(pair='USDJPY', provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**pair**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* EURUSD<br/>
Currency pair, in market quoting convention. Limited to the pairs whose options are reported to the CFTC in enough depth to build a surface each day. The USD/EM pairs (USDBRL, USDKRW, ...) are built from non-deliverable options against a spot and forward taken from the reported non-deliverable forwards.

**basis**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* empirical<br/>
How the surface is built: 'empirical' medians the traded options at each grid strike (gaps where nothing traded); 'theoretical' fits a lognormal-SABR smile per expiry and evaluates it on the grid (smooth, gap-free).

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC) of the options. Defaults to the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3<br/>
Minimum trades for an OIS curve node used to price the rate legs.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcFxImpliedVol`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Dissemination date of the options.

**pair**: `str`<br/>
Currency pair.

**strike**: `float`<br/>
Strike price of the underlying, on a grid of offsets from spot.

**strike_offset**: `float`<br/>
The strike's distance from spot, positive above spot: in points for a deliverable major, in basis points of spot for a non-deliverable USD/EM pair.

**vol_1w**: `float | None`<br/>
1-week implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_2w**: `float | None`<br/>
2-week implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_1m**: `float | None`<br/>
1-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_2m**: `float | None`<br/>
2-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_3m**: `float | None`<br/>
3-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_6m**: `float | None`<br/>
6-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_9m**: `float | None`<br/>
9-month implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_1y**: `float | None`<br/>
1-year implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**vol_2y**: `float | None`<br/>
2-year implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

**num_options**: `int`<br/>
Number of options aggregated into the strike row, across expiries.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "ois_curve"
description: "Get an overnight index swap curve, built from executed swap transactions"
keywords:
- cftc
- ois_curve
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/ois_curve - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get an overnight index swap curve, built from executed swap transactions.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the USD SOFR curve.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(provider='cftc')
# Get the EUR ESTR curve.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(currency='EUR', provider='cftc')
# Fill in a thinly traded currency's short end, which needs a longer window and admits single prints.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(currency='CHF', lookback_days=30, min_trades=1, provider='cftc')
# Get the curve at every distinct tenor traded, not just benchmarks.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(granularity='observed', min_trades=1, provider='cftc')
# Build from a single day's file instead of a search window.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(source='slice', provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap curve. Each maps to that currency's overnight benchmark rate. Currencies whose overnight index swaps are too thinly reported to bootstrap a curve are not offered. CNY builds from FR007 fixed-float swaps, backstopped by the CFETS daily bulletin's traded curve.

**curve_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* par<br/>
Which representation of the curve to return in `rate`: the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. The forward curve is a separate endpoint, `ois_forward_curve`.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency, which still leaves sparse tenors missing.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects the most recent day on or before it that priced this currency, defaulting to the latest. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 7<br/>
Number of dissemination days to look back over, ending on `date`. With source='search' a longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days` and cap it with `max_staleness_days`. A thinly traded currency reaches a full curve only over a long window - the search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon. With source='slice' it is how far back to walk for the most recent day that priced this currency.

**max_staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Drop any node whose freshest print is older than this many days, measured from the curve's own date. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago in a different rate regime; capping staleness keeps the curve current rather than a mosaic of old levels. Only meaningful with source='search'. None keeps every live node and reports its age in `staleness_days`. Nodes that have already matured by the curve date are always dropped, cap or none.

**granularity**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* benchmark<br/>
Tenor axis of the curve. 'benchmark' snaps trades to standard nodes; 'observed' emits a node for every distinct tenor traded, including broken dates.

**aggregation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* median<br/>
How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate. Median is the default because notionals above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap, which biases notional-weighted averages.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades on their as-of day. The default keeps every node, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is. Raise it to admit only nodes several trades agree on, at the cost of losing the tenors a thin currency never trades in depth on any single day.

**cleared**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Keep only centrally cleared or intent-to-clear trades, dropping the bilateral uncleared prints that carry most of the off-market noise. Most useful with granularity='observed', where thin nodes are exposed to it.

**interpolation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* log_linear<br/>
How discount factors are interpolated between pillars, on the log of the discount factor. 'log_linear' is piecewise linear, giving piecewise-flat instantaneous forwards. 'log_cubic' is a monotone Hermite cubic, giving smooth forwards without overshooting into negative rates.

**overnight_anchor**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Anchor the curve's front end with the benchmark's latest published overnight fixing, as a 1-day node. The fixing is a realized rate, so the node carries no trades and its own as-of date.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcOisCurve`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve, being that of its freshest node.

**currency**: `str`<br/>
Currency of the curve.

**benchmark**: `str`<br/>
Overnight benchmark rate the swaps reference (SOFR, ESTR, ...).

**index**: `str`<br/>
Curve index plotted on the chart and used as the row index: the tenor label under 'benchmark' granularity, else the node's maturity date under 'observed' granularity.

**as_of_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the node's trades were reported on. Nodes are priced from the most recent day that cleared min_trades, so a thin tenor is dated earlier than a deep one.

**staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Days between the node's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest nodes.

**tenor**: `str`<br/>
Tenor of the curve node.

**tenor_days**: `int`<br/>
Tenor of the node, in days.

**tenor_years**: `float`<br/>
Tenor of the node, in years, on an ACT/365F basis.

**maturity_date**: `date`<br/>
Maturity date implied by the node's tenor, from its as-of date. Under 'observed' granularity this is also the curve's index.

**rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Rate of the selected `curve_type` at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%): the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. In percent rather than a decimal so the chart axis reads as a rate - the grid formatter is not applied to the chart. Omitted where the bootstrap degenerates.

**curve_type**: `str`<br/>
Which representation `rate` holds: par or zero.

**discount_factor**: `float | None`<br/>
Discount factor bootstrapped to the node's maturity.

**day_count**: `str | None`<br/>
Fixed-leg day count convention the node's trades reported, used to accrue the fixed leg in the bootstrap. ACT/360 for USD, EUR, CHF, MXN, COP and CLP; ACT/365F for GBP, JPY, CAD, SGD, INR, ZAR, THB, ILS, AUD and NZD. BRL reports BUS/252, recovered to the same year fraction on calendar days.

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Number of executed trades aggregated into the node.

**total_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Sum of the leg 1 notional of the node's trades.

**min_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Lowest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

**max_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Highest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

**is_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether any trade at the node had its notional disseminated at the reporting cap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get an overnight index swap curve over time, as a date-by-tenor table.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.ois_curve_history(provider='cftc')
# Track benchmark tenors over time.
obb.cftc.ois_curve_history(tenor='2Y,5Y,10Y,30Y', provider='cftc')
# Get the history of bootstrapped SONIA zero rates, in long form.
obb.cftc.ois_curve_history(currency='GBP', measure='zero_rate', pivot=False, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap curve.

**start_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Start date of the history. Default is 30 days before the end date. Files are retained for 366 days.

**end_date**: `date | None`<br/>
End date of the history. Default is the most recent date published.

**measure**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* par_rate<br/>
Curve measure to return for each tenor.

**tenor**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Filter to specific benchmark tenors. Default is all tenors. E.g., '2Y,5Y,10Y'. Multiple items allowed.

**aggregation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* median<br/>
How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades on a given date. The default keeps every node, because one executed trade is still a price.

**interpolation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* log_linear<br/>
How discount factors are interpolated between pillars, on the log of the discount factor. 'log_linear' is piecewise linear; 'log_cubic' is a monotone Hermite cubic giving smooth forwards. Only affects zero_rate, discount_factor and forward_rate, not par_rate.

**pivot**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Return a date-by-tenor table. Set to False for flat, long-form rows.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily files locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

title: "ois_forward_curve"
description: "Get the forward par swap rate curve, by forward start date"
keywords:
- cftc
- ois_forward_curve
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/ois_forward_curve - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the forward par swap rate curve, by forward start date.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.ois_forward_curve(provider='cftc')
# Plot the 5Y forward rate at yearly start dates.
obb.cftc.ois_forward_curve(forward_tenor='5Y', forward_step='1Y', provider='cftc')
# Get the next ten years of the SONIA 1Y forward.
obb.cftc.ois_forward_curve(currency='GBP', forward_tenor='1Y', forward_step='1Y', forward_count=10, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap curve.

**forward_tenor**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1Y<br/>
Length of the forward swap - the tenor of the swap priced at each forward start date. Independent of the spacing between starts.

**forward_step**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3M<br/>
Spacing between forward start dates. Set it apart from `forward_tenor` to plot, say, the 5Y forward at yearly starts (forward_tenor='5Y', forward_step='1Y').

**forward_count**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of forward start dates to plot. Defaults to the whole curve out to its last pillar; set it to plot only the first N steps (e.g. 10 with a 1Y step is the next ten years of the forward).

**method**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* implied<br/>
How the forward rates are formed. 'implied' reads them off the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson fit of the bootstrapped spot curve. 'observed' takes the fixed rates of the forward-starting swaps of the tenor directly, medianed by start and smoothed onto the grid - the market's own forward quotes, which reach only as far as that forward has traded.

**source**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* search<br/>
Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days; 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC). Ends the search window, or selects the most recent slice on or before it that priced this currency. History is retained for 366 days.

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 7<br/>
Days to look back over: the search window with source='search', or how far to walk back for the most recent priced day with source='slice'. The search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon, so a thin currency can fill its forwards from a full year of prints.

**max_staleness_days**: `int | None`<br/>
Drop any underlying node whose freshest print is older than this many days. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago; capping staleness keeps the forward strip current. Only meaningful with source='search'.

**aggregation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* median<br/>
How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades.

**interpolation**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* log_linear<br/>
Discount-factor interpolation for the bootstrap the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson forward fit is drawn from.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcOisForwardCurve`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**date**: `date | str`<br/>
Date of the curve.

**currency**: `str`<br/>
Currency of the curve.

**index**: `str`<br/>
Forward start date of the swap - the row and chart index.

**tenor**: `str`<br/>
The forward swap and its start, e.g. '1Y @ 5.00Y' (a 1Y swap 5Y out).

**start_years**: `float`<br/>
Forward start of the swap, in years. 0 is spot.

**forward_rate**: `float`<br/>
Forward par swap rate, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

**extrapolated**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the swap's tail ran past the last pillar, extended by the fit.

**num_trades**: `int`<br/>
Trades behind the curve nodes spanning this forward's start-to-tenor span, or the nearest node's when none fall inside it.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get the central bank's expected overnight-rate path from forward-starting OIS.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>

**date**: `date | None`<br/>

**lookback_days**: `int | None`<br/>

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 3<br/>
Drop a forward start priced by fewer than this many trades across the window. The default trims the one-off prints that are not meeting nodes.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>

---
title: "swap_summary"
description: "Summarize a disseminated swap's net economics on the current curve"
keywords:
- cftc
- swap_summary
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/swap_summary - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Summarize a disseminated swap's net economics on the current curve.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.swap_summary(provider='cftc')
# Summarize a specific disseminated print's net economics.
obb.cftc.swap_summary(currency='USD', dissemination_identifier='4339565190000000401', provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap, priced off that currency's reported rate curve - its OIS, or its fixed-vs-floating IRS when it has no OIS (CNY, TWD, MYR, ...).

**dissemination_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
The disseminated trade to value, as printed on the Swap Transactions tape. Any non-matured print is valuable by its own identifier. Default is the day's largest standalone par print; a package leg or off-par print's rate may reflect a package structure rather than a market level, flagged `is_vanilla_par` in the metadata rather than excluded.

**trade_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the trade printed on (UTC). Default is the curve date, today's tape; an older print is looked up on the day it was disseminated and valued on its remaining life against the current curve. Slices are retained for 366 days.

**side**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* pay<br/>
Whether the position pays or receives the fixed rate. The net present value is signed to this side; dissemination does not say which side either counterparty took.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
*Default:* 0.0<br/>
Only consider prints at least this large when defaulting to the day's largest. Ignored when a dissemination identifier is given.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC) of the trades and the rate curve. Default is the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Minimum trades for a curve node. The default keeps every traded tenor, because thin EM curves would otherwise lose their pillars.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcSwapSummary`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**metric**: `str`<br/>
Name of the summary metric.

**value**: `str`<br/>
Value of the summary metric, formatted in its own unit.

**detail**: `str | None`<br/>
Context the metric carries beyond its value.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "swap_trades"
description: "Get swap transaction and pricing data disseminated by DTCC"
keywords:
- cftc
- swap_trades
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="cftc/swap_trades - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get swap transaction and pricing data disseminated by DTCC.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.swap_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get USD SOFR swap transactions reported on a given date.
obb.cftc.swap_trades(asset_class='rates', currency='USD', underlier='SOFR', action_type='NEWT', provider='cftc')
# Get large cleared credit transactions.
obb.cftc.swap_trades(asset_class='credits', cleared='Y', min_notional=50000000, provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**asset_class**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* rates<br/>
Asset class of the transactions. Only the two priceable classes are offered: rates, valued against the DTCC-reported curve, and forex. Credit index prints have their own CDS Index Trades endpoint.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start of the report-date window (UTC). Default is the end date, a single day. Every day in the window is a separately published file, so a long window is a proportionally larger download.

**end_date**: `date | None`<br/>
End of the report-date window (UTC). Default is the most recent date whose file holds transactions matching the query; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Retained 366 days.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by the leg 1 notional currency. E.g., 'USD'.

**underlier**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by UPI underlier name, matched as a case-insensitive substring. E.g., 'SOFR'.

**upi_fisn**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by UPI FISN, matched as a case-insensitive substring. E.g., 'Swap OIS'.

**ticker**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. E.g., 'QZXQ4R16245X' for a SOFR OIS. The window is answered by the source's search API, one filtered query across the date range, cached per day.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by action type. E.g., 'NEWT' for new trades.

**cleared**: `bool | None`<br/>
Filter by whether the transaction is centrally cleared. True keeps cleared and intent-to-clear trades (Cleared 'Y' or 'I'); False keeps bilateral trades (Cleared 'N').

**trade_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by trade-type family, for the rates asset class: 'spot' and 'forward' are single-currency fixed-vs-floating swaps in a recognized curve family, split by whether the trade has already started; 'basis' floats two indices in the same currency against each other; 'cross_currency' floats two different currencies; 'inflation' is a zero-coupon swap of a fixed breakeven against a published price index. Ignored outside the rates asset class.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Filter out transactions with a leg 1 notional below this amount.

**max_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
Filter out transactions with a leg 1 notional above this amount.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of transactions to return. Default is all matching.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcSwapTrades`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

Value a disseminated swap on its own printed terms against the rate curve.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(provider='cftc')
# Value a specific disseminated print against today's curve.
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(currency='USD', dissemination_identifier='4339565190000000401', provider='cftc')
# Value the largest CNY print off its fixed-float IRS curve.
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(currency='CNY', provider='cftc')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* USD<br/>
Currency of the swap, priced off that currency's reported rate curve - its OIS, or its fixed-vs-floating IRS when it has no OIS (CNY, TWD, MYR, ...).

**dissemination_identifier**: `str | None`<br/>
The disseminated trade to value, as printed on the Swap Transactions tape. Any non-matured print is valuable by its own identifier. Default is the day's largest standalone par print; a package leg or off-par print's rate may reflect a package structure rather than a market level, flagged `is_vanilla_par` in the metadata rather than excluded.

**trade_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date the trade printed on (UTC). Default is the curve date, today's tape; an older print is looked up on the day it was disseminated and valued on its remaining life against the current curve. Slices are retained for 366 days.

**side**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* pay<br/>
Whether the position pays or receives the fixed rate. The net present value is signed to this side; dissemination does not say which side either counterparty took.

**min_notional**: `float | None`<br/>
*Default:* 0.0<br/>
Only consider prints at least this large when defaulting to the day's largest. Ignored when a dissemination identifier is given.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Dissemination date (UTC) of the trades and the rate curve. Default is the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

**min_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Minimum trades for a curve node. The default keeps every traded tenor, because thin EM curves would otherwise lose their pillars.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CftcSwapValuation`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='cftc' label='cftc'>

**period**: `int`<br/>
Coupon period, ordered from the first payment to maturity.

**start_date**: `date | str`<br/>
Start of the accrual period.

**payment_date**: `date`<br/>
Payment date at the end of the accrual period.

**year_fraction**: `float`<br/>
Accrual year fraction of the period, on the currency's money-market day count.

**discount_factor**: `float`<br/>
Discount factor to the payment date, off the bootstrapped curve.

**forward_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Curve-implied forward rate for the period, in percent. Reported on the fixed leg's rows where the floating leg's periods align with them.

**floating_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Floating rate applied to the period, in percent - the curve's implied forward plus the contract spread.

**notional**: `float`<br/>
Notional outstanding over the period, as the trade reported it - an amortising schedule steps down.

**fixed_rate**: `float`<br/>
Fixed rate applied to the period, in percent - the rate the trade printed at.

**fixed_cashflow**: `float`<br/>
Fixed-leg cash flow paid at the payment date.

**fixed_pv**: `float`<br/>
Present value of the fixed-leg cash flow.

**floating_cashflow**: `float | None`<br/>
Floating-leg cash flow at the period's forward rate.

**floating_pv**: `float | None`<br/>
Present value of the floating-leg cash flow.

**index_ratio**: `float | None`<br/>
Total index ratio applied to the period on an inflation swap - the reference index at maturity over the trade's base index.

**realized_ratio**: `float | None`<br/>
The part of the index ratio already fixed by published index levels, on a seasoned inflation swap.

**projected_ratio**: `float | None`<br/>
The part of the index ratio still projected off the curve's forward breakeven, on an inflation swap.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get the term structure of a Deribit underlying's dated futures.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# The current BTC futures term structure.
obb.deribit.futures.curve(symbol='BTC', provider='deribit')
# The curve against where it stood a day ago.
obb.deribit.futures.curve(symbol='BTC', hours_ago=24, provider='deribit')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
A specific date to get data for.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='deribit' label='deribit'>

**symbol**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* BTC<br/>
Symbol to get data for. The underlying root, as it appears in the instrument name.

**date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
A specific date to get data for.

**hours_ago**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Compare the current curve against how it stood this many hours ago. Multiple items allowed.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

**results**: `DeribitFuturesCurve`

Serializable results.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
The price of the futures contract.

The date of the data.

**expiration**: `str`<br/>
Futures expiration month.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
The price of the futures contract, taken from the mark.

**symbol**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the contract.

**last_price**: `float | None`<br/>
The price the contract last traded at, which on a thin contract can be a long way from the mark the curve is built on.

**hours_ago**: `int | None`<br/>
How many hours back the price was read, when the query asked for one.

Get candles for any listed Deribit instrument.

```python
from openbb import obb
# Daily candles for the BTC perpetual.
obb.deribit.futures.historical(symbol='BTC-PERPETUAL', provider='deribit')
# Hourly candles over a named span.
obb.deribit.futures.historical(symbol='BTC-PERPETUAL', interval='1h', start_date='2026-09-01', end_date='2026-09-15', provider='deribit')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): deribit.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**expiration**: `str | None`<br/>
Future expiry date with format YYYY-MM

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='deribit' label='deribit'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Any listed instrument works, not only futures. A perpetual can also be given by its shortened root, such as 'SOLUSDC'.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**expiration**: `str | None`<br/>
Future expiry date with format YYYY-MM

**interval**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1d<br/>
Time interval of the data to return.

- 1m
- 3m
- 5m
- 10m
- 15m
- 30m
- 1h
- 2h
- 3h
- 6h
- 12h
- 1d
</details>

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Get the Deribit prints that crossed, by instrument or across a currency.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# The most recent prints on the BTC perpetual.
obb.deribit.market.trades(symbol='BTC-PERPETUAL', provider='deribit')
# Every BTC option print over a span.
obb.deribit.market.trades(currency='BTC', kind='option', start_date='2026-09-01', end_date='2026-09-02', provider='deribit')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='deribit' label='deribit'>

**symbol**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
One or more instrument names. When given, the currency is ignored. Multiple items allowed.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* BTC<br/>
The settlement currency of the instruments.

**kind**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* future<br/>
The kind of instrument. Only used when reading by currency, where the exchange rejects a request that leaves it out, and where spot is not offered at all. Read spot trades by symbol instead.

**start_date**: `Any | None | str`<br/>
Return trades from this date onwards.

**end_date**: `Any | None | str`<br/>
Return trades up to this date.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 100<br/>
The number of trades to return, at most 1000.

**sorting**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* desc<br/>
The order the trades are returned in.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `DeribitTrades`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

The name of the instrument.

Which side the aggressor was on.

**price**: `float`<br/>
The price the trade printed at.

**amount**: `float | None`<br/>
The size of the trade, in base currency.

**contracts**: `float | None`<br/>
The size of the trade, in contracts.

**iv**: `float | None`<br/>
The volatility the option trade implies.

The price the exchange marked the instrument at.

The price of the index at the time of the trade.

How the price moved against the previous trade. 0 and 1 are upticks, 2 and 3 are downticks.

**volume**: `list[Union[int, float]]`<br/>
The volume of the session.

**theoretical_price**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The theoretical price of the contract. Deribit publishes none.

**last_trade_price**: `list[float]`<br/>
The price the contract last traded at.

**last_trade_size**: `list[Union[int, float]] | None`<br/>
The size of the last trade. Deribit publishes none.

**last_trade_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the last trade printed. Deribit publishes none.

**tick**: `list[str] | None`<br/>
The direction of the last price move. Deribit publishes none.

**bid**: `list[float]`<br/>
The highest price bid.

**bid_size**: `list[Union[int, float]]`<br/>
The size resting at the best bid.

**bid_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the bid was published. Deribit publishes none.

**bid_exchange**: `list[str] | None`<br/>
The exchange the bid came from. Deribit publishes none.

**ask**: `list[float]`<br/>
The lowest price offered.

**ask_size**: `list[Union[int, float]]`<br/>
The size resting at the best offer.

**ask_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the offer was published. Deribit publishes none.

**ask_exchange**: `list[str] | None`<br/>
The exchange the offer came from. Deribit publishes none.

**mark**: `list[float]`<br/>
The mark price of the contract.

**open**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The opening price of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**open_bid**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The opening bid of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**open_ask**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The opening offer of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**high**: `list[float]`<br/>
The highest price of the session.

**bid_high**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The highest bid of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**ask_high**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The highest offer of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**low**: `list[float]`<br/>
The lowest price of the session.

**bid_low**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The lowest bid of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**ask_low**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The lowest offer of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**close**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The closing price of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**close_size**: `list[Union[int, float]] | None`<br/>
The size of the closing trade. Deribit publishes none.

**close_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the closing trade printed. Deribit publishes none.

**close_bid**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The closing bid of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**close_bid_size**: `list[Union[int, float]] | None`<br/>
The size at the closing bid. Deribit publishes none.

**close_bid_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the closing bid was published. Deribit publishes none.

**close_ask**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The closing offer of the session. Deribit publishes none.

**close_ask_size**: `list[Union[int, float]] | None`<br/>
The size at the closing offer. Deribit publishes none.

**close_ask_time**: `list[datetime] | None`<br/>
When the closing offer was published. Deribit publishes none.

**prev_close**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The closing price of the previous session. Deribit publishes none.

**change**: `list[float] | None`<br/>
The price change over the session. Deribit publishes none.

**change_percent**: `list[float]`<br/>
The price change over the session.

**implied_volatility**: `list[float]`<br/>
The volatility implied by the mark price.

**delta**: `list[float]`<br/>
The sensitivity to the underlying's price.

**gamma**: `list[float]`<br/>
The sensitivity of delta to the underlying's price.

**theta**: `list[float]`<br/>
The sensitivity to the passage of time.

**vega**: `list[float]`<br/>
The sensitivity to implied volatility.

**rho**: `list[float]`<br/>
The sensitivity to the interest rate.

**volume_notional**: `list[float]`<br/>
The notional volume of the contract, in USD or USDC.

**bid_iv**: `list[float]`<br/>
The volatility implied by the bid price.

**ask_iv**: `list[float]`<br/>
The volatility implied by the ask price.

**interest_rate**: `list[float]`<br/>
The rate the exchange prices the greeks at.

**settlement_price**: `list[float]`<br/>
The price the contract last settled at.

**min_price**: `list[float]`<br/>
The lowest price an order will be accepted at.

**max_price**: `list[float]`<br/>
The highest price an order will be accepted at.

**underlying_spot_price**: `list[float]`<br/>
The spot price of the underlying the option is based on.

**is_inverse**: `list[bool] | None`<br/>
Whether the contract settles in the underlying rather than in the quote currency, which changes how its payoff is valued.

**timestamp**: `list[datetime]`<br/>
When the quote was published, as America/New_York time.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "optimizer"
description: "Rank every combo structure against a view on the underlying"
keywords:
- deribit
- options
- optimizer
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="deribit/options/optimizer - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Rank every combo structure against a view on the underlying.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Rank strategies for a move to 100,000 by year end.
obb.deribit.options.optimizer(symbol='BTC', target_price=100000, target_date='2026-12-25')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* BTC<br/>
The underlying root, as it appears in the instrument name.

**target_price**: `float`<br/>
The price the underlying is expected to reach.

**target_date**: `str`<br/>
When it is expected to reach it.

**budget**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 5000.0<br/>
The capital to put at risk, in the quote currency. Each position is sized so its worst loss across a threefold move either way is this much.

**limit**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 40<br/>
How many structures to return, each at its best strikes.

**legs**: `str`<br/>
The strategy picked from the Legs column, shared with the payoff chart. It does not change the ranking.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `Any`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="deribit/options/payoff - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Draw what one position returns across a range of underlying prices.

 Raises
 ------
 HTTPException
 If the expiration lists no strategy, or does not list the position.

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* BTC<br/>
The underlying root, as it appears in the instrument name.

**target_price**: `float`<br/>
The price the underlying is expected to reach.

**target_date**: `str`<br/>
When it is expected to reach it.

**budget**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 5000.0<br/>
The capital to put at risk, in the quote currency. Each position is sized so its worst loss across a threefold move either way is this much.

**legs**: `str`<br/>
The contracts to draw, as 'Buy SYMBOL / Sell 2 SYMBOL'. Click the Legs cell of a strategy in the optimizer to set it, or pick one here. Left empty, the best strategy for the view is drawn.

**raw**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
**theme**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* dark<br/>
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get the multi-leg structures Deribit lists, one row per leg.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb

obb.deribit.reference.combos(currency='BTC', provider='deribit')
```

**end_date**: `Any | None | str`<br/>
Return candles up to this date.

**interval**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1d<br/>
Time interval of the data to return.

**reference_area**: `str | None`<br/>

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 500<br/>
Maximum number of series to return (None or &lt;=0 returns all).

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Use the parsed-data disk cache for the enumerated series.

**symbol**: `str | None`<br/>
Dummy field so a clicked series can group by symbol.

---
title: "eligible_assets"
description: "Get the Eurosystem list of eligible marketable assets"
keywords:
- ecb
- eligible_assets
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="ecb/eligible_assets - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the Eurosystem list of eligible marketable assets.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.ecb.eligible_assets(provider='ecb', currency='EUR', limit=10)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='ecb' label='ecb'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Snapshot date. Defaults to the latest available business day.

**isin**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Filter by one or more ISIN codes. Multiple items allowed.

**asset_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by asset type (e.g. 'Bond').

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- Bond
- Medium-term note
- Treasury bill / commercial paper / certificate of deposit
- EEA legislative covered bond
- Asset-backed security (ABS)
- Multi-cédulas
- Non-EEA G10 legislative covered bond
</details>

**haircut_category**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by Eurosystem haircut (liquidity) category.

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- Category I – central government, EU, central banks
- Category II – regional/local govt, agencies, supranationals, covered bonds
- Category III – corporate and other issuers
- Category IV – unsecured credit-institution debt
- Category V – asset-backed securities
</details>

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by denomination currency (e.g. 'EUR').

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- EUR
- USD
- GBP
- JPY
- ATS
- DEM
- HRK
- SKK
</details>

**issuer_group**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by issuer group (e.g. 'Central government').

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- Central bank
- Central government
- Corporate and other issuers
- Credit institution (excluding agencies)
- Regional/local government
- Supranational issuer
- Agency – non-credit institution
- Agency – credit institution
- Financial corporation other than credit institution
- Public corporation
</details>

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Limit the number of assets returned.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
If true, cache the parsed list on disk for the dataset TTL.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `EcbEligibleAssets`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='ecb' label='ecb'>

**isin**: `str`<br/>
International Securities Identification Number.

**asset_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Asset type.

**haircut_category**: `str | None`<br/>
Eurosystem haircut (liquidity) category.

**haircut**: `float | None`<br/>
Valuation haircut, in percent.

**haircut_own_use**: `float | None`<br/>
Own-use valuation haircut, in percent.

**reference_market**: `str | None`<br/>
Reference market.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Denomination currency.

**coupon_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Coupon rate, percent.

**coupon_definition**: `str | None`<br/>
Coupon definition (Fixed, Variable, or Zero).

title: "autocorrelation"
description: "Learn how to perform the Durbin-Watson test for autocorrelation in Python.  Understand the parameters and return value of the function, and how to use exogenous  variables in the analysis. This documentation provides a detailed explanation."
keywords:
- Durbin-Watson test
- autocorrelation
- Python
- data analysis
- exogenous variables
- parameter
- return
- documentation
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/autocorrelation - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Perform the Durbin-Watson test for autocorrelation in regression residuals.

The Durbin-Watson statistic ranges from 0 to 4. A value near 2 suggests no
autocorrelation; values toward 0 indicate positive autocorrelation and values
toward 4 indicate negative autocorrelation.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.autocorrelation(y_column='close', x_columns=['open', 'high', 'low'], data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**y_column**: `str`<br/>
Name of the dependent (target) column.

**x_columns**: `list[str]`<br/>
Names of the independent (exogenous) columns.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `AutocorrelationData`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**durbin_watson**: `float`<br/>
Durbin-Watson statistic (near 2 = no autocorrelation).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Perform the Granger causality test to assess whether X helps predict y.

Granger causality tests whether past values of one series improve the forecast of
another. It is a predictive, not a structural, notion of causality.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Granger causality test with mock data.
obb.econometrics.causality(y_column='close', x_column='open', lag=1, data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

title: "cointegration"
description: "Learn how to use the two-step Engle-Granger test to show co-integration  between two time series in Python. Explore the parameters, input dataset, data columns,  and the OBBject returned with the test results."
keywords:
- co-integration
- Engle-Granger test
- time series
- data
- columns
- cointegration
- maxlag
- Python

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/cointegration - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Test pairs of time series for cointegration via the Engle-Granger two-step test.

Cointegration means two non-stationary series share a long-run equilibrium. The
Engle-Granger test regresses one series on the other and checks the residuals for
stationarity.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.cointegration(columns=['open', 'close'], data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**columns**: `list[str]`<br/>
Columns to test pairwise for cointegration.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[CointegrationData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**pair**: `str`<br/>
The tested column pair, formatted as 'x/y'.

**c**: `float`<br/>
Constant of the long-run relationship.

**gamma**: `float`<br/>
Slope of the long-run relationship.

**alpha**: `float`<br/>
Error-correction speed of adjustment.

**adf_stat**: `float`<br/>
Dickey-Fuller statistic on the residuals.

**p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Dickey-Fuller statistic.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/cointegration_johansen - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Perform the Johansen cointegration test on multiple time series.

The Johansen test detects cointegrating relationships among two or more series
simultaneously, reporting the number of cointegrating vectors via the trace and
maximum-eigenvalue statistics.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.cointegration_johansen(columns=['open', 'close'], data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**columns**: `list[str]`<br/>
Columns (time series) to test jointly for cointegration.

**deterministic_order**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 0<br/>
Deterministic trend: -1 none, 0 constant, 1 constant and trend.

**k_ar_diff**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Number of lagged differences in the model.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Serializable results.

Trace test statistic.

title: "correlation_matrix"
description: "Learn how to get the correlation matrix of an input dataset using Python.  Find information on the parameters and return value of the function."
keywords:
- correlation matrix
- input dataset
- Python
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/correlation_matrix - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the correlation matrix of an input dataset.

The correlation matrix shows how strongly the variables in the dataset move in
relation to one another. Scores range from -1 (perfect negative correlation) through
0 (no correlation) to 1 (perfect positive correlation).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the correlation matrix of a dataset.
stock_data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='TSLA', start_date='2023-01-01', provider='fmp').to_df()
obb.econometrics.correlation_matrix(data=stock_data)
obb.econometrics.correlation_matrix(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**method**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* pearson<br/>
Correlation method: 'pearson' (standard), 'kendall' (Kendall Tau), or 'spearman' (rank correlation).

**min_periods**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Minimum number of observations required per pair of columns to compute a correlation.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>

title: "garch"
description: "Fit a configurable volatility model from the GARCH family to a series"
keywords:
- econometrics
- garch
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/garch - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Fit a configurable volatility model from the GARCH family to a series.

The mean model, volatility process, lag orders, power, and innovation distribution
are all configurable. The estimated conditional volatility series is returned; the
fitted parameters and information criteria are attached to ``OBBject.extra``. Best
applied to a return series.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.garch(column='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**column**: `str`<br/>
Column to model. Best applied to a return series.

**x_columns**: `list[str]`<br/>
Exogenous regressor columns for the mean model (used by the 'LS', 'ARX', and 'HARX' mean models).

**mean**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* Constant<br/>
Mean model: 'Constant' (constant mean), 'Zero' (zero mean), 'LS' (least squares), 'AR'/'ARX' (autoregressive, 'ARX' adds exogenous regressors), 'HAR'/'HARX' (heterogeneous autoregressive).

**lags**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 0<br/>
Lag order of the 'AR', 'ARX', 'HAR', and 'HARX' mean models.

**vol**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* GARCH<br/>
Volatility process: 'GARCH', 'ARCH', 'EGARCH' (exponential GARCH, captures leverage), 'FIGARCH' (fractionally integrated, long memory), 'APARCH' (asymmetric power ARCH), 'HARCH' (heterogeneous ARCH).

**p**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Order of the symmetric ARCH (innovation) term.

**o**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 0<br/>
Order of the asymmetric (leverage) term.

**q**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Order of the lagged volatility (GARCH) term.

**power**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 2.0<br/>
Power applied to the conditional volatility (2.0 is standard GARCH; other values give power-GARCH and APARCH variants).

**distribution**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* normal<br/>
Distribution of the model innovations: 'normal' (Gaussian), 't' (Student's t, fat tails), 'skewt' (skewed Student's t), or 'ged' (generalized error distribution).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[GarchData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | datetime | int | str`<br/>
Observation date (integer position when the input has no date).

**conditional_volatility**: `float`<br/>
Estimated conditional volatility at the observation.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "heteroskedasticity"
description: "Perform the Breusch-Pagan and White tests for heteroskedasticity"
keywords:
- econometrics
- heteroskedasticity
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/heteroskedasticity - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Perform the Breusch-Pagan and White tests for heteroskedasticity.

Heteroskedasticity - non-constant variance of the regression residuals - violates a
key OLS assumption and makes standard errors unreliable. The Breusch-Pagan test
detects linear forms; the White test additionally captures non-linear forms.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.heteroskedasticity(y_column='close', x_columns=['open', 'high', 'low'], data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**y_column**: `str`<br/>
Name of the dependent (target) column.

**x_columns**: `list[str]`<br/>
Names of the independent (exogenous) columns.

**robust**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Use the robust (studentized Koenker) Breusch-Pagan variant, which does not assume normally distributed residuals.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `HeteroskedasticityData`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**breusch_pagan_lm_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Breusch-Pagan LM statistic.

**breusch_pagan_lm_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Breusch-Pagan LM statistic.

**breusch_pagan_f_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Breusch-Pagan F statistic.

**breusch_pagan_f_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Breusch-Pagan F statistic.

**white_lm_statistic**: `float`<br/>
White LM statistic.

**white_lm_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the White LM statistic.

**white_f_statistic**: `float`<br/>
White F statistic.

**white_f_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the White F statistic.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="econometrics/kpss - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Perform the KPSS test for stationarity.

The KPSS null hypothesis is that the series IS stationary - the opposite of the ADF
test - so running both tests gives a more robust read on stationarity.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.econometrics.kpss(column='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**column**: `str`<br/>
Column to test.

**regression**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* c<br/>
Null hypothesis: 'c' level-stationary, 'ct' trend-stationary.

**nlags**: `int | str`<br/>
*Default:* auto<br/>
Lags for the variance estimator: 'auto', 'legacy', or an explicit non-negative integer.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>
