## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Target periodic return series (index column plus the target column).

**factors_data**: `list[Data]`<br/>
Factor return matrix (index column plus one column per factor), in the same units as the target.

**periods**: `list[str]`<br/>
Named look-back periods to regress over, anchored to the latest factor observation. Supported values: '1 Month', '3 Month', 'YTD', '1 Year', '3 Year', 'Max'.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Name of the return column in `data` to regress on the factor matrix.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Name of the index column shared by `data` and `factors_data`.

**risk_free_column**: `str`<br/>
Optional name of the risk-free rate column in `factors_data`. When provided, the target is regressed in excess form (target minus the risk-free column) and the column itself is dropped from the regressors.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[FactorRegressionData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**period**: `str`<br/>
Look-back period the regression was run over.

**factor**: `str`<br/>
Factor name (or 'const' for the regression intercept).

**coefficient**: `float`<br/>
OLS coefficient estimate for the factor.

**p_value**: `float`<br/>
Two-sided p-value of the coefficient estimate.

**lower_ci**: `float`<br/>
Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval.

**upper_ci**: `float`<br/>
Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval.

**r_squared**: `float`<br/>
R-squared of the regression for this period (repeated per row).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "normality"
description: "Learn about normality statistics and their significance in data analysis.  Discover different techniques such as kurtosis, skewness, Jarque-Bera, Shapiro-Wilk,  and Kolmogorov-Smirnov for evaluating normality in time series data. Explore how  these tests can help determine if a data sample follows a normal distribution."
keywords:
- normality statistics
- kurtosis
- skewness
- Jarque-Bera
- Shapiro-Wilk
- Kolmogorov-Smirnov
- time series data
- target column
- normality tests
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/normality - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get normality statistics for a data series.

Runs the kurtosis, skewness, Jarque-Bera, Shapiro-Wilk, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov
tests, each assessing whether the sample is drawn from a normal distribution.
Returns the test statistic and p-value for every test.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.quantitative.normality(target='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**target**: `str`<br/>
Name of the column to analyze.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `NormalityData`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**kurtosis_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Kurtosis test statistic.

**kurtosis_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the kurtosis test.

**skewness_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Skewness test statistic.

**skewness_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the skewness test.

**jarque_bera_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Jarque-Bera test statistic.

**jarque_bera_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Jarque-Bera test.

**shapiro_wilk_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Shapiro-Wilk test statistic.

**shapiro_wilk_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Shapiro-Wilk test.

**kolmogorov_smirnov_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistic against a normal distribution with the sample mean and variance (Lilliefors test).

**kolmogorov_smirnov_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the Lilliefors-corrected Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, bounded to the range 0.001 to 0.99.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "omega_ratio"
description: "Calculate the Omega ratio of a periodic return series across return thresholds"
keywords:
- quantitative
- performance
- omega_ratio
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/performance/omega_ratio - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate the Omega ratio of a periodic return series across return thresholds.

The Omega ratio measures the probability-weighted gains above a threshold relative
to the losses below it. Each annualized threshold is converted to a per-period
threshold assuming 252 periods per year. The ratio is evaluated at `bins`
thresholds spanning the requested range, giving a profile of risk and reward
rather than a single number.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.quantitative.performance.omega_ratio(target='return', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'return': 0.01}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'return': 0.01}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'return': 0.01}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'return': 0.01}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'return': 0.01}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**target**: `str`<br/>
Name of the periodic return column to analyze.

**threshold_start**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 0.0<br/>
Lower bound of the annualized return-threshold range, as a decimal fraction.

**threshold_end**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 1.5<br/>
Upper bound of the annualized return-threshold range, as a decimal fraction.

**bins**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 50<br/>
Number of evenly spaced thresholds to evaluate.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[OmegaRatioData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**threshold**: `float`<br/>
Annualized return threshold the ratio is evaluated at.

**omega**: `float`<br/>
Omega ratio at the threshold.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Calculate the rolling annualized Sharpe ratio of a price series.

The prices are converted to periodic returns. In each rolling window, the mean

---
title: "sortino_ratio"
description: "Calculate the rolling annualized Sortino ratio of a price series"
keywords:
- quantitative
- performance
- sortino_ratio
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/performance/sortino_ratio - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate the rolling annualized Sortino ratio of a price series.

The prices are converted to periodic returns. In each rolling window, the mean
return in excess of the minimum acceptable return is divided by the downside
deviation below that return and annualized assuming 252 periods per year. When
adjusted, the ratio is scaled by 1/sqrt(2) so it can be compared directly with
the Sharpe ratio.

Examples
--------

---
title: "risk_decomposition"
description: "Decompose Var(target) into per-factor contributions plus residual variance"
keywords:
- quantitative
- risk_decomposition
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/risk_decomposition - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Decompose Var(target) into per-factor contributions plus residual variance.

For each look-back period, runs OLS of the target on the factor matrix and
splits the target's variance via the additive identity
`Var(target) = sum_i beta_i * Cov(factor_i, target) + Var(residual)`.
Returned shares sum to 1 per period: factor shares sum to R^2 and the residual
row holds `1 - R^2`. Handles correlated factors cleanly because each share is
measured by the covariance with the target rather than by the factor's
standalone variance.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Target periodic return series (index column plus the target column).

**factors_data**: `list[Data]`<br/>
Factor return matrix (index column plus one column per factor), in the same units as the target.

**periods**: `list[str]`<br/>
Named look-back periods to decompose over, anchored to the latest factor observation.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Name of the return column in `data` to decompose against the factors.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Name of the index column shared by `data` and `factors_data`.

**risk_free_column**: `str`<br/>
Optional name of the risk-free rate column in `factors_data`. When provided, the target is converted to excess returns before decomposition and the column is dropped from the factor set.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[RiskDecompositionData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**period**: `str`<br/>
Look-back period the decomposition was run over.

**factor**: `str`<br/>
Factor name, or 'Residual' for the idiosyncratic component.

**contribution**: `float`<br/>
Covariance-based contribution to Var(target): for a factor, beta_i * Cov(factor_i, target); for 'Residual', Var(target) * (1 - R^2).

**share**: `float`<br/>
Fraction of Var(target) attributed to this factor (or to the residual). Factor shares sum to R^2; the residual share equals 1 - R^2.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "factors"
description: "Refit factor OLS on a rolling window and emit per-factor betas through time"
keywords:
- quantitative
- rolling
- factors
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/rolling/factors - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Refit factor OLS on a rolling window and emit per-factor betas through time.

For each window end at stride `step`, runs OLS of the target on the factor
matrix using the trailing `window` observations and records each factor's
coefficient and t-statistic. Suitable for visualizing time-varying factor
exposures and detecting regime shifts that named-window decompositions hide.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Roll a 1-year window stepping monthly across a multi-factor regression of `close` on the supplied factor matrix.
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Target periodic return series (index column plus the target column).

**factors_data**: `list[Data]`<br/>
Factor return matrix (index column plus one column per factor), in the same units as the target.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Name of the return column in `data` to regress on the factor matrix.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Name of the index column shared by `data` and `factors_data`.

**risk_free_column**: `str`<br/>
Optional name of the risk-free rate column in `factors_data`. When provided, the target is regressed in excess form and the column is dropped from the regressors.

**window**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 252<br/>
Number of observations in each rolling regression window.

**step**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 21<br/>
Stride between successive windows in observations. A value of 1 refits at every observation; larger values reduce cost on long histories.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

**results**: `list[RollingFactorsData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
End date of the rolling window.

**factor**: `str`<br/>
Factor name (or 'const' for the regression intercept).

**coefficient**: `float`<br/>
OLS coefficient estimate for the factor at this window end.

**t_statistic**: `float`<br/>
t-statistic for the coefficient at this window end.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "kurtosis"

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/rolling/kurtosis - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate the rolling kurtosis of a target column over a moving window.

Kurtosis measures the tailedness of a distribution. High kurtosis indicates heavy
tails and a higher risk of extreme outcomes, while low kurtosis indicates the
opposite.

Examples
--------

Calculate the rolling mean of a target column over a moving window.

The rolling mean is a simple moving average that smooths short-term fluctuations
and highlights longer-term trends or cycles in a time series.

Calculate the rolling quantile of a target column over a moving window.

Quantiles divide the range of a distribution into intervals with equal
probabilities. This command returns the rolling median alongside the requested
quantile for analyzing trends, outliers, and risk.

---
title: "stdev"
description: "Calculate the rolling standard deviation of a target column over a moving window"
keywords:
- quantitative
- rolling
- stdev
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/rolling/stdev - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate the rolling standard deviation of a target column over a moving window.

Standard deviation measures the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of
values. It is the square root of the variance and is widely used to assess risk.

Examples
--------

title: "kurtosis"

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/stats/kurtosis - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Compute the kurtosis of a target column.

Kurtosis measures the tailedness of a distribution. High kurtosis indicates heavy
tails and a higher risk of extreme outcomes, while low kurtosis indicates lighter
tails.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.quantitative.stats.kurtosis(target='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/stats/mean - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Compute the arithmetic mean of a target column.

The mean is the average of a set of values and is widely used to summarize the
central tendency of a time series.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.quantitative.stats.mean(target='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

title: "unitroot_test"
description: "Learn about the Unit Root Test function in Python, including the Augmented  Dickey-Fuller test and the Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin test. Explore the parameters,  such as data, target, fuller_reg, and kpss_reg, and understand how to interpret  the unit root tests summary."
keywords:
- Unit Root Test
- Augmented Dickey-Fuller test
- Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin test
- data
- target
- fuller_reg
- kpss_reg
- Time series data

- unit root tests summary
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="quantitative/unitroot_test - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get unit root test results for a data series.

Applies the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test, whose null hypothesis is the
presence of a unit root, and the Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin (KPSS) test,
whose null hypothesis is stationarity. Together they characterize whether the
series is stationary.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.quantitative.unitroot_test(target='close', data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input dataset.

**target**: `str`<br/>
Name of the column to analyze.

**fuller_reg**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* c<br/>
Constant/trend terms for the ADF test: 'c' constant, 'ct' constant and trend, 'ctt' constant, linear and quadratic trend, 'n' no constant or trend.

**kpss_reg**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* c<br/>
Null hypothesis for the KPSS test: 'c' level-stationary, 'ct' trend-stationary.

**maxlag**: `int`<br/>
Maximum lag for the ADF test. If None, a data-dependent default is used.

**autolag**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* AIC<br/>
Lag-selection method for the ADF test: 'AIC', 'BIC', or 't-stat'; None uses maxlag directly without selection.

**nlags**: `int | str`<br/>
*Default:* auto<br/>
Lags for the KPSS variance estimator: 'auto', 'legacy', or an explicit non-negative integer.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `UnitRootData`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**adf_statistic**: `float`<br/>
Augmented Dickey-Fuller test statistic.

**adf_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the ADF test.

**adf_nlags**: `int`<br/>
Number of lags used in the ADF test.

**adf_nobs**: `int`<br/>
Number of observations used in the ADF test.

**adf_icbest**: `float`<br/>
Best information criterion value of the ADF test (None when autolag is disabled).

**kpss_statistic**: `float`<br/>
KPSS test statistic.

**kpss_p_value**: `float`<br/>
p-value of the KPSS test.

**kpss_nlags**: `int`<br/>
Number of lags used in the KPSS test.

**kpss_p_value_interpolated**: `bool`<br/>
False when the KPSS p-value is clamped to a table boundary (the true p-value is more extreme than reported).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get the balance sheet for a given company.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.balance_sheet(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
obb.sec.balance_sheet(symbol='AAPL', period='annual', limit=5, provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return. For balance sheet, TTM is treated as the average of the last 4 quarters.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache (4-hour memory) for the SEC request. Defaults to True.

**include_preliminary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to include preliminary data from 8-K filings for periods not yet reported on 10-Q/K.

**pit_mode**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Point-in-time mode. When True, returns data as originally reported at the time of filing, without subsequent restatements or amendments. For annual data, uses the original 10-K values. For quarterly data, preserves 10-Q filing vintage instead of using restated comparatives from the 10-K.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get the growth of a company's balance sheet items over time.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.balance_sheet_growth(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
obb.sec.balance_sheet_growth(symbol='AAPL', limit=10, provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return. For balance sheet growth, 'quarterly_yoy' compares the most recent quarter to the same quarter in the prior year, and TTM compares the most recent quarter to the average of the same quarter and the three preceding quarters in the prior year.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache (4-hour memory) for the SEC request. Defaults to True.

**include_preliminary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to include preliminary data from 8-K filings for periods not yet reported on 10-Q/K.

**pit_mode**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Point-in-time mode. When True, returns data as originally reported at the time of filing, without subsequent restatements or amendments. For annual data, uses the original 10-K values. For quarterly data, preserves 10-Q filing vintage instead of using restated comparatives from the 10-K.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Get the 5%+ beneficial owners table from a company's proxy statement (DEF 14A).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.beneficial_ownership(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**calendar_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar year the proxy was filed. Defaults to the most recent.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Use the cache for downloaded filings. Default is True.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SecBeneficialOwnership`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**content**: `str`<br/>
The 5%+ beneficial owners table from the proxy (DEF 14A) as a formatted markdown table.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "cash_flow"
description: "Get the cash flow statement for a given company"
keywords:
- sec
- cash_flow
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="sec/cash_flow - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the cash flow statement for a given company.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.cash_flow(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
obb.sec.cash_flow(symbol='AAPL', period='annual', limit=5, provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 5<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 5<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache (4-hour memory) for the SEC request. Defaults to True.

**include_preliminary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to include preliminary data from 8-K filings for periods not yet reported on 10-Q/K.

**pit_mode**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Point-in-time mode. When True, returns data as originally reported at the time of filing, without subsequent restatements or amendments. For annual data, uses the original 10-K values. For quarterly data, preserves 10-Q filing vintage instead of using restated comparatives from the 10-K.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SecCashFlowStatement`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

**other_net_changes_in_cash**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount of other net changes in cash and cash equivalents not separately disclosed in the statement of cash flows.

**net_change_in_cash**: `float | None`<br/>
The increase (decrease) during the reporting period in cash and cash equivalents. While for technical reasons this element has no balance attribute, the default assumption is a debit balance consistent with its label.

**cash_at_beginning_of_period**: `float | None`<br/>
Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and restricted cash equivalents at the beginning of the reporting period. Derived from the previous period's ending balance.

**cash_at_end_of_period**: `float | None`<br/>
Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and restricted cash equivalents at the end of the reporting period.

**cash_interest_paid**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount of cash paid for interest, excluding capitalized interest, classified as operating activity. Includes, but is not limited to, payment to settle zero-coupon bond for accreted interest of debt discount and debt instrument with insignificant coupon interest rate in relation to effective interest rate of borrowing attributable to accreted interest of debt discount.

**cash_interest_received**: `float | None`<br/>
The cash inflow from interest received, classified as operating activities.

**cash_income_taxes_paid**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount, after refund, of cash paid to foreign, federal, state, and local jurisdictions as income tax.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "compare_company_facts"
description: "Compare reported company facts and fundamental data points"
keywords:
- sec
- compare_company_facts
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="sec/compare_company_facts - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Compare reported company facts and fundamental data points.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.compare_company_facts(provider='sec')
obb.sec.compare_company_facts(provider='sec', fact='PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock', year=2023)
obb.sec.compare_company_facts(provider='sec', symbol='NVDA,AAPL,AMZN,MSFT,GOOG,SMCI', fact='RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax', year=2024)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): sec.

**fact**: `str | None`<br/>
The fact to lookup, typically a GAAP-reporting measure. Choices vary by provider.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): sec.

**fact**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Revenues<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Fact or concept from the SEC taxonomy, in UpperCamelCase. Defaults to, 'Revenues'. AAPL, MSFT, GOOG, BRK-A currently report revenue as, 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax'. In previous years, they have reported as 'Revenues'.<br/>
Facts fall into two groups. Instantaneous balance-sheet concepts are measured at a point in time (e.g. 'Assets', 'Liabilities', 'StockholdersEquity', 'Goodwill', 'LongTermDebt'); the full set is openbb_sec.utils.definitions.INSTANT_FACTS. Everything else is a flow concept from the income or cash-flow statement, measured over a period (e.g. 'Revenues', 'NetIncomeLoss', 'NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities'). The 'instantaneous' parameter and the standalone-Q4 derivation apply only to flow concepts; balance-sheet concepts are always point-in-time, including the year-end (Q4) value.<br/>
</details>

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
The calendar year to retrieve the data for. If not provided, the current year is used. When symbol(s) are provided, excluding the year will return all reported values for the concept. Values are aligned by the calendar quarter/year of the period end, not the fiscal calendar.

**calendar_period**: `str | None`<br/>
The calendar period to retrieve the data for. Periods are aligned to the calendar quarter/year of the report period end, not the filer's fiscal calendar, so off-calendar filers stay comparable. If not provided, the most recent quarter is used. 'q1'-'q4' return standalone (3-month) quarters; the fourth quarter is derived as FY - 9-month. When a symbol is supplied, cumulative year-to-date values are reduced to standalone quarters.

<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Choices</summary>

- fy
- q1
- q2
- q3
- q4
</details>

**instantaneous**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Whether to retrieve instantaneous data. See the notes above for more information. Defaults to False. Some facts are only available as instantaneous data.<br/>
The function will automatically attempt the inverse of this parameter if the initial calendar quarter request fails. This parameter is ignored when a symbol is supplied.<br/>
</details>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache for the request. Defaults to True.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SecCompareCompanyFacts`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

**value**: `float`<br/>
The reported value of the fact or concept.

**reported_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date when the report was filed.

**period_beginning**: `date | None`<br/>
The start date of the reporting period.

The end date of the reporting period.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str | None`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the entity.

**value**: `float`<br/>
The reported value of the fact or concept.

**reported_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date when the report was filed.

**period_beginning**: `date | None`<br/>
The start date of the reporting period.

**period_ending**: `date | None`<br/>
The end date of the reporting period.

**fiscal_year**: `int | None`<br/>
The fiscal year.

**fiscal_period**: `str | None`<br/>
The fiscal period of the fiscal year.

</TabItem>

The specific URL is not directly used or downloaded, but is used to generate the base URL for the filing. e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/317540/000031754024000045/coke-20240731.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/317540/000031754024000045/ are both valid URLs for the same filing.

title: "form_13f"
description: "Get the form 13F"
keywords:
- sec
- form_13f
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="sec/form_13f - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the form 13F.

The Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) Form 13F is a quarterly
report that is required to be filed by all institutional investment
managers with at least $100 million in assets under management.
Managers are required to file Form 13F within 45 days after the last
day of the calendar quarter. Most funds wait until the end of this
period in order to conceal their investment strategy from competitors
and the public.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.form_13f(symbol='NVDA', provider='sec')
# Enter a date (calendar quarter ending) for a specific report.
obb.sec.form_13f(symbol='BRK-A', date='2016-09-30', provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. A CIK or Symbol can be used.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
A specific date to get data for. The date represents the end of the reporting period. All form 13F-HR filings are based on the calendar year and are reported quarterly. If a date is not supplied, the most recent filing is returned. Submissions beginning 2013-06-30 are supported.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
The number of data entries to return. The number of previous filings to return. The date parameter takes priority over this parameter.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. A CIK or Symbol can be used.

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
A specific date to get data for. The date represents the end of the reporting period. All form 13F-HR filings are based on the calendar year and are reported quarterly. If a date is not supplied, the most recent filing is returned. Submissions beginning 2013-06-30 are supported.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
The number of data entries to return. The number of previous filings to return. The date parameter takes priority over this parameter.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SecForm13FHR`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**period_ending**: `date`<br/>
The end-of-quarter date of the filing.

**issuer**: `str`<br/>
The name of the issuer.

**cusip**: `str`<br/>
The CUSIP of the security.

**asset_class**: `str`<br/>
The title of the asset class for the security.

**security_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the principal amount represents the number of shares or the principal amount of such class. 'SH' for shares. 'PRN' for principal amount. Convertible debt securities are reported as 'PRN'.

**option_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Defined when the holdings being reported are put or call options. Only long positions are reported.

**investment_discretion**: `str | None`<br/>
The investment discretion held by the Manager. Sole, shared-defined (DFN), or shared-other (OTR).

**voting_authority_sole**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of shares for which the Manager exercises sole voting authority.

**voting_authority_shared**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of shares for which the Manager exercises a defined shared voting authority.

**voting_authority_none**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of shares for which the Manager exercises no voting authority.

**principal_amount**: `int`<br/>
The total number of shares of the class of security or the principal amount of such class. Defined by the 'security_type'. Only long positions are reported

**value**: `int`<br/>
The fair market value of the holding of the particular class of security. The value reported for options is the fair market value of the underlying security with respect to the number of shares controlled. Values are rounded to the nearest US dollar and use the closing price of the last trading day of the calendar year or quarter.

Get the income statement for a given company.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.income_statement(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
obb.sec.income_statement(symbol='AAPL', period='annual', limit=5, provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache (4-hour memory) for the SEC request. Defaults to True.

**include_preliminary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to include preliminary data from 8-K filings for periods not yet reported on 10-Q/K.

**pit_mode**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Point-in-time mode. When True, returns data as originally reported at the time of filing, without subsequent restatements or amendments. For annual data, uses the original 10-K values. For quarterly data, preserves 10-Q filing vintage instead of using restated comparatives from the 10-K.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Principal types of exploration costs, which include depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of exploration activities, are: (i) Costs of topographical, geographical and geophysical studies, rights of access to properties to conduct those studies, and salaries and other expenses of geologists, geophysical crews, and others conducting those studies. **weighted_ave_basic_diluted_shares_os**: `int | None`<br/>
Average number of shares or units issued and outstanding that are used in calculating basic and diluted earnings per share (EPS).

**basic_diluted_eps**: `float | None`<br/>
The amount of net income or loss for the period per each share in instances when basic and diluted earnings per share are the same amount and reported as a single line item on the face of the financial statements. Basic earnings per share is the amount of net income or loss for the period per each share of common stock or unit outstanding during the reporting period. Diluted earnings per share includes the amount of net income or loss for the period available to each share of common stock or common unit outstanding during the reporting period and to each share or unit that would have been outstanding assuming the issuance of common shares or units for all dilutive potential common shares or units outstanding during the reporting period.

**cash_dividends_per_share**: `float | None`<br/>
Aggregate dividends declared during the period for each share of common stock outstanding.

**other_comprehensive_income_parent**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount after tax and reclassification adjustments of OCI attributable to parent.

**comprehensive_income_parent**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount after tax of increase (decrease) in equity from transactions and other events, attributable to parent.

**other_comprehensive_income_nci**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount after tax and reclassification adjustments of OCI attributable to noncontrolling interests.

**comprehensive_income_nci**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount after tax of increase (decrease) in equity from transactions and other events, attributable to noncontrolling interests.

**comprehensive_income**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount after tax of increase (decrease) in equity from transactions and other events/circumstances from net income and OCI. Includes portion attributable to NCI.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Parameters

The number of data entries to return.

Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use cache (4-hour memory) for the SEC request. Defaults to True.

**include_preliminary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to include preliminary data from 8-K filings for periods not yet reported on 10-Q/K.

**pit_mode**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Point-in-time mode. When True, returns data as originally reported at the time of filing, without subsequent restatements or amendments. For annual data, uses the original 10-K values. For quarterly data, preserves 10-Q filing vintage instead of using restated comparatives from the 10-K.

```python
from openbb import obb
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>

<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Wide date ranges can result in long download times. Recommended to use a smaller date range, default is 120 days ago.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Default is today.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Persist the data locally for future use. Default is True. Each form submission is an individual download and the SEC limits the number of concurrent downloads. This prevents the same file from being downloaded multiple times.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "management_discussion_analysis"
description: "Get the Management Discussion & Analysis section from the financial statements for a given company"
keywords:
- sec
- management_discussion_analysis
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="sec/management_discussion_analysis - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get the Management Discussion & Analysis section from the financial statements for a given company.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.management_discussion_analysis(symbol='AAPL', provider='sec')
# Get the Management Discussion & Analysis section by calendar year and period.
obb.sec.management_discussion_analysis(symbol='AAPL', calendar_year=2020, calendar_period='Q4', provider='sec')
# Setting 'include_tables' to True will attempt to extract all tables in valid Markdown.
obb.sec.management_discussion_analysis(symbol='AAPL', calendar_year=2020, calendar_period='Q4', provider='sec', include_tables=True)
# Setting 'raw_html' to True will bypass extraction and return the raw HTML file, as is. Use this for custom parsing or to access the entire HTML filing.
obb.sec.management_discussion_analysis(symbol='AAPL', calendar_year=2020, calendar_period='Q4', provider='sec', raw_html=True)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**calendar_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar year of the report. By default, is the current year. If the calendar period is not provided, but the calendar year is, it will return the annual report.

**calendar_period**: `str | None`<br/>
Calendar period of the report. By default, is the most recent report available for the symbol. If no calendar year and no calendar period are provided, it will return the most recent report.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**calendar_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Calendar year of the report. By default, is the current year. If the calendar period is not provided, but the calendar year is, it will return the annual report.

**calendar_period**: `str | None`<br/>
Calendar period of the report. By default, is the most recent report available for the symbol. If no calendar year and no calendar period are provided, it will return the most recent report.

**include_tables**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Return tables formatted as markdown in the text. Default is True.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
When True, the file will be cached for use later. Default is True.

**raw_html**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When True, the raw HTML content of the entire filing will be returned. Default is False. Use this option to parse the document manually.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SecManagementDiscussionAnalysis`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**calendar_year**: `int`<br/>
The calendar year of the report.

**calendar_period**: `int`<br/>
The calendar period of the report.

**period_ending**: `date | None`<br/>
The end date of the reporting period.

**content**: `str`<br/>
The content of the management discussion and analysis.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**calendar_year**: `int`<br/>
The calendar year of the report.

**calendar_period**: `int`<br/>
The calendar period of the report.

**period_ending**: `date | None`<br/>
The end date of the reporting period.

**content**: `str`<br/>
The content of the management discussion and analysis.

**url**: `str`<br/>
The URL of the filing from which the data was extracted.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

```python
from openbb import obb

```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Fund ticker symbol (mutual fund or ETF).

**date**: `date | None`<br/>
Specific filing period (period end date). Defaults to the latest.

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
Reporting year of the filing. Default is the most recent.

**quarter**: `int | None`<br/>
Reporting quarter of the filing. Default is the most recent.

## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**period**: `date`<br/>
Month-end date the metrics apply to.

**fund_name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the fund series.

**total_return**: `float | None`<br/>
Monthly total return of the fund.

**net_assets**: `float | None`<br/>
Net assets of the fund as of the reporting period.

**total_assets**: `float | None`<br/>
Total assets of the fund as of the reporting period.

**cash_and_equivalents**: `float | None`<br/>
Cash and cash equivalents not reported elsewhere.

**creation**: `float | None`<br/>
Total subscriptions (creations) during the month.

**redemption**: `float | None`<br/>
Total redemptions during the month.

**net_flow**: `float | None`<br/>
Net fund flow (creations minus redemptions).

**realized_gains**: `float | None`<br/>
Net realized gains during the month.

title: "schema_files"
description: "Explore SEC and FASB XBRL taxonomy schemas, labels, and presentation structures"
keywords:
- sec
- schema_files
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="sec/schema_files - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Explore SEC and FASB XBRL taxonomy schemas, labels, and presentation structures.

- No parameters: list all available taxonomy families.
- taxonomy only: get all parsed structures for the most recent year.
- taxonomy + year: get all parsed structures for a specific year.
- taxonomy + component: get one component's structure using the most recent year.
- taxonomy + year + component: get one component's parsed structure.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.sec.schema_files(provider='sec')
# Explore XBRL taxonomies progressively.
# List all available taxonomy families
obb.sec.schema_files(provider='sec')
# List components for US GAAP (latest year)
obb.sec.schema_files(taxonomy='us-gaap', provider='sec')
# List presentation components for US GAAP 2024
obb.sec.schema_files(taxonomy='us-gaap', year=2024, provider='sec')
# Get the Statement of Income presentation structure
obb.sec.schema_files(taxonomy='us-gaap', year=2024, component='soi', provider='sec')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**taxonomy**: `str | None`<br/>
Taxonomy family to explore. Omit to list all available taxonomies and their descriptions.

**year**: `int | None`<br/>
Taxonomy year (e.g. 2011+ for us-gaap, varies by taxonomy). Defaults to the most recent year when omitted.

**component**: `str | None`<br/>
Presentation component to retrieve. Values are taxonomy-specific. Omit to return all components for the taxonomy.

**category**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter taxonomies by SEC filer category.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `SchemaFiles`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='sec' label='sec'>

**name**: `str`<br/>
Identifier: taxonomy key, year, component name, or XBRL element ID depending on the query mode.

**label**: `str | None`<br/>
Human-readable label.

**description**: `str | None`<br/>
Description or long name.

**category**: `str | None`<br/>
Taxonomy category (e.g., operating_company).

**style**: `str | None`<br/>
Taxonomy style (e.g., FASB_STANDARD, SEC_EMBEDDED).

**has_label_linkbase**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the taxonomy has a parseable label linkbase.

**url**: `str | None`<br/>
URL to the taxonomy resource or SEC reference page.

**level**: `int | None`<br/>
Hierarchy depth in presentation structure (0 = root).

**order**: `float | None`<br/>
Sort order within parent in presentation structure.

**parent_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Parent XBRL element ID in presentation structure.

**preferred_label**: `str | None`<br/>
Preferred label role URI for presentation rendering.

**xbrl_type**: `str | None`<br/>
XBRL data type (e.g., monetaryItemType, textBlockItemType, stringItemType, sharesItemType, perShareItemType, domainItemType).

**period_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Period type: 'instant' (point-in-time) or 'duration' (over a period).

**balance_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Balance type for monetary items: 'credit' or 'debit'.

**abstract**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the element is abstract (grouping/heading only, not taggable).

**substitution_group**: `str | None`<br/>
XBRL substitution group: 'item' (line item), 'dimensionItem' (axis), 'hypercubeItem' (table).

**nillable**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the element value can be nil.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Calculate the Aroon Up, Aroon Down, and Aroon Oscillator series.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Aroon(25) on daily TSLA.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='TSLA', start_date='2023-01-01', provider='fmp').results
aroon = obb.technical.aroon(data=data, length=25)
obb.technical.aroon(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], length=2)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
OHLC price series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``, by default ``"date"``.

**length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 25<br/>
Aroon lookback window.

**scalar**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 100.0<br/>
Output magnification factor.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
Observation date.

**aroon_up**: `float`<br/>
Bars since the highest high, scaled.

**aroon_down**: `float`<br/>
Bars since the lowest low, scaled.

**aroon_oscillator**: `float`<br/>
``aroon_up`` minus ``aroon_down``.

Calculate the Average True Range (ATR), Wilder's volatility measure.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# ATR(14) on daily TSLA.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='TSLA', start_date='2023-01-01', provider='fmp').results
atr = obb.technical.atr(data=data, length=14)
obb.technical.atr(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], length=14)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
OHLC price series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``, by default ``"date"``.

**length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 14<br/>
ATR lookback window.

**mamode**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* rma<br/>
Smoothing applied to true-range. ``rma`` is the Wilder default.

**drift**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Difference period for true-range.

**offset**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 0<br/>
Shift the output series by this many bars, by default 0.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

List of warnings.

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
Observation date.

**atr**: `float`<br/>
Average true range over the trailing ``length`` bars.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Compute autocorrelation (ACF) and partial autocorrelation (PACF) with bands.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.technical.autocorrelation(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Column to evaluate.

**use_returns**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Difference and percent-change before computing.

**max_lag**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 40<br/>
Largest lag to compute.

**method**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* both<br/>
Which functions to compute.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[AutocorrelationData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**lag**: `int`<br/>
Lag in bars (0 is the series with itself, by definition 1.0 for ACF).

**acf**: `float`<br/>
Sample autocorrelation at this lag, or ``None`` when ACF was skipped.

**pacf**: `float`<br/>
Sample partial autocorrelation at this lag, or ``None`` when PACF was skipped.

**acf_confidence_lower**: `float`<br/>
Lower bound of the 95% confidence band for the ACF estimate.

**acf_confidence_upper**: `float`<br/>
Upper bound of the 95% confidence band for the ACF estimate.

**significant**: `bool`<br/>
``True`` when the ACF estimate at this lag (other than lag 0) lies outside the 95% confidence band.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="technical/clenow - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate Clenow Volatility-Adjusted Momentum on log prices.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Clenow momentum on TSLA over the trailing 90 days.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='TSLA', start_date='2023-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
out = obb.technical.clenow(data=data, period=90)
obb.technical.clenow(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], period=2)
```

Build a volatility-cone snapshot summarising realised volatility by window.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get volatility cones for the past two years of SPY.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='SPY', start_date='2022-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
cones = obb.technical.cones(data=data, model='yang_zhang')
obb.technical.cones(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
OHLC price series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``, by default ``"date"``.

**lower_q**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 0.25<br/>
Lower quantile for the cone band (0–1, exclusive of 1).

**upper_q**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 0.75<br/>
Upper quantile for the cone band (0–1, exclusive of 1).

**model**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* std<br/>
Estimator applied to each rolling window, by default ``"std"``.

**is_crypto**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When ``True`` and ``trading_periods`` is unset, annualise over 365 instead of 252, by default ``False``.

**trading_periods**: `int`<br/>
Annualisation factor. When unset, resolves to 365 if ``is_crypto`` is ``True``, otherwise 252.

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="technical/hurst - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Estimate the Hurst exponent via Rescaled-Range analysis or DFA.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.technical.hurst(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Column to evaluate.

**method**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* rs<br/>
``rs`` = Rescaled Range; ``dfa`` = Detrended Fluctuation.

**min_lag**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 2<br/>
Smallest window length.

**max_lag**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 100<br/>
Largest window length (exclusive).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[HurstData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**hurst_exponent**: `float`<br/>
Estimated Hurst exponent in ``[0, 1]``. ``None`` when the fit could not be computed.

**interpretation**: `str`<br/>
Qualitative classification: ``trending`` for H > 0.55, ``mean_reverting`` for H &lt; 0.45, otherwise ``random_walk``.

**confidence**: `float`<br/>
R-squared of the log-log fit used to estimate the exponent.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "realized_volatility"
description: "Calculate annualised rolling realised volatility under a chosen estimator"
keywords:
- technical
- realized_volatility
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="technical/realized_volatility - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Calculate annualised rolling realised volatility under a chosen estimator.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Yang-Zhang realised volatility on daily SPY.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='SPY', start_date='2022-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
rv = obb.technical.realized_volatility(data=data, model='yang_zhang', window=30)
obb.technical.realized_volatility(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], model='parkinson')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input OHLC(V) price series.

**model**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* yang_zhang<br/>
Volatility estimator. ``yang_zhang`` is the lowest-error blend; ``parkinson`` and ``rogers_satchell`` are range-based and drift-invariant; ``hodges_tompkins`` is bias-corrected close-to-close.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**window**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 30<br/>
Rolling window length in bars.

**trading_periods**: `int`<br/>
Annualisation factor. ``None`` resolves to 365 when ``is_crypto`` is true, otherwise 252.

**is_crypto**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
When true and ``trading_periods`` is unset, annualise over 365 instead of 252.

**clean**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Drop the leading warm-up rows where the rolling window is incomplete.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[RealizedVolatilityData]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

Compute the Relative Rotation Graph (RRG) for a basket against a benchmark.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Relative Strength Ratio and Momentum for a basket of symbols against a benchmark.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='AAPL,MSFT,GOOGL,META,AMZN,TSLA,SPY', start_date='2022-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
rr = obb.technical.relative_rotation(data=data, benchmark='SPY')
obb.technical.relative_rotation(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], benchmark='SPY')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
The data to be used for the relative rotation calculations. This should be the multi-symbol output from the 'equity.price.historical' endpoint, or similar, at a daily interval. Or a pivot table with the 'date' column as the index, the symbols as the columns, and the 'study' as the values. It is recommended to use the 'equity.price.historical' endpoint to get the data, and feed the results as-is.

**benchmark**: `str`<br/>
The symbol to be used as the benchmark.

**study**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* price<br/>
The data point for the calculations. If 'price', the closing price will be used. If 'volatility', the standard deviation of the closing price will be used. If 'data' is supplied as a pivot table, the 'study' will assume the values are the closing price and 'volume' will be ignored.

**long_period**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 252<br/>
The length of the long period for momentum calculation, by default is 252. Adjust this value, to 365, when supplying assets such as crypto.

**short_period**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 21<br/>
The length of the short period for momentum calculation, by default is 21. Adjust this value, to 30, when supplying assets such as crypto.

**window**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 21<br/>
The length of window for the standard deviation calculation, by default is 21. Adjust this value, to 30, when supplying assets such as crypto.

**trading_periods**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 252<br/>
The number of trading periods per year, for the standard deviation calculation, by default is 252. Adjust this value, to 365, when supplying assets such as crypto.

**chart_params**: `dict[str, Any]`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Additional parameters to pass when `chart=True` and the `openbb-charting` extension is installed. Parameters can be passed again to redraw the chart using the charting.to_chart() method of the response.<br/>
<br/>
            ChartParams<br/>
            -----------<br/>
            date: Optional[str]<br/>
                A target end date within the data, by default is the last date in the data.<br/>
            show_tails: bool<br/>
                Show the tails on the chart, by default is True.<br/>
            tail_periods: Optional[int]<br/>
                Number of periods to show in the tails, by default is 16.<br/>
            tail_interval: Literal['day', 'week', 'month']<br/>
                Interval to show the tails, by default is 'week'.<br/>
            title: Optional[str]<br/>
                Title of the chart.<br/>
</details>

**chart**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Detect bullish and bearish moving-average crossover events.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# 20/50 SMA crossover events on daily SPY.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='SPY', start_date='2022-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
events = obb.technical.crossovers(data=data, fast_length=20, slow_length=50)
obb.technical.signals.crossovers(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}])
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input price series.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Column on which to compute moving averages.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**fast_length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 20<br/>
Lookback for the fast moving average.

**slow_length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 50<br/>
Lookback for the slow moving average.

**mamode**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* sma<br/>
Moving-average flavour. ``sma`` is the default; ``ema``, ``wma``, ``hma`` and ``zlma`` are also supported.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[CrossoverEvent]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
Date of the crossover bar.

**direction**: `str`<br/>
``bullish`` when fast crosses above slow, ``bearish`` when fast crosses below.

**fast_value**: `float`<br/>
Fast moving-average value at the crossover bar.

**slow_value**: `float`<br/>
Slow moving-average value at the crossover bar.

**price**: `float`<br/>
Target-column price at the crossover bar.

**distance**: `float`<br/>
``fast_value - slow_value``. Positive for bullish, negative for bearish crossovers.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Detect regular and hidden divergences between price swings and an oscillator.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# RSI divergences on daily SPY.
data = obb.equity.price.historical(symbol='SPY', start_date='2022-01-01', provider='yfinance').results
events = obb.technical.divergences(data=data, indicator='rsi')
obb.technical.signals.divergences(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], indicator='rsi')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
OHLC price series.

**indicator**: `str`<br/>
Oscillator paired with price for divergence detection.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**indicator_length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 14<br/>
Lookback length used inside the oscillator.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Price column used for swings.

**lookback**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 60<br/>
Number of recent bars in which to search for swing pairs.

**min_swing_distance**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 5<br/>
Minimum number of bars separating two swing points. Also doubles as the half-window for local-extreme detection.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `list[DivergenceEvent]`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**confirmation_date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
Bar of the later (confirming) swing.

**prior_swing_date**: `date | datetime | str`<br/>
Bar of the earlier swing in the pair.

**kind**: `str`<br/>
``regular_bullish`` / ``regular_bearish`` flag reversal signals; ``hidden_*`` flag trend-continuation signals.

**price_at_prior**: `float`<br/>
Target-column price at ``prior_swing_date``.

**price_at_confirmation**: `float`<br/>
Target-column price at ``confirmation_date``.

**indicator_at_prior**: `float`<br/>
Oscillator value at ``prior_swing_date``.

**indicator_at_confirmation**: `float`<br/>
Oscillator value at ``confirmation_date``.

**strength**: `float`<br/>
0-1 score combining the relative price and indicator displacements. Higher means a wider, more emphatic divergence.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Label every bar with its oscillator regime and emit crossing events.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.technical.signals.oscillator_signals(data=[{'date': '2023-01-02', 'open': 110.0, 'high': 120.0, 'low': 100.0, 'close': 115.0, 'volume': 10000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-03', 'open': 165.0, 'high': 180.0, 'low': 150.0, 'close': 172.5, 'volume': 15000.0}, {'date': '2023-01-04', 'open': 146.67, 'high': 160.0, 'low': 133.33, 'close': 153.33, 'volume': 13333.33}, {'date': '2023-01-05', 'open': 137.5, 'high': 150.0, 'low': 125.0, 'close': 143.75, 'volume': 12500.0}, {'date': '2023-01-06', 'open': 132.0, 'high': 144.0, 'low': 120.0, 'close': 138.0, 'volume': 12000.0}], indicator='rsi', length=14)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
Input OHLC(V) price series.

**indicator**: `str`<br/>
Which oscillator to evaluate against its threshold bands.

**target**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* close<br/>
Price column used for oscillators that take a single series (rsi, cci).

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 14<br/>
Lookback window for the oscillator.

**overbought_threshold**: `float`<br/>
Upper band. ``None`` resolves to the indicator default (rsi 70, mfi 80, stoch 80, williams_r -20, cci 100).

**oversold_threshold**: `float`<br/>
Lower band. ``None`` resolves to the indicator default (rsi 30, mfi 20, stoch 20, williams_r -80, cci -100).

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

```python
from openbb import obb
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**data**: `Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray`<br/>
OHLC price series.

**index**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* date<br/>
Index column name in ``data``.

**adx_length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 14<br/>
ADX lookback window.

**choppiness_length**: `int`<br/>
*Default:* 14<br/>
Choppiness Index lookback window.

**adx_trend_threshold**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 25.0<br/>
ADX above this threshold marks a trending bar. Half this value is the cutoff for a weak trend.

**choppiness_range_threshold**: `float`<br/>
*Default:* 61.8<br/>
Choppiness above this threshold marks a ranging bar. The default 61.8 is a common Fibonacci-derived cutoff.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Choppiness Index reading at this bar. ``None`` during warm-up.

title: "smile"

keywords:
- tmx
