import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="tmx/derivatives/options/smile - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Implied-volatility smile / skew across strikes.

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* AC<br/>
The underlying symbol. Suffix with ':US' for OPRA-listed contracts; a bare symbol resolves to the Montreal Exchange listing.

**expirations**: `str`<br/>
Up to five expiration dates (comma-separated).

**otm**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Show only out-of-the-money contracts.

**skew**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Plot skew relative to ATM instead of IV.

**raw**: `bool`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* annual<br/>
Time period of the data to return.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use the on-disk response cache. Set to False to bypass.

</TabItem>

Historical prices for any listed instrument.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Daily price history.
obb.tmx.equity.historical(symbol='AC', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**interval**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* day<br/>
Time interval of the data to return. Or, any integer (entered as a string) representing the number of minutes. Default is daily data. There is no extended hours data, and intraday data is limited to after April 12 2022.

**adjustment**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* splits_only<br/>
The adjustment factor to apply. Only valid for daily data.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Insider buying and selling activity.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Insider activity summary.
obb.tmx.equity.ownership.insider_trading(symbol='AC', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return.

**summary**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Return a summary of the insider activity instead of the individuals.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

The type of security transacted.

Individual insider filings, as reported to SEDI.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Every insider filing over the past year.
obb.tmx.equity.ownership.insider_transactions(symbol='AC', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
The company symbol.

**period**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 12m<br/>
How far back to read filings.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use a cached request. Filings are cached for one day. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `TmxInsiderTransactions`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**owner_name**: `str | None`<br/>
The name of the insider.

**relationship**: `str | None`<br/>
The insider's relationship to the issuer.

**transaction_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date of the transaction.

**filing_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date the transaction was filed to SEDI.

**transaction_type**: `str | None`<br/>
The nature of the transaction.

**transaction_type_code**: `int | None`<br/>
The SEDI code for the nature of the transaction.

**securities_transacted**: `float | None`<br/>
The number of securities transacted.

**securities_owned**: `float | None`<br/>
The number of securities held after the transaction.

**ownership_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the holding is direct or indirect.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
The price the securities were transacted at.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
The currency of the price.

**market_value**: `float | None`<br/>
The value of the transaction.

**security_type**: `str | None`<br/>
The designation of the security transacted.

**underlying_security_type**: `str | None`<br/>
The designation of the underlying security.

**underlying_shares**: `float | None`<br/>
The number of underlying shares represented.

**insider_since**: `date | None`<br/>
The date the filer became an insider.

**filing_id**: `int | None`<br/>
The SEDI transaction ID.

**issuer_number**: `str | None`<br/>
The SEDI issuer number.

**insider_number**: `str | None`<br/>
The SEDI insider number.

</TabItem>

Delayed quote, for any symbol the feed addresses.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Delayed quote for a listing.
obb.tmx.equity.quote(symbol='AC', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str | list[str]`<br/>
Symbol to get data for. Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `TmxEquityQuote`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**asset_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of asset - i.e, stock, ETF, etc.

**name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the company or asset.

**exchange**: `str | None`<br/>
The name or symbol of the venue where the data is from.

**bid**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the top bid order.

**bid_size**: `int | None`<br/>
This represents the number of round lot orders at the given price. The normal round lot size is 100 shares. A size of 2 means there are 200 shares available at the given price.

**bid_exchange**: `str | None`<br/>
The specific trading venue where the purchase order was placed.

**ask**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the top ask order.

**ask_size**: `int | None`<br/>
This represents the number of round lot orders at the given price. The normal round lot size is 100 shares. A size of 2 means there are 200 shares available at the given price.

**ask_exchange**: `str | None`<br/>
The specific trading venue where the sale order was placed.

**quote_conditions**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Conditions or condition codes applicable to the quote.

**quote_indicators**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Indicators or indicator codes applicable to the participant quote related to the price bands for the issue, or the affect the quote has on the NBBO.

**sales_conditions**: `int | list[int] | list[str] | str | None`<br/>
Conditions or condition codes applicable to the sale.

**sequence_number**: `int | None`<br/>
The sequence number represents the sequence in which message events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11).

**market_center**: `str | None`<br/>
The ID of the UTP participant that originated the message.

**participant_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the quote was generated by the exchange.

**trf_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the TRF (Trade Reporting Facility) received the message.

**sip_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Timestamp for when the SIP (Security Information Processor) received the message from the exchange.

**last_price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the last trade.

**last_tick**: `str | None`<br/>
Whether the last sale was an up or down tick.

**last_size**: `int | None`<br/>
Size of the last trade.

**last_timestamp**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Date and Time when the last price was recorded.

**open**: `float | None`<br/>
The open price.

**high**: `float | None`<br/>
The high price.

**low**: `float | None`<br/>
The low price.

**close**: `float | None`<br/>
The close price.

**volume**: `float | int | None`<br/>
The trading volume.

**exchange_volume**: `float | int | None`<br/>
Volume of shares exchanged during the trading day on the specific exchange.

**prev_close**: `float | None`<br/>
The previous close price.

**change**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in price from previous close.

**change_percent**: `float | None`<br/>
Change in price as a normalized percentage.

**year_high**: `float | None`<br/>
The one year high (52W High).

**year_low**: `float | None`<br/>
The one year low (52W Low).

</TabItem>

Read the TSX 30 and TSX Venture 50 annual rankings.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# The Toronto Stock Exchange's top thirty performers.
obb.tmx.equity.rankings(ranking='tsx30', provider='tmx')
# The TSX Venture Exchange's top fifty performers.
obb.tmx.equity.rankings(ranking='venture50', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**ranking**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* tsx30<br/>
The published ranking. 'tsx30' is the Toronto Stock Exchange's top thirty performers, 'venture50' the TSX Venture Exchange's top fifty.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use a cached request. The rankings are published annually and cached for one day. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

*Default:* 200<br/>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>

---
title: "prices"
description: "Return reference data and last prices for every CIRO-designated bond"
keywords:
- tmx
- fixedincome
- prices
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="tmx/fixedincome/prices - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Return reference data and last prices for every CIRO-designated bond.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# The designated bond master.
obb.tmx.fixedincome.prices(provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**country**: `str | None`<br/>
The country to get data. Matches partial name.

**issuer_name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the issuer.  Returns partial matches and is case insensitive.

**isin**: `list | str | None | list[list | str | None]`<br/>
International Securities Identification Number(s) of the bond(s). Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

**lei**: `str | None`<br/>
Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing entity.

**currency**: `list | str | None`<br/>
Currency of the bond. Formatted as the 3-letter ISO 4217 code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).

**coupon_min**: `float | None`<br/>
Minimum coupon rate of the bond.

**coupon_max**: `float | None`<br/>
Maximum coupon rate of the bond.

**issued_amount_min**: `int | None`<br/>
Minimum issued amount of the bond.

**issued_amount_max**: `str | None`<br/>
Maximum issued amount of the bond.

**maturity_date_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Minimum maturity date of the bond.

**maturity_date_max**: `date | None`<br/>
Maximum maturity date of the bond.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**country**: `str | None`<br/>
The country to get data. Matches partial name.

**issuer_name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the issuer.  Returns partial matches and is case insensitive.

**isin**: `list | str | None | list[list | str | None]`<br/>
International Securities Identification Number(s) of the bond(s). Multiple items allowed for provider(s): tmx.

**lei**: `str | None`<br/>
Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing entity.

**currency**: `list | str | None`<br/>
Currency of the bond. Formatted as the 3-letter ISO 4217 code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).

**coupon_min**: `float | None`<br/>
Minimum coupon rate of the bond.

**coupon_max**: `float | None`<br/>
Maximum coupon rate of the bond.

**issued_amount_min**: `int | None`<br/>
Minimum issued amount of the bond.

**issued_amount_max**: `str | None`<br/>
Maximum issued amount of the bond.

**maturity_date_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Minimum maturity date of the bond.

**maturity_date_max**: `date | None`<br/>
Maximum maturity date of the bond.

**issue_date_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the minimum original issue date.

**issue_date_max**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the maximum original issue date.

**last_traded_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the minimum last trade date.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
All bond data is sourced from a single JSON file that is updated daily. The file is cached for one day to eliminate downloading more than once. Caching will significantly speed up subsequent queries. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `TmxBondPrices`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
International Securities Identification Number of the bond.

**lei**: `str | None`<br/>
Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing entity.

**figi**: `str | None`<br/>
FIGI of the bond.

**cusip**: `str | None`<br/>
CUSIP of the bond.

**coupon_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Coupon rate of the bond.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
International Securities Identification Number of the bond.

**lei**: `str | None`<br/>
Legal Entity Identifier of the issuing entity.

**figi**: `str | None`<br/>
FIGI of the bond.

**cusip**: `str | None`<br/>
CUSIP of the bond.

**coupon_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Coupon rate of the bond.

**ytm**: `float | None`<br/>
Yield to maturity (YTM) is the rate of return anticipated on a bond if it is held until the maturity date. It takes into account the current market price, par value, coupon rate and time to maturity. It is assumed that all coupons are reinvested at the same rate. Values are returned as a normalized percent.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
The last price for the bond.

**highest_price**: `float | None`<br/>
The highest price for the bond on the last traded date.

**lowest_price**: `float | None`<br/>
The lowest price for the bond on the last traded date.

**total_trades**: `int | None`<br/>
Total number of trades on the last traded date.

**last_traded_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Last traded date of the bond.

**maturity_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Maturity date of the bond.

**issue_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Issue date of the bond. This is the date when the bond first accrues interest.

**issuer_name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the issuing entity.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="tmx/fixedincome/trades - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Every reported trade for a bond, across its full history.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Reported bond trades.
obb.tmx.fixedincome.trades(cusip='135087U28', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**country**: `str | None`<br/>
The country to get data. Matches partial name.

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
ISIN of the bond.

**issuer_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of bond issuer.

**notional_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Currency of the bond, which might differ from the currency of the trade.<br/>
            Formatted as the 3-letter ISO 4217 code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).<br/>
</details>

**start_date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. YYYY-MM-DD or  ISO-8601 format. E.g. 2023-01-14T10:55:00Z

**end_date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. YYYY-MM-DD or  ISO-8601 format. E.g. 2023-01-14T10:55:00Z

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**country**: `str | None`<br/>
The country to get data. Matches partial name.

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
ISIN of the bond.

**issuer_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of bond issuer.

**notional_currency**: `str | None`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Currency of the bond, which might differ from the currency of the trade.<br/>
            Formatted as the 3-letter ISO 4217 code (e.g. GBP, EUR, USD).<br/>
</details>

**start_date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. YYYY-MM-DD or  ISO-8601 format. E.g. 2023-01-14T10:55:00Z

**end_date**: `date | str | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. YYYY-MM-DD or  ISO-8601 format. E.g. 2023-01-14T10:55:00Z

**cusip**: `str | None`<br/>
CUSIP of the bond. One of cusip, isin, or figi is required.

**figi**: `str | None`<br/>
FIGI of the bond.

**account_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* all<br/>
Restrict to trades booked to one account type.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use the on-disk bond master. Set to False to bypass.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

**results**: `TmxBondTrades`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**trade_date**: `date | datetime | None`<br/>
Date of the transaction.

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
ISIN of the bond.

**figi**: `str | None`<br/>
FIGI of the bond.

**cusip**: `str | None`<br/>
CUSIP of the bond.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the bond.

**current_yield**: `float | None`<br/>
Current yield of the bond.

**coupon_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Coupon rate of the bond.

**volume**: `int | None`<br/>
The trading volume.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**trade_date**: `datetime | None`<br/>
Execution date and time of the trade.

**isin**: `str | None`<br/>
ISIN of the bond.

**figi**: `str | None`<br/>
FIGI of the bond.

**cusip**: `str | None`<br/>
CUSIP of the bond.

**price**: `float | None`<br/>
Price of the bond.

**current_yield**: `float | None`<br/>
Current yield of the bond.

**coupon_rate**: `float | None`<br/>
Coupon rate of the bond.

**volume**: `int | None`<br/>
The trading volume.

**settlement_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Settlement date of the trade.

**issuer**: `str | None`<br/>
The issuer of the bond.

**maturity_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Maturity date of the bond.

**transaction_type**: `str | None`<br/>
The type of transaction reported.

**account_type**: `str | None`<br/>
The account type the trade was booked to.

**commission**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether a commission was charged.

**volume_capped**: `bool | None`<br/>
Whether the reported volume is capped at the disclosure limit.

**reported_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date the trade was submitted to CIRO, which is later than the execution date when a trade is reported late or amended.

**record_id**: `str | None`<br/>
CIRO's unique identifier for the trade record.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Government of Canada bond reference data and prices.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Government of Canada bond prices.
obb.tmx.fixedincome.treasury_prices(provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
A specific date to get data for. Defaults to the last business day.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
A specific date to get data for. Defaults to the last business day.

**govt_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* federal<br/>
The level of government issuer.

**issue_date_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the minimum original issue date.

**issue_date_max**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the maximum original issue date.

**last_traded_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the minimum last trade date.

**maturity_date_min**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the minimum maturity date.

**maturity_date_max**: `date | None`<br/>
Filter by the maximum maturity date.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
All bond data is sourced from a single JSON file that is updated daily. The file is cached for one day to eliminate downloading more than once. Caching will significantly speed up subsequent queries. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Return the S&P/TSX index universe.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Every index TMX publishes.
obb.tmx.index.available(provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use a cached request. Index data is from a single JSON file, updated each day after close. It is cached for one day. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `TmxAvailableIndices`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

**name**: `str | None`<br/>
**exchange**: `str | None`<br/>
Stock exchange where the index is listed.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the index is traded in.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
The ticker symbol of the index.

**name**: `str | None`<br/>
**exchange**: `str | None`<br/>
Stock exchange where the index is listed.

**currency**: `str | None`<br/>
Currency the index is traded in.

</TabItem>

Daily open, high, low, close, and volume for an index.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Daily levels of an index.
obb.tmx.index.historical(symbol='^TSX', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use a cached request. The daily levels are cached for six hours. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>

Profile of an index, with links to its factsheet and methodology.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Index profile, documents, and key data.
obb.tmx.index.info(symbol='^TSX', provider='tmx')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='tmx' label='tmx'>

**symbol**: `str`<br/>
Symbol to get data for.

**use_cache**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* True<br/>
Whether to use a cached request. Index data is from a single JSON file, updated each day after close. It is cached for one day. To bypass, set to False.

</TabItem>

keywords:

---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="tmx/news/market - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

News across a basket of symbols, in the news feed widget's shape.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# News across the large banks.
obb.tmx.news.market(symbols='RY,TD,BMO,BNS,CM')
# Only the earnings coverage.
obb.tmx.news.market(symbols='RY,TD', topic='FINANCIAL RESULTS')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

**symbols**: `str`<br/>
*Default:* AC,RY,BCE,ENB,SHOP<br/>
The symbols the news should cover.

**topic**: `str`<br/>
Keep only the articles carrying this subject.

**limit**: `int`<br/>

Get and filter lists of Congressional Amendments.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.uscongress.amendments(provider='congress_gov')
obb.uscongress.amendments(congress=119, amendment_type='hamdt', provider='congress_gov')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='congress_gov' label='congress_gov'>

**congress**: `int | None`<br/>
Congress number (e.g., 119 for the 119th Congress). When None, defaults to the current Congress.

**amendment_type**: `str | None`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Amendment type (e.g., 'hamdt' for House Amendments).<br/>
<br/>
Must be one of:<br/>
<br/>
- hamdt: An amendment offered or adopted in the House of Representatives.<br/>
House amendments are identified by 'H.Amdt.' followed by a number.<br/>
- samdt: An amendment offered or adopted in the Senate.<br/>
Senate amendments are identified by 'S.Amdt.' followed by a number.<br/>
</details>

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Filter amendments updated on or after this date.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Filter amendments updated on or before this date.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
Maximum number of results to return. When None, defaults to 100 (max 250). Set to 0 for no limit (must be used with 'amendment_type').

**offset**: `int | None`<br/>
The starting record returned. 0 is the first record.

**sort_by**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* desc<br/>
Sort by update date. Default is latest first.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "bills"
description: "Get and filter lists of Congressional Bills"
keywords:
- uscongress
- bills
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="uscongress/bills - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get and filter lists of Congressional Bills.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.uscongress.bills(provider='congress_gov')
obb.uscongress.bills(start_date='2025-01-01', end_date='2025-01-31', provider='congress_gov')
# Get all bills of type 's' (Senate) for the 118th Congress.
obb.uscongress.bills(bill_type='s', congress=118, limit=0, provider='congress_gov')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='congress_gov' label='congress_gov'>

**congress**: `int | None`<br/>
Congress number (e.g., 118 for the 118th Congress). The 103rd Congress started in 1993, which is the earliest date supporting full text versions. Each Congress spans two years, starting in odd-numbered years.

**bill_type**: `str | None`<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Bill type (e.g., 'hr' for House bills).<br/>
<br/>
Must be one of: hr, s, hjres, sjres, hconres, sconres, hres, sres.<br/>
<br/>
Bills<br/>
-----<br/>
<br/>
A bill is the form used for most legislation, whether permanent or temporary, general or special, public or private.<br/>
<br/>
A bill originating in the House of Representatives is designated by the letters “H.R.”,<br/>
signifying “House of Representatives”, followed by a number that it retains throughout all its parliamentary stages.<br/>
<br/>
Bills are presented to the President for action when approved in identical form<br/>
by both the House of Representatives and the Senate.<br/>
<br/>
Joint Resolutions<br/>
-----------------<br/>
<br/>
Joint resolutions may originate either in the House of Representatives or in the Senate.<br/>
<br/>
There is little practical difference between a bill and a joint resolution. Both are subject to the same procedure,<br/>
except for a joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution.<br/>
<br/>
On approval of such a resolution by two-thirds of both the House and Senate,<br/>
it is sent directly to the Administrator of General Services for submission to the individual states for ratification.<br/>
<br/>
It is not presented to the President for approval.<br/>
A joint resolution originating in the House of Representatives is designated “H.J.Res.” followed by its individual number.<br/>
Joint resolutions become law in the same manner as bills.<br/>
<br/>
Concurrent Resolutions<br/>
----------------------<br/>
<br/>
Matters affecting the operations of both the House of Representatives and Senate<br/>
are usually initiated by means of concurrent resolutions.<br/>
<br/>
A concurrent resolution originating in the House of Representatives is designated “H.Con.Res.”<br/>
followed by its individual number.<br/>
<br/>
On approval by both the House of Representatives and Senate,<br/>
they are signed by the Clerk of the House and the Secretary of the Senate.<br/>
<br/>
They are not presented to the President for action.<br/>
<br/>
Simple Resolutions<br/>
------------------<br/>
<br/>
A matter concerning the operation of either the House of Representatives or Senate<br/>
alone is initiated by a simple resolution.<br/>
<br/>
A resolution affecting the House of Representatives is designated “H.Res.” followed by its number.<br/>
<br/>
They are not presented to the President for action.<br/>
</details>

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters bills by the last updated date.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters bills by the last updated date.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return. When None, default sets to 100 (max 250). Set to 0 for no limit (must be used with 'bill_type' and 'congress'). Setting to 0 will nullify the start_date, end_date, and offset parameters.

**offset**: `int | None`<br/>
The starting record returned. 0 is the first record.

**sort_by**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* desc<br/>
Sort by update date. Default is latest first.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CongressBills`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='congress_gov' label='congress_gov'>

**bill_id**: `str`<br/>
The bill identifier, e.g. '119-hr-29'.

**latest_action_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date of the latest action on the bill.

**update_date**: `date`<br/>
The date the bill was last updated.

**congress**: `int`<br/>
The congress session number.

**bill_number**: `int`<br/>
The bill number.

**origin_chamber**: `str`<br/>
The chamber where the bill originated.

**origin_chamber_code**: `str`<br/>
The chamber code where the bill originated.

**bill_type**: `str`<br/>
The type of bill (e.g., HR, S).

**title**: `str`<br/>
The title of the bill.

**latest_action**: `str | None`<br/>
Latest action information for the bill.

**update_date_including_text**: `datetime | None`<br/>
The date and time the bill text was last updated.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "laws"

keywords:
- uscongress
- laws
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="uscongress/laws - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get and filter lists of enacted Congressional Laws (public or private).

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.uscongress.laws(provider='congress_gov')
# Get the 5 most recent public laws of the 118th Congress.
obb.uscongress.laws(congress=118, law_type='public', limit=5, provider='congress_gov')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='congress_gov' label='congress_gov'>

**congress**: `int | None`<br/>
Congress number (e.g., 119 for the 119th Congress). When None, defaults to the current Congress.

**law_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* public<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Law type filter. Must be one of: public, private.<br/>
<br/>
A public law affects the general public or classes of citizens and is identified<br/>
by a number in the format '&#123;congress&#125;-&#123;number&#125;' (e.g., '119-44'). A private law<br/>
affects specific individuals, organizations, or localities rather than the<br/>
general public, and is far less common than public laws.<br/>
</details>

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return. When None, default sets to 100. Set to 0 for no limit.

**offset**: `int | None`<br/>
The starting record returned. 0 is the first record.

**sort_by**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* desc<br/>
Sort by law number. Default is highest first.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `CongressLaws`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='congress_gov' label='congress_gov'>

**law_id**: `str`<br/>
The law identifier, e.g. '119-1'.

**law_number**: `int`<br/>
The law number within the Congress.

**law_type**: `str`<br/>
The type of law (public or private).

**congress**: `int`<br/>
The congress session number.

**enacted_date**: `date | None`<br/>
The date the law was approved/enacted.

**title**: `str`<br/>
The title of the law.

**citation**: `str`<br/>
The public/private law citation.

**statute_citation**: `str | None`<br/>
The Statutes at Large citation.

**package_id**: `str`<br/>
The GovInfo package identifier for the law.

**pdf**: `str`<br/>
URL to the law text in PDF format.

**htm**: `str`<br/>
URL to the law text in HTML format.

**xml**: `str`<br/>
URL to the law text in XML format.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Parameters

**congress**: `int | None`<br/>
Restrict results to a specific Congress number.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters by publish date.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters by publish date.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
The number of data entries to return. When None, defaults to 20.

title: "adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops"
description: "Get ERS adoption of genetically engineered crops - the annual share of planted acres in genetically engineered corn, upland cotton, and soybean varieties, by trait and by State, pivoted to a wide layout with the GE traits as columns and years as rows"
keywords:
- usda
- adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="usda/adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get ERS adoption of genetically engineered crops - the annual share of planted acres in genetically engineered corn, upland cotton, and soybean varieties, by trait and by State, pivoted to a wide layout with the GE traits as columns and years as rows.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops(provider='usda')
# Get U.S. corn GE adoption by trait since 2010.
obb.usda.adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops(crop='corn', state='United States', start_year=2010, provider='usda')
# Get Texas upland cotton GE adoption.
obb.usda.adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops(crop='cotton', state='Texas', provider='usda')
# Get U.S. herbicide-tolerant soybean adoption.
obb.usda.adoption_of_genetically_engineered_crops(crop='soybeans', state='United States', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**crop**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* corn<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Crop whose sheet is retrieved. The crop selects the trait columns and the state option list. Corn and cotton publish four trait columns (Bt only, HT only, Stacked, All GE); soybeans publish only HT only and All GE. Valid crops are:<br/>
    corn, cotton, soybeans<br/>
</details>

**state**: `str | None | list[str | None]`<br/>
*Default:* United States<br/>
State(s) to retrieve, as a comma-separated list of names. The published estimating-program states vary by crop; 'United States' is the national total and 'Other States' is the residual aggregate. If None, defaults to 'United States'. Multiple items allowed.

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data, compared against the observation year. If None, returns from 2000, the first year of the series.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the data, compared against the observation year. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `AdoptionOfGeneticallyEngineeredCropsInTheUnitedStates`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**state**: `str`<br/>
State of the observation, or 'United States' for the national total and 'Other States' for the residual aggregate.

**year**: `int`<br/>
Year of the observation.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Get ERS agricultural and food research and development (R&D) expenditures - public and private U.S. R&D spending in current and constant dollars with the R&D price index, pivoted to a wide layout with the R&D series as columns and years as rows.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb

```

## Parameters

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**measure**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* real<br/>
Measure to retrieve, selecting which values fill the R&D series columns. 'real' is inflation-adjusted constant 2022 U.S. dollars; 'nominal' is current U.S. dollars. Both are in millions. The R&D price index column is the same under either measure.

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data, compared against the observation year. If None, returns from 1970.

End year for filtering the data, compared against the observation year. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

Get the ERS U.S. agricultural trade data update - each table pivoted to a wide layout with the year and period in the rows and the trade direction, commodity, or trade partner spread into columns.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.agricultural_trade(provider='usda')
# Get the top export markets for corn, by volume.
obb.usda.agricultural_trade(table='top_export_markets', commodity='Corn', provider='usda')
# Get the monthly agricultural trade totals since 2020.
obb.usda.agricultural_trade(table='monthly', start_year=2020, provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**table**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* exports_ytd<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Table to retrieve, pivoted to a wide layout. The natural 'many' dimension spreads into columns (trade direction for the summary and monthly tables, commodity for the year-to-date export and import tables, trade partner for the top-market tables) while a single pinned period column labels the rows. Valid tables are:<br/>
    summary, monthly, exports_ytd, imports_ytd, top_export_markets, top_import_sources<br/>
</details>

**period_basis**: `str | None`<br/>
Reporting basis to keep, one of those the selected table publishes: 'Fiscal year', 'Calendar year', 'Fiscal year-to-date', 'Calendar year-to-date', or 'Monthly'. Filtering to one basis yields a single aligned time series instead of mixing annual totals, year-to-date spans, and single months. If None, the table's default basis is used.

**value_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Measure to spread into the wide cells, scoped to the table: 'value' (customs value), 'volume', or 'cif' (cost, insurance, and freight). If None or invalid for the table, the table's first measure is used.

**commodity**: `str | None`<br/>
Commodity whose trade partners spread into columns, for the top-export-market and top-import-source tables only, as a single exact name as published, e.g. 'Soybeans'. If None, the table's first commodity is used. Ignored by the summary, monthly, and year-to-date tables.

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data. None returns from the beginning of the series.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the data. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

**latest**: `bool | None`<br/>
*Default:* False<br/>
Return only the most recent monthly update vintage for tables that retain the marketing year's prior vintages. No effect on the summary and monthly tables.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Download one, or more, USDA FAS Bell Reports.

This command returns only the results portion of the OBBject response.
It contains a list of dictionaries where the base64 encoded content of the
document is under the 'content' key.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.bell_report(provider='usda', urls=['https://apps.fas.usda.gov/esrqs/ReportsHome.aspx?RN=BR&wed=07%2F03%2F2025&YGO=07%2F04%2F2024&RD=07%2F10%2F2025&MY=N&CID=1%2C&AppUserId=0'])
# List the reports published for wheat and corn, then download them.
urls = [d['value'] for d in obb.usda.bell_report_urls(commodity_code='101,401')]
pdfs = obb.usda.bell_report(urls=urls)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**urls**: `dict[str, list[str]] | list[str] | str | list[dict[str, list[str]] | list[str] | str]`<br/>
Report viewer URLs to download, as returned by the bell_report_urls endpoint. Multiple items allowed.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Any

Base64-encoded PDF document.

Get ERS commodity costs and returns - annual per-unit cost-and-return budgets by commodity and ERS Farm Resource Region.

--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.commodity_costs_and_returns(provider='usda')
# Get the U.S. total corn budget since 2020.
obb.usda.commodity_costs_and_returns(commodity='corn', region='U.S. total', start_year=2020, provider='usda')
# Get farrow-to-finish hog operating costs.
obb.usda.commodity_costs_and_returns(commodity='hogs_farrow_finish', category='operating_costs', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**commodity**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* corn<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Commodity budget to retrieve; selects the per-commodity cost-and-return file. Valid commodities are:<br/>
    corn, cotton, barley, peanuts, rice, sorghum, oats, soybeans, wheat, milk, cow_calf, hogs_all, hogs_farrow_finish, hogs_farrow_feeder, hogs_feeder_finish, hogs_farrow_weanling, hogs_weanling_feeder<br/>
</details>

**region**: `str | None`<br/>

    gross_value_of_production, operating_costs, net_value, allocated_overhead, costs_listed, supporting_information, production_practices, size_of_operation, production_arrangement<br/>
</details>

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>

<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

    US consumers aged 2 and above, Sex - Males, Sex - Females, Ages 2-19, Ages 20-64, Ages 65 and above, Cohort - Boys age 2-19, Cohort - Girls age 2-19, Cohort - Men age 20 and above, Cohort - Women age 20 and above, Income - low-income households, Income - mid-income households, Income - high-income households, Race - Non-Hispanic White, Race - Non-Hispanic Black, Race - Hispanic, Race - Other racial & ethnic, Edu. - Less than high school, Edu. - High school degree, Edu. - College attended<br/>
</details>

**statistic**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* mean<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Statistic to spread across the survey-cycle columns for the intake tables (2-7): the mean, or the standard error of the mean. Ignored by the sample-size and recommended-density tables. Valid statistics are:<br/>
    mean, se_of_mean<br/>
</details>

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the survey-cycle columns, compared against the first year of each cycle. Ignored by the recommended-density table. If None, returns from 1977.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the survey-cycle columns, compared against the first year of each cycle. Ignored by the recommended-density table. If None, returns through 2017-2018.

**table**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
Food-dollar table to retrieve, by table number. Nominal offers tables 1-22 (six dollar aggregates and 16 commodity groups); real offers only tables 1-6.

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>

**taxes**: `str | None`<br/>

**state**: `str | None`<br/>

Get ERS Food Price Outlook - consumer and producer food price index forecasts, prediction intervals, and the annual percent-change record, each pivoted to a wide layout.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.food_price_outlook(provider='usda')
# Get the annual consumer food price index changes since 2000.
obb.usda.food_price_outlook(table='cpi_annual', start_year=2000, provider='usda')
# Get the consumer forecast prediction intervals for beef and eggs.
obb.usda.food_price_outlook(table='cpi_forecast', item='beef,eggs', provider='usda')
# Get the historical consumer forecast vintages for all food.
obb.usda.food_price_outlook(table='cpi_forecast_history', item='all food', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**table**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* cpi_forecast<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Food Price Outlook table to retrieve. The forecast tables spread each price-index measure into a column, the annual tables spread each food category into a column with years as rows, and the forecast-history tables spread the prediction-interval bounds into columns. Valid tables are:<br/>
    cpi_forecast, ppi_forecast, cpi_annual, ppi_annual, cpi_forecast_history, ppi_forecast_history<br/>
</details>

**item**: `str | None`<br/>
Filter by a single exact price-index item as published, e.g. 'Beef and veal', scoped to the selected table. Filters rows for the forecast and forecast-history tables and value columns for the annual tables. If None, all items are included.

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data, applied to the annual calendar year and the forecast-history year being forecast. Forecast measures with no year, such as month-over-month changes, are always kept. If None, returns from the beginning of the series.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the data, applied to the annual calendar year and the forecast-history year being forecast. Forecast measures with no year, such as month-over-month changes, are always kept. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get ERS international agricultural productivity - agricultural total factor productivity indices, output and input quantity indices, and the underlying physical output and input quantities for countries, territories, regions, income groups, and the world, pivoted to a wide layout by year.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.international_agricultural_productivity(provider='usda')
# Get U.S. agricultural productivity indices since 2000.
obb.usda.international_agricultural_productivity(grouping='north_america', country=179, start_year=2000, provider='usda')
# Get India's physical output and input quantities.
obb.usda.international_agricultural_productivity(grouping='asia_pacific', country=103, measure='physical_quantities', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**grouping**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* country_grouping<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Grouping that scopes the country selector into buckets derived from the entity's region, income level, or aggregate type. It scopes the dropdown only; the data is selected by country. Valid groupings are:<br/>
    sub_saharan_africa, latin_america_caribbean, asia_pacific, cwana, europe, oceania, north_america, income_group, country_grouping<br/>
</details>

**country**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 220<br/>
Country, territory, region, income group, or aggregate to retrieve, as its unique dataset order. The order disambiguates entities sharing a name, e.g. the country 'China' (81) from the income aggregate 'China' (227). Defaults to 220, the world.

**measure**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* productivity_indices<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Measure family spread into the wide value columns. 'productivity_indices' emits the seven 2015=100 indices; 'physical_quantities' emits the twelve output and input quantities in their published units. Valid measures are:<br/>
    productivity_indices, physical_quantities<br/>
</details>

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data, from 1961. If None, returns from the beginning of the series.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the data, up to 2023. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Tabs>

</details>

**attribute**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Production<br/>

Get ERS Poverty Area Measures - county- and census-tract-level poverty-area classification flags (high-poverty, extreme-poverty, persistent-poverty, and enduring-poverty), published in successive editions as a FIPS/tract lookup table scoped by edition, geography level, and state.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.poverty_area_measures(provider='usda')
# Get the 2025-edition county poverty-area measures for Mississippi.
obb.usda.poverty_area_measures(edition='2025', state='MS', provider='usda')
# Get the 2025-edition census-tract poverty-area measures for Mississippi.
obb.usda.poverty_area_measures(edition='2025', level='tract', state='MS', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**edition**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 2025<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Published edition to retrieve. Each edition is a separate release of the poverty-area classification, differing in census-tract geography, metro/Beale/RUCA vintage, and the most recent ACS measurement periods carried. Valid editions are:<br/>
    2025, 2023, 2022<br/>
</details>

**level**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* county<br/>
Geographic level of the lookup. 'county' returns one row per county FIPS reading the county classification flags; 'tract' returns one row per census tract reading the tract flags. Valid levels are: county, tract.

**state**: `str | None`<br/>
Two-letter state postal abbreviation to scope the rows to a single state. If None, returns every area in the edition. At tract level the state filter is the primary usability lever.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "psd_report"
description: "Download one, or more, USDA FAS commodity PSD circulars"
keywords:
- usda
- psd_report
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="usda/psd_report - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Download one, or more, USDA FAS commodity PSD circulars.

This command returns only the results portion of the OBBject response.
It contains a list of dictionaries where the base64 encoded content of the
document is under the 'content' key.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.psd_report(provider='usda', urls=['https://apps.fas.usda.gov/PSDOnline/Circulars/2026/01/Citrus.pdf'])
# List the latest circular for every commodity, then download them.
urls = [d['value'] for d in obb.usda.psd_report_urls()]
pdfs = obb.usda.psd_report(urls=urls)
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**urls**: `dict[str, list[str]] | list[str] | str | list[dict[str, list[str]] | list[str] | str]`<br/>
Circular URLs to download, as returned by the psd_report_urls endpoint. Multiple items allowed.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

Any
---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**error_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Error type, if the circular could not be downloaded.

**content**: `str`<br/>
Base64-encoded PDF document.

**filename**: `str | None`<br/>
The filename of the downloaded PDF.

**data_format**: `dict[str, str] | None`<br/>
Data format information, including data type and filename.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

title: "resource_requirements_of_food_demand"
description: "Get ERS resource requirements of food demand - the employment, freshwater withdrawals, and energy use, total and by source, embodied across the U"
keywords:
- usda
- resource_requirements_of_food_demand
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="usda/resource_requirements_of_food_demand - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Get ERS resource requirements of food demand - the employment, freshwater withdrawals, and energy use, total and by source, embodied across the U.S. food supply chain to meet final consumer demand for each food, beverage, and food-related category, pivoted to a wide layout with the resource-and-source measures as columns and year and supply-chain stage as rows.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.resource_requirements_of_food_demand(provider='usda')
# Get the resources embodied in beef demand since 2015.
obb.usda.resource_requirements_of_food_demand(table='Xf1103', start_year=2015, provider='usda')
# Get the household home-kitchen and transportation resource use.
obb.usda.resource_requirements_of_food_demand(table='Xf3000', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**table**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Xf0000<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Food group, commodity, or aggregate table to retrieve, identified by its Xf table number. Each table holds the employment, freshwater withdrawal, and energy resources embodied across the food supply chain to meet final demand for that category; the resource-and-source measures become the wide value columns while year and supply-chain stage stay as pinned rows. Valid tables are:<br/>

Get ERS rural-urban commuting area (RUCA) codes - primary and secondary RUCA classification codes and descriptions for U.S. census tracts and ZIP codes across the 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020 vintages, as a per-area lookup table scoped by state.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.rural_urban_commuting_area_codes(provider='usda')
# Get the 2020 census-tract RUCA codes for Delaware.
obb.usda.rural_urban_commuting_area_codes(table='tract_2020', state='DE', provider='usda')
# Get the 2010 ZIP-code RUCA codes for Vermont.
obb.usda.rural_urban_commuting_area_codes(table='zip_2010', state='VT', provider='usda')
# Get the 1990 census-tract RUCA codes for Wyoming.
obb.usda.rural_urban_commuting_area_codes(table='tract_1990', state='WY', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

*Default:* tract_2020<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Vintage and geography of the code set to retrieve, as one lookup table per census-tract or ZIP-code vintage. Valid tables are:<br/>
    tract_2020, tract_2010, tract_2000, tract_1990, zip_2020, zip_2010<br/>
</details>

**state**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* DE<br/>
Two-letter state or territory code to scope the lookup to, e.g. 'DE'. If None, every area in the table is returned, which is tens of thousands of rows. The set of states differs by table.

Two-letter state or territory code of the area.

```python
from openbb import obb
```

<Tabs>

**vintage**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 2023<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Classification vintage to retrieve. Each vintage is a separate county lookup published in that year, carrying the RUCC code, its vintage-specific description, and the county population; codes and descriptions are vintage-specific because the urbanization thresholds changed over time. Valid vintages are:<br/>
    2023, 2013, 2003<br/>
</details>

**state**: `str | None`<br/>
Two-letter state or territory code to scope the county rows to a single state. If None, returns every county of the vintage. The available states vary by vintage: the 2023 and 2013 vintages include the AS, GU, MP, VI, PR, and DC territories, and the 2003 vintage adds PR to the fifty states and DC.

County or county-equivalent area name, as published.

BBCE asset limit in thousands of dollars. Blank when the state does not use BBCE or BBCE eliminates the asset test; applies to only the few states that keep an asset limit, so hidden by default.

**bbce_a_veh**: `float | None`<br/>
BBCE vehicle rule: 1 = exempt an amount, 2 = exclude at least one, 3 = exclude all. Blank when the state does not use BBCE or the asset test is eliminated; applies to only the few states that keep an asset limit, so hidden by default.

**bbce_inclmt**: `float | None`<br/>
BBCE gross income limit as a percentage of the Federal poverty level. Blank when the state does not use BBCE.

**bbce_child**: `float | None`<br/>
Whether BBCE is limited to households with dependent children: 0 = no, 1 = yes. Blank when the state does not use BBCE.

**bbce_elddisinclmt**: `float | None`<br/>
BBCE gross income limit (% FPL) for households with a senior or disabled member; -8 = gross income test eliminated, -7 = 200% FPL only for all-senior/disabled households. Blank when the state does not use BBCE.

**bbce_multiple**: `float | None`<br/>
Whether multiple BBCE guidelines apply to different household types: 0 = no, 1 = yes. Blank when the state does not use BBCE.

**call_any**: `float | None`<br/>
Whether the state operates call centers in any part of the state: 0 = no, 1 = yes.

**cap**: `float | None`<br/>
Whether the state operates a Combined Application Project for SSI recipients: 0 = no, 1 = yes.

**certearn_0103**: `float | None`<br/>

**certearn_0406**: `float | None`<br/>

**certearn_0712**: `float | None`<br/>

**certearn_1399**: `float | None`<br/>
Proportion of SNAP units with earnings with 13+ month recertification periods.

**certearnavg**: `float | None`<br/>

**certearnmed**: `float | None`<br/>

**certeld_0103**: `float | None`<br/>

Proportion of SNAP units with no earnings and a senior member with 4-6 month recertification periods.

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Get ERS state agricultural trade - state-level U.S. agricultural exports by commodity and by state on a calendar-year basis, and the top export and import commodities by state on a fiscal-year basis, each pivoted to a wide layout with the years in the rows.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.state_agricultural_trade(provider='usda')
# Get California's agricultural exports by commodity.
obb.usda.state_agricultural_trade(table='exports_by_commodity', state='California', provider='usda')
# Get total agricultural exports spread across the states.
obb.usda.state_agricultural_trade(table='exports_by_state', commodity='Total agricultural exports', provider='usda')
# Get Texas's top export commodities by fiscal year.
obb.usda.state_agricultural_trade(table='top_exports', state='Texas', provider='usda')
# Get California's top import commodities by fiscal year.
obb.usda.state_agricultural_trade(table='top_imports', state='California', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**table**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* exports_by_commodity<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Table to retrieve. 'exports_by_commodity' spreads a state's export commodities across the calendar years; 'exports_by_state' spreads the states across the calendar years for one commodity; 'top_exports' and 'top_imports' spread a state's top fiscal-year commodities across the fiscal years. Valid tables are:<br/>
    exports_by_commodity, exports_by_state, top_exports, top_imports<br/>
</details>

**state**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* California<br/>
State whose commodities are spread into columns for the 'exports_by_commodity', 'top_exports', and 'top_imports' tables, as a full state name or two-letter code, or 'United States' for the national total. Ignored by the 'exports_by_state' table. The calendar-year tables cover the 50 states and the United States; the fiscal-year tables also cover the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands.

**commodity**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Total agricultural exports<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Commodity whose states are spread into columns for the 'exports_by_state' table. Ignored by the other tables. Valid commodities are:<br/>
    Total agricultural exports, Total animal products, Total plant products, Beef and veal, Broiler meat, Corn, Cotton, Dairy products, Feeds and other feed grains, Fruits, fresh, Fruits, processed, Grain products, Hides and skins, Other livestock products, Other oilseeds and products, Other plant products, Other poultry products, Pork, Rice, Soybean meal, Soybeans, Tobacco, Tree nuts, Vegetable oils, Vegetables, fresh, Vegetables, processed, Wheat<br/>
</details>

**start_year**: `int | None`<br/>
Start year for filtering the data, compared against the calendar or fiscal year. If None, returns from the first published year.

**end_year**: `int | None`<br/>
End year for filtering the data, compared against the calendar or fiscal year. If None, returns up to the most recent year.

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

Get ERS Urban Influence Codes - a county-level classification of every U.S. county by metropolitan status, size, and adjacency to metro and micro areas, published in the 1993, 2003, 2013, and 2024 vintages as a FIPS lookup table.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.usda.urban_influence_codes(provider='usda')
# Get the 2024 Urban Influence Codes for Alabama counties.
obb.usda.urban_influence_codes(vintage='2024', state='AL', provider='usda')
# Get the 2003 codes with population density for Wyoming.
obb.usda.urban_influence_codes(vintage='2003', state='WY', provider='usda')
# Get the 1993 vintage codes for the whole United States.
obb.usda.urban_influence_codes(vintage='1993', provider='usda')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**vintage**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* 2024<br/>
<details>
<summary mdxType="summary">Description</summary>

Classification vintage to retrieve; each vintage is a separate published file. The 2024 revision uses a nine-code scheme, 2013 and 2003 use a twelve-code scheme, and 1993 uses a different nine-code scheme. Valid vintages are:<br/>
    2024, 2013, 2003, 1993<br/>
</details>

**state**: `str | None`<br/>
State to retrieve, as a two-letter code, scoping the rows to one state's counties. If None, every county in the vintage is returned. The published state set varies by vintage: the 2024 revision adds the American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and U.S. Virgin Islands territories, 2013 and 2003 add Puerto Rico, and 1993 covers the states and the District of Columbia only.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---

<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='usda' label='usda'>

**fips**: `str`<br/>
Five-digit county FIPS code, zero-padded.

**state**: `str`<br/>
Two-letter state or territory postal code of the county.

**county_name**: `str`<br/>
County or municipio name, as published.

**urban_influence_code**: `str | None`<br/>
Urban Influence Code of the county, as an ordinal string: one to nine for the 2024 and 1993 vintages, one to twelve for the 2013 and 2003 vintages.

**description**: `str | None`<br/>
Published description of the county's Urban Influence Code.

**population**: `float | int | None`<br/>
Published population count of the county; the 2020 census for the 2024 vintage, the 2010 census for 2013, and the 2000 census for the 2003 and 1993 vintages.

**population_density**: `float | None`<br/>
Published population density in persons per square mile, from the 2000 census. Populated only for the 2003 and 1993 vintages; the 2024 and 2013 files carry no density.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---
title: "award"
description: "Drill into a federal award from USAspending - its summary, transactions, subawards, federal accounts, funding, or the orders placed against a vehicle"
keywords:
- ustreasury
- award
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="ustreasury/award - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Drill into a federal award from USAspending - its summary, transactions, subawards, federal accounts, funding, or the orders placed against a vehicle.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the summary of an award by its usaspending.gov id.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', provider='us_treasury')
# Drill into the subawards of an award.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', section='subawards', provider='us_treasury')
# Get the orders placed against an indefinite delivery vehicle.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', section='idv_children', provider='us_treasury')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='us_treasury' label='us_treasury'>

**award_id**: `str`<br/>
The award identifier, as it appears in a usaspending.gov/award/&lt;id> URL, e.g. 'CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549'. The internal integer award id is also accepted.

**section**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* detail<br/>
The section of the award to return. 'detail' returns the award summary as a single row. 'idv_children' is only valid for IDV awards.

**idv_children_type**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* child_awards<br/>
For section='idv_children', the relation to return. 'child_awards' are the orders placed against the vehicle, 'child_idvs' are nested vehicles, and the two are disjoint sets.

**page**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
The page of results to return.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 100<br/>
The number of data entries to return. Capped by the source at 5000 for 'transactions' and 100 for every other paginated section. Ignored when section='detail'.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `UsSpendingAward`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.

---
## Data

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='us_treasury' label='us_treasury'>

**action_date**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the transaction or subaward action was taken.

**award_id**: `str`<br/>
Identifier of the award the row belongs to.

**child_award_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Identifier of the child award, for section='idv_children'. Supply it back as award_id to drill into the child.

**transaction_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Natural identifier of the transaction, for section='transactions'.

**modification_number**: `str | None`<br/>
Modification number of the transaction.

**subaward_id**: `int | None`<br/>
Internal identifier of the subaward, for section='subawards'.

**subaward_number**: `str | None`<br/>
Subaward number as reported by the prime recipient. Not unique - it can repeat across rows.

**piid**: `str | None`<br/>
Procurement Instrument Identifier, for contracts and IDVs.

**fain**: `str | None`<br/>
Federal Award Identification Number, for assistance awards.

**uri**: `str | None`<br/>
Unique Record Identifier, for assistance awards.

**parent_award_id**: `str | None`<br/>
Identifier of the parent IDV, when the award has one.

**parent_piid**: `str | None`<br/>
PIID of the parent IDV, when the award has one.

**internal_id**: `int | None`<br/>
Internal surrogate identifier of the row's award.

**record_type**: `int | None`<br/>
Assistance record type - 1 is aggregate, 2 and 3 are non-aggregate.

**category**: `str | None`<br/>
Award category - contract, idv, grant, loans, direct payment, other, or insurance.

**award_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Award type code, e.g. 'IDV_E' or '02'.

**award_type_description**: `str | None`<br/>
Human readable award type, e.g. 'BPA'.

**action_type**: `str | None`<br/>
Action type code of the transaction, e.g. 'A' or 'G'.

**action_type_description**: `str | None`<br/>
Human readable action type of the transaction.

**amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Face value of the subaward, in dollars, for section='subawards'.

**federal_action_obligation**: `float | None`<br/>
Obligation recorded by the transaction, in dollars. This is a per-modification delta and is negative for de-obligations.

**obligated_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount obligated to the child award, in dollars, for section='idv_children'.

**total_obligation**: `float | None`<br/>
Total amount obligated to the award, in dollars. Reported as 0 for an IDV, whose obligations sit on its children.

**base_and_all_options**: `float | None`<br/>
Award ceiling if all options are exercised, in dollars. Null for assistance awards.

**base_exercised_options**: `float | None`<br/>
Award value including exercised options, in dollars.

**total_outlay**: `float | None`<br/>
Total amount outlayed against the award, in dollars.

**total_account_obligation**: `float | None`<br/>
Total obligation reported in the award's federal account records, in dollars.

**total_account_outlay**: `float | None`<br/>
Total outlay reported in the award's federal account records, in dollars.

**subaward_count**: `int | None`<br/>
Number of subawards reported under the award.

**total_subaward_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Total value of subawards reported under the award, in dollars. Null when there are no subawards.

**total_subsidy_cost**: `float | None`<br/>
Total subsidy cost, in dollars. Loans only.

**total_loan_value**: `float | None`<br/>
Total face value of the loan, in dollars. Loans only.

**face_value_loan_guarantee**: `float | None`<br/>

**original_loan_subsidy_cost**: `float | None`<br/>
Original subsidy cost of the loan, in dollars. Loans only.

**non_federal_funding**: `float | None`<br/>
Non-federal funding, in dollars. Grants only.

**total_funding**: `float | None`<br/>
Total federal and non-federal funding, in dollars. Grants only.

**transaction_obligated_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount obligated by the funding record, in dollars. Mutually exclusive with gross_outlay_amount on a funding row.

**gross_outlay_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount outlayed by the funding record, in dollars. Negative values are downward adjustments. Mutually exclusive with transaction_obligated_amount on a funding row.

**total_transaction_obligated_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Amount obligated from the federal account, in dollars, for section='federal_accounts'. Coalesced to 0 by the source when no funding records exist.

**date_signed**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the award was signed.

**period_start**: `date | None`<br/>
Start date of the period of performance.

**period_end**: `date | None`<br/>
Current end date of the period of performance.

**period_potential_end**: `date | None`<br/>
Potential end date of the period of performance, if all options are exercised.

**last_date_to_order**: `date | None`<br/>
Last date an order may be placed against the vehicle, for section='idv_children'.

**last_modified**: `date | None`<br/>
Date the award record was last modified.

**recipient_name**: `str | None`<br/>
Name of the recipient. For section='subawards' this is the subrecipient, otherwise the prime recipient.

**recipient_uei**: `str | None`<br/>
Unique Entity Identifier of the recipient.

**parent_recipient_name**: `str | None`<br/>

Congressional district of the recipient.

Country where the award is performed.

Congressional district where the award is performed.

Name of the funding sub-tier agency.

Name of the funding office.

Assistance Listing (CFDA) number. Assistance awards only.

Assistance Listing (CFDA) title. Assistance awards only.

---
title: "award_search"
description: "Search federal contract and assistance awards from USAspending by agency, recipient, keyword, amount, and date, then drill into any award by its id"
keywords:
- ustreasury
- award_search
---

import HeadTitle from '@site/src/components/General/HeadTitle.tsx';

<HeadTitle title="ustreasury/award_search - Reference | OpenBB Docs" />

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD012 MD031 MD033 -->

import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';

Search federal contract and assistance awards from USAspending by agency, recipient, keyword, amount, and date, then drill into any award by its id.

Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Search the largest recent defense contracts.
obb.ustreasury.award_search(award_group='contracts', agency='Department of Defense', provider='us_treasury')
# Find recent grants to a recipient by keyword.
obb.ustreasury.award_search(award_group='grants', recipient='California', keywords='medicaid', provider='us_treasury')
```

## Parameters

<Tabs>
<TabItem value='standard' label='standard'>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value='us_treasury' label='us_treasury'>

**award_group**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* contracts<br/>
Award family to search: 'contracts', 'idvs' (indefinite delivery vehicles), 'grants', 'direct_payments', 'loans', or 'other_assistance'. Sets the underlying award-type codes.

**start_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters on the award action period. When None, defaults to the trailing 365 days rather than all of history.

**end_date**: `date | None | str`<br/>
End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Filters on the award action period.

**keywords**: `str | None`<br/>
Free-text search over award descriptions and identifiers. Accepts a comma-separated list; awards matching any term are kept.

**recipient**: `str | None`<br/>
Recipient name search text, e.g. 'Boeing'.

**agency**: `str | None`<br/>
Awarding top-tier agency name, exactly as published, e.g. 'Department of Defense'.

**min_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Minimum award amount, in dollars.

**max_amount**: `float | None`<br/>
Maximum award amount, in dollars.

**award_number**: `str | None`<br/>
Award number, its PIID, FAIN, or URI, e.g. 'SPE30018FLGFZ'. Accepts a comma-separated list. Matching is fuzzy; wrap a value in double quotes for an exact match, which is needed for identifiers containing spaces.

**description**: `str | None`<br/>
Search text matched against the award description only, unlike 'keywords', which also searches identifiers.

**naics**: `str | None`<br/>
North American Industry Classification System code, e.g. '541519'. Accepts a comma-separated list. Validated against the source's reference list.

**psc**: `str | None`<br/>
Product or Service Code, e.g. 'R425'. Accepts a comma-separated list. Validated against the source's reference list.

**assistance_listing**: `str | None`<br/>
Assistance Listing (CFDA) program number, e.g. '10.331'. Accepts a comma-separated list. Validated against the source's reference list. Assistance awards only.

**defc**: `str | None`<br/>
Disaster Emergency Fund Code, e.g. 'L' for COVID-19 or 'Z' for infrastructure. Accepts a comma-separated list.

**contract_pricing**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of contract pricing, by code, e.g. 'J' for Firm Fixed Price. Accepts a comma-separated list. Contracts and IDVs only.

**set_aside**: `str | None`<br/>
Type of set aside, by code, e.g. 'SBA' for Small Business Set Aside - Total. Accepts a comma-separated list. Contracts and IDVs only.

**extent_competed**: `str | None`<br/>
Extent competed, by code, e.g. 'A' for Full and Open Competition. Accepts a comma-separated list. Contracts and IDVs only.

**sort**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* Award Amount<br/>
Field to sort by.

**order**: `str | None`<br/>
*Default:* desc<br/>
Sort order.

**page**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 1<br/>
The page of results to return.

**limit**: `int | None`<br/>
*Default:* 100<br/>
The number of data entries to return. Capped by the source at 100.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Returns

**results**: `UsSpendingAwardSearch`

Serializable results.

**provider**: `str | None`

Provider name.

**warnings**: `Optional[list[Warning_]]`

List of warnings.

**chart**: `Optional[Chart]`

Chart object.

**extra**: `dict[str, Any]`

Extra info.
